passage.text: In 1876, the town council of Millbrook introduced a curfew requiring everyone under eighteen to be indoors by 9 p.m. The stated purpose was to reduce vandalism after a string of broken shop windows. Town marshal Eva Ortega was tasked with enforcing the rule, though she requested extra lanterns to patrol the streets safely.

stem: According to the passage, what was the stated purpose of Millbrook's curfew?

choices.label: D
choices.text: To help the town marshal obtain more lanterns

explanation: The passage explicitly states that the curfew's stated purpose was 'to reduce vandalism after a string of broken shop windows.' The other choices introduce motives not mentioned in the text.

passage.text: Slow fashion is often misunderstood as simply buying fewer clothes. In practice, the movement emphasizes a longer view: choosing well-made garments, repairing them when possible, and supporting producers who use sustainable materials. Advocates argue that this approach lessens waste and pressures companies to improve labor conditions. The goal, they say, is not anti-consumption but more thoughtful consumption.

stem: Which choice best summarizes the central idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The slow fashion movement rejects all clothing purchases.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Slow fashion is mainly about extending the life of clothing through repairs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Slow fashion encourages thoughtful clothing choices to reduce waste and improve industry practices.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most clothing companies already follow slow fashion principles.

explanation: The passage defines slow fashion as thoughtful consumption: choosing well-made garments, repairing them, and supporting sustainable producers to lessen waste and improve labor conditions. Choice C captures this central idea; A is an extreme misreading, B is only part of the idea, and D is unsupported.

passage.text: Researchers studying the Bengal monitor lizard have discovered that the animal can tolerate high body temperatures that would be lethal to most reptiles. The lizard's blood contains a special protein that keeps enzymes from breaking down at extreme heat. This protein, they note, appears only in adults, which may explain why young monitors seek shade more often than adults do.

stem: According to the passage, what allows Bengal monitor lizards to tolerate high body temperatures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Their habit of seeking shade during the hottest hours

choices.label: B
choices.text: A body temperature lower than that of most reptiles

choices.label: C
choices.text: The absence of enzymes in their bloodstream

choices.label: D
choices.text: A protein in their blood that protects enzymes

explanation: The passage states that the lizard's blood contains a special protein that keeps enzymes from breaking down at extreme heat. That protein is what allows the lizards to tolerate high body temperatures, so D is correct.

passage.text: Leafcutter ants are often shown in nature documentaries carrying pieces of leaves, which makes them appear to be plant eaters. In fact, the ants do not eat the leaves. They bring them underground to cultivate a fungus that serves as the colony's food. The ants provide the fungus with fresh plant material, and the fungus breaks down substances in the leaves that the ants cannot digest.

stem: Which choice best states the central idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Leafcutter ants eat the leaves they carry into their nests.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Leafcutter ants use leaves to cultivate a fungus that the colony eats.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Leafcutter ants collect leaves mainly to build their underground nests.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Leafcutter ants are the only animals that can digest fungus.

explanation: The passage corrects the misconception that leafcutter ants eat leaves; instead, they use leaves to cultivate a fungus that serves as the colony's food. Choice B states that central idea accurately. The other choices are contradicted or unsupported.

passage.text: Although rooftop gardens are often praised for lowering urban temperatures and filtering storm water, their most lasting effect may be on the people who tend them. Gardeners report stronger neighborhood ties, greater willingness to share tools and produce, and reduced stress after a day spent working with soil. In cities where green space is scarce, these social and emotional gains can be as valuable as the vegetables themselves.

stem: The central idea of the passage is primarily that rooftop gardens...

choices.label: A
choices.text: are an efficient way to reduce storm water in crowded cities

choices.label: B
choices.text: cannot succeed unless cities provide gardeners with ongoing funding

choices.label: C
choices.text: offer social and emotional benefits that may matter as much as their environmental effects

choices.label: D
choices.text: are less valuable than ordinary parks because they produce vegetables

explanation: The passage opens by acknowledging environmental benefits but then argues that the most lasting effect is on people: stronger neighborhood ties, sharing, and reduced stress. Thus the central idea is that rooftop gardens offer social and emotional benefits comparable to their environmental ones.

passage.text: The male superb lyrebird of Australia is a remarkable vocal mimic. In addition to imitating other bird species, it can reproduce sounds from its environment, including camera shutters, car alarms, and chainsaws. Scientists believe this ability helps the bird attract mates by demonstrating age and experience, because a more varied repertoire requires years of practice and exposure to many sounds.

stem: According to the passage, why do scientists think a male lyrebird benefits from a varied repertoire?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The extra sounds frighten away predators that might raid its nest.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complex songs are easier for the bird to produce than simple songs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Imitating artificial sounds helps the bird find food in urban areas.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A varied repertoire signals age and experience to potential mates.

explanation: The passage explicitly states that scientists believe the lyrebird's varied vocal repertoire helps it attract mates by demonstrating age and experience, since a wider range of sounds requires years of practice and exposure.

passage.text: Tree-planting campaigns are a popular response to climate change, and forests do absorb large amounts of carbon dioxide. Yet the protection they offer is fragile. Droughts, insect outbreaks, and wildfires can kill trees and release stored carbon back into the atmosphere within a few years. For this reason, many climate scientists argue that planting new trees must be paired with reducing fossil-fuel emissions and better management of existing forests.

stem: The central idea of the passage is that...

choices.label: A
choices.text: Planting trees is the most effective way to remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reducing fossil-fuel emissions and managing existing forests should accompany new tree planting.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Wildfires are the single greatest cause of carbon emissions worldwide.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Forests cannot store carbon for more than a few years.

explanation: The passage says tree planting alone is not enough because forests can release stored carbon through droughts, insects, and fires. Scientists therefore argue that planting must be paired with cutting emissions and managing existing forests, which is the central idea.

passage.text: In 1907, Pablo Picasso visited the ethnographic museum in Paris and studied African masks and sculptures. Their bold geometric forms and distorted proportions stayed with him as he completed Les Demoiselles d'Avignon. The painting's fractured faces and sharp angles show this influence and are often cited as early steps toward Cubism. Georges Braque saw the painting and soon adopted a similar angular language in his own work.

stem: According to the passage, the African sculptures Picasso studied were significant because they...

choices.label: A
choices.text: influenced the fragmented, angular style of Les Demoiselles d'Avignon

choices.label: B
choices.text: were the only artworks that ever influenced Picasso's painting

choices.label: C
choices.text: persuaded Picasso to give up oil painting and work in sculpture

choices.label: D
choices.text: had been commissioned by the Paris museum from African artists

explanation: The passage states that the geometric forms and distorted proportions of the African sculptures stayed with Picasso and are visible in the fractured faces and sharp angles of Les Demoiselles d'Avignon.

passage.text: In 1986, protesters in Rome camped near the site where a McDonald's was opening, holding bowls of pasta and handing out recipe cards. Their action grew into the Slow Food movement, now active in more than 160 countries. Followers advocate for local ingredients, traditional cooking methods, and the social pleasure of sharing meals. What began as a stand against fast food has evolved into a broader effort to make food production more sustainable and communities more connected.

stem: The central idea of the passage is that the Slow Food movement...

choices.label: A
choices.text: was created to convince people to cook pasta rather than eat at restaurants

choices.label: B
choices.text: began as a protest but has remained limited to Italy

choices.label: C
choices.text: promotes local, traditional, and community-centered food practices

choices.label: D
choices.text: has concentrated mainly on preventing fast-food restaurants from opening

explanation: The passage describes how the movement grew from a protest into a broad effort for sustainable food and connected communities, centered on local ingredients, traditional cooking, and sharing meals.

passage.text: Community gardens in midsize cities do more than beautify vacant lots. In a three-year study of fourteen gardens, neighborhoods with active gardens reported a 12 percent drop in petty crime, and property values within two blocks rose by an average of 6 percent. The gardens also became gathering places where older residents exchanged gardening tips and homemade preserves. The findings suggest that well-maintained community gardens can strengthen both the social fabric and the economic health of nearby neighborhoods.

stem: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Community gardens primarily benefit older residents by giving them a place to socialize.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Community gardens can improve the social and economic conditions of surrounding neighborhoods.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Community gardens reduce crime more consistently than they raise property values.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Community gardens are valuable mainly because they make use of otherwise vacant city lots.

explanation: The passage gives examples of social benefits (gathering places, exchanges) and economic benefits (reduced crime, higher property values), all of which support the idea that community gardens strengthen the social and economic conditions of nearby neighborhoods. A is too narrow, C makes an unsupported comparison, and D contradicts the opening claim.

passage.text: Solar-powered irrigation systems for dry farmlands can obtain water from an unexpected source. The system draws warm, humid air through buried ceramic pipes. As the air moves through the cooler ground, water vapor condenses on the pipe walls and drips into collection tanks. Because the process runs entirely on passive cooling, it uses no electricity and can supply five liters of water per square meter of pipe each day.

stem: According to the passage, how does the irrigation system produce water?

choices.label: A
choices.text: By pumping groundwater upward through ceramic pipes

choices.label: B
choices.text: By collecting rainwater in underground storage tanks

choices.label: C
choices.text: By condensing moisture from air drawn through pipes

choices.label: D
choices.text: By desalinating seawater with solar heat

explanation: The passage explicitly states that warm, humid air is drawn through buried pipes and that water vapor condenses on the pipe walls. Therefore, the system produces water by condensing moisture from air drawn through pipes.

passage.text: The Millport Free Library began in 1923 inside a converted railway depot. During its first decade, patrons borrowed mostly novels, but a survey in 1935 found rising demand for books on agriculture and mechanical repair. The librarian added a technical section, and within a year those books made up half of all circulation. The change reflected Millport's economy, which depended on small farms and machine shops.

stem: Which statement best summarizes the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The library's collection shifted to meet the practical needs of its community.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The survey in 1935 was the first survey ever conducted by a public library.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most people in Millport preferred novels to technical books.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The library became successful because it was located in a railway depot.

explanation: The passage traces how the library added books on agriculture and mechanical repair in response to demand, and it concludes that the change reflected the town's farm and machine-shop economy. A captures this central idea, while B overstates the survey, C is the opposite, and D is unrelated.

passage.text: Black-crowned night herons are unusual among herons because they hunt mainly after sunset. Their eyes have an exceptionally high density of rod cells, which makes them very sensitive to dim light. During the day the birds roost in dense trees, often in groups, and at twilight they move to shallow water. There they stalk small fish and insects, using sight rather than touch to catch prey.

stem: According to the passage, black-crowned night herons can hunt in dim light mainly because of their

choices.label: A
choices.text: habit of roosting together in dense trees

choices.label: B
choices.text: reliance on touch to detect prey

choices.label: C
choices.text: use of shallow water as a hunting ground

choices.label: D
choices.text: large number of rod cells in their eyes

explanation: The passage directly states that the herons' eyes have an exceptionally high density of rod cells, making them sensitive to dim light. The other choices mention behaviors or habitats but not the reason they can see in low light.

passage.text: Psychologists long believed that young children who could delay gratification tended to do better in school. In a recent study, 500 four-year-olds chose between one marshmallow now and two marshmallows later. Those who waited scored moderately higher on tests at age 12. But once family income was taken into account, the advantage vanished, suggesting that the earlier results were partly driven by resources and opportunities available to wealthier families.

stem: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Waiting for a second marshmallow is the most reliable predictor of success in school.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The link between self-control in childhood and later test scores may be influenced by family income.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Wealthier families are more likely to teach their children to delay gratification.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The study proved that family income has no effect on academic test scores.

explanation: The passage reports that the advantage disappeared after controlling for family income, which suggests the link may be partly explained by income-related factors. B matches this idea, while A is too strong, C is not stated, and D contradicts the passage.

passage.text: At Elm Park Community Garden, gardeners replaced most sprinklers with drip irrigation lines and began collecting rainwater in two large tanks. The changes cut the garden's overall water use by nearly forty percent while keeping vegetables healthy. Organizers say the new system cost more upfront but saves money over time. They hope other neighborhood gardens will adopt similar methods.

stem: Which choice best states the central idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A community garden reduced its water use and saved money over time by installing drip irrigation and collecting rainwater.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Drip irrigation lines are the most expensive watering method available to urban gardeners.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vegetables watered by drip irrigation are healthier than vegetables watered by sprinklers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Community gardens should not use sprinklers because they increase water bills.

explanation: The passage says the changes cut water use by nearly forty percent and save money over time, so A best captures the central idea.

passage.text: Researchers asked two groups of college students to listen to a recorded lecture: one group at normal speed and one at one and a half times normal speed. On a comprehension test, the faster group scored almost as well as the normal-speed group. However, when asked to recall details a week later, the faster group remembered significantly less. The researchers concluded that speeded audio may work for immediate understanding but not for lasting memory.

stem: Which choice best states the main conclusion of the researchers?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Listening to faster speech always produces lower scores on immediate comprehension tests.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Students who study with recorded lectures remember more than students who attend live lectures.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Speeded audio may be acceptable for immediate understanding but harms long-term recall.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The main benefit of speeded audio is that it improves memory of lecture details.

explanation: The passage states that the faster group scored almost as well on the immediate comprehension test but remembered significantly less later, matching C.

passage.text: To receive International Dark Sky Park designation, a site must demonstrate exceptional nighttime darkness and commit to reducing light pollution. Staff must offer public astronomy programs. In addition, the park must replace at least some outdated lighting with shielded fixtures that direct light downward. The certification is renewed every five years.

stem: According to the text, which of the following is required for a park to receive International Dark Sky Park designation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It must have no artificial light within ten miles.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It must offer public astronomy programs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It must replace all outdoor lighting with LED bulbs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It must apply for recertification every five years.

explanation: The passage explicitly states that staff must offer public astronomy programs, so B is correct.

passage.text: Patricia Bath, an ophthalmologist, invented the Laserphaco Probe in the 1980s to treat cataracts. The device used laser light to vaporize the cataract and a vacuum to remove the debris, reducing damage to surrounding tissue. Bath's invention helped restore sight for people who had been blind for years. She also worked to improve eye care in underserved communities.

stem: According to the text, what did Patricia Bath's Laserphaco Probe do during cataract treatment?

choices.label: B
choices.text: It used a small blade to cut the cataract.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It replaced the need for surgery.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It vaporized the cataract with laser light and removed the debris with a vacuum.

explanation: The passage says the device used laser light to vaporize the cataract and a vacuum to remove the debris, so D is correct.

passage.text: Some studies suggest that taking a short walk after studying can improve memory. In one experiment, participants who walked for ten minutes immediately after memorizing a list recalled more words than participants who sat quietly. Researchers think light physical activity may increase blood flow to the brain. They caution that intense exercise after learning may have the opposite effect.

stem: Which choice best describes the main finding of the experiment in the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sitting quietly after studying improves memory more than walking.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intense exercise after learning always improves memory.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A ten-minute walk after studying may improve recall of studied material.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Blood flow to the brain is unaffected by physical activity.

explanation: The experiment found that participants who walked for ten minutes after memorizing recalled more words, so C matches the main finding.

passage.text: Although rooftop gardens have received considerable attention as a way to cool cities, planting trees along streets may have a greater overall effect. Street trees provide shade that lowers pavement temperatures, and their root systems absorb heavy rainfall, reducing the burden on storm drains. However, maintaining street trees is costly; cities must prune branches, repair cracked sidewalks, and replace trees that die. Even so, many urban planners argue that the environmental benefits outweigh the expenses.

stem: Which statement best captures the central idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rooftop gardens are less effective than street trees in reducing pavement temperatures.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Although street trees have significant environmental benefits, they come with expenses that some planners still consider worthwhile.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Street trees lower pavement temperatures and absorb heavy rainfall.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Urban planners should replace rooftop gardens with street trees.

explanation: The passage describes both the environmental advantages of street trees and their maintenance costs, then concludes that many urban planners believe the benefits justify the expenses. Choice B captures this balance; the other choices are either supporting details or unsupported claims.

passage.text: The Great Pacific Garbage Patch is not a solid island of trash but a diffuse collection of debris spread over a vast area. It consists largely of microplastics, which are tiny fragments resulting from the breakdown of larger plastic items. Because these particles float at or near the surface, they are often mistaken for sea life by marine animals. While the patch is enormous, its low density means that a vessel can travel through it for days without seeing obvious trash.

stem: According to the passage, which statement accurately describes the Great Pacific Garbage Patch?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It appears as a dense island of plastic that ships can easily avoid.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is composed mainly of large plastic items that break down over time.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Its plastic is concentrated just below the waterline, making it hard to observe.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a vast but dispersed area containing many microplastics.

explanation: The passage explicitly states that the patch is a diffuse collection of debris, consists largely of microplastics, and is so low in density that ships can pass through without seeing obvious trash. Choice D matches these details.

passage.text: Citizen science projects enlist members of the public to collect data for researchers. For example, volunteers photograph plants and animals, count birds, or record water quality. The resulting data can be large, spanning many locations and seasons, which would be impossible for a small research team to gather alone. However, professional scientists must still verify the observations, because volunteers may make measurement errors or misidentify species. Thus, citizen science works best when experts design the protocols and check the results.

stem: What is the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Citizen science can gather large amounts of data, but expert oversight is needed to ensure that data are trustworthy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Volunteers are not capable of making accurate scientific observations.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Citizen science projects are useful mainly for photographing plants and animals.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Research teams are too small to collect data across many locations and seasons.

explanation: The passage presents both the value of citizen science and the need for professional verification, concluding that expert-designed protocols and checks are essential. Choice A captures this central idea.

passage.text: In parts of Asia, bamboo scaffolding remains common on construction sites despite the availability of steel and aluminum. Builders choose bamboo because it is strong, lightweight, and inexpensive. A bamboo pole can support surprisingly heavy loads, and the material bends under stress rather than snapping, giving workers warning before failure. Moreover, bamboo grows quickly, making it a renewable resource. Critics point out that bamboo scaffolding requires skilled workers to tie and inspect, but supporters say its safety record compares well with that of metal systems.

stem: Which statement best expresses the central idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bamboo scaffolding is safer than steel and aluminum scaffolding.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because bamboo grows quickly, it is a renewable building material.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bamboo scaffolding remains common because it is practical, although it demands specialized expertise.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most construction in Asia uses bamboo because metal scaffolding is too expensive.

explanation: The passage explains why builders choose bamboo—strength, low cost, light weight, renewability—and also notes the need for skilled workers to address its drawbacks. Choice C best summarizes both sides.

passage.text: Coral bleaching occurs when stressed corals expel the algae that live in their tissues, causing the corals to turn white. High water temperatures are the leading cause, but pollution and changes in salinity can also trigger bleaching. If conditions return to normal, corals can recover, but prolonged stress often kills them. Because coral reefs support roughly a quarter of marine species, large bleaching events can be catastrophic for ocean ecosystems.

stem: Which statement best identifies the central idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: High water temperatures are the only cause of coral bleaching.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Corals turn white because they expel algae from their tissues.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coral bleaching can be reversed if ocean temperatures drop quickly.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Warm-water stress causes coral bleaching, which can devastate ecosystems that depend on reefs.

explanation: The passage identifies heat stress as the leading cause of coral bleaching and explains the potential harm to coral reefs and the marine species that rely on them. Choice D captures this central idea.

passage.text: Local libraries have changed far beyond their traditional role as places to borrow books. Today many libraries offer internet access, job-search assistance, and free workshops on topics from financial literacy to coding. Librarians help patrons complete forms, prepare for citizenship tests, and connect with social services. In doing so, libraries have become essential hubs for community support, particularly for people who lack reliable access to technology or guidance.

stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Libraries now serve as essential hubs for community support by offering services beyond book lending.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Librarians are trained to help patrons prepare for citizenship tests.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Internet access is the most important service that libraries provide.

choices.label: D
choices.text: People without reliable technology should visit their local library.

explanation: The passage describes several new library services and concludes that libraries have become essential hubs for community support, so A captures the main idea.

passage.text: Desert tortoises spend most of their lives in underground burrows, which protect them from extreme heat and predators. They may dig several burrows and move among them throughout the year. During hot summers, they become less active, a state similar to hibernation called estivation. In winter, they sometimes emerge on warm days to drink rainwater collected in shallow pools.

stem: According to the passage, why do desert tortoises spend most of their lives in burrows?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To find food and drink rainwater

choices.label: B
choices.text: To protect themselves from extreme heat and predators

choices.label: C
choices.text: To avoid entering a state similar to hibernation

choices.label: D
choices.text: To dig multiple shelters throughout the year

explanation: The passage states that burrows "protect them from extreme heat and predators," directly answering why desert tortoises spend most of their lives in burrows.

passage.text: Many people assume that electric vehicles produce no pollution, but this view overlooks the electricity used to charge them. If that electricity comes from coal-burning power plants, the vehicle's overall emissions can be substantial. Nevertheless, when charged from renewable sources such as solar or wind, electric vehicles can be nearly emission-free. Their environmental benefit therefore depends heavily on how the electricity is generated.

stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Electric vehicles are not truly emission-free.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The environmental impact of electric vehicles depends on the source of the electricity used to charge them.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Solar and wind power should replace coal-burning plants.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Coal-burning power plants are more efficient than electric vehicles.

explanation: The passage contrasts emissions from coal-generated electricity with nearly emission-free renewable charging and concludes that the benefit depends on how the electricity is generated, matching B.

passage.text: Several factors determine whether a wildfire spreads quickly. Wind supplies oxygen and pushes flames forward, while dry vegetation acts as fuel. Humidity matters as well: when the air is moist, plants and soil retain water, making ignition less likely. Steep slopes also encourage rapid spread because fire heats the vegetation above it, drying and igniting it sooner.

stem: According to the passage, how does steep terrain affect a wildfire?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It lowers humidity, making the air drier.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It pushes flames forward in the same way wind does.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It causes fire to heat and ignite vegetation above it more quickly.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It supplies additional dry vegetation as fuel.

explanation: The passage says steep slopes "encourage rapid spread because fire heats the vegetation above it, drying and igniting it sooner."

passage.text: Citizen science projects rely on volunteers to collect data for researchers. In one nationwide project, volunteers photograph butterflies and submit their observations through an app. Scientists use these records to track migration patterns and population changes. Because the volunteers are not professional scientists, project coordinators provide clear identification guides and require photographs as evidence. This careful design keeps the data useful while involving thousands of people in research.

stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Citizen science projects can yield valuable data when volunteers receive guidance and provide evidence.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Butterfly migration patterns are best studied through photographs submitted by volunteers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: People without scientific training cannot collect data reliably.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Researchers should avoid relying on volunteers because of the risk of error.

explanation: The passage emphasizes that careful design—identification guides and photographic evidence—makes volunteer-collected data useful, matching A.

passage.text: Community gardens in Detroit have expanded from small vacant-lot vegetable plots into networks that supply fresh produce to local farmers' markets. Although supporters emphasize health benefits, the gardens' most lasting effect may be social: neighbors who coordinate planting schedules and share harvests report stronger relationships and greater willingness to collaborate on other neighborhood projects.

stem: Which choice best states the central idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The main significance of Detroit's community gardens may be their effect on social bonds among neighbors.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Supporters of Detroit's community gardens argue that fresh produce is more important than any other benefit.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Detroit's farmers' markets have become more popular as a result of nearby community gardens.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vacant lots in Detroit should be converted into community gardens to improve public health.

explanation: The passage says the gardens' most lasting effect may be social, with neighbors building stronger relationships and collaborating more. Thus the central idea is that their main significance may be social, not merely agricultural or health-related.

passage.text: A simple solar cooker uses a curved reflective panel to concentrate sunlight onto a dark cooking pot. The panel focuses the light, and the dark surface absorbs heat, while a clear cover traps rising warm air. Cooks must adjust the cooker about every half hour to follow the movement of the sun.

stem: According to the passage, what is the role of the clear cover in a solar cooker?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It concentrates sunlight onto the pot.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It absorbs heat from the dark surface.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It prevents the pot from overheating.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It keeps heated air from escaping.

explanation: The passage explicitly states that a clear cover traps rising warm air, so its role is to keep heated air from escaping.

passage.text: For decades, volunteers have counted birds in their backyards for the North American Breeding Bird Survey. These observations are sometimes dismissed as less reliable than professional surveys, but the immense geographic coverage makes them valuable. Data collected by volunteers have documented population declines and range shifts that professional teams could not have tracked at the same scale.

stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Professional surveys of bird populations are more reliable than volunteer counts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Volunteer bird counts are primarily a form of recreation rather than of science.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Volunteer-collected bird data are highly valuable because they cover a very large area.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bird populations are declining because of habitat and climate changes.

explanation: The passage contrasts the perceived lower reliability of volunteer data with the advantage of immense geographic coverage, concluding that this coverage makes the data valuable. The main idea is that volunteer-collected bird data are valuable because they cover a large area.

passage.text: Natural vanilla flavor comes from vanilla beans, which are cured and dried before use. The compound vanillin is responsible for the characteristic taste and smell. Chemists can synthesize vanillin from lignin, a substance found in wood, and most commercial vanilla flavoring is synthetic. Because synthetic vanillin contains the same molecule as natural vanillin, the two forms are often hard to distinguish.

stem: According to the passage, why is it often difficult to distinguish natural vanilla flavoring from synthetic vanilla flavoring?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both forms are made from vanilla beans.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both contain the same flavor molecule.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both are produced through the same chemical process.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Both are dried and cured before they are used.

explanation: The passage says synthetic vanillin contains the same molecule as natural vanillin, which makes the two forms hard to distinguish. Therefore the correct answer is that both contain the same flavor molecule.

passage.text: Efforts to preserve endangered languages often focus on creating written records, but some linguists argue that the most useful tools are digital dictionaries and mobile apps. These resources can be updated in real time, include audio pronunciation, and reach speakers in remote areas. As a result, communities are more likely to use them than printed grammars. The value of a language tool, according to these linguists, depends less on academic completeness than on how readily people incorporate it into daily life.

stem: Which choice best states the central idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: For some linguists, digital language tools may best preserve endangered languages because they are actually used by communities.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Printed grammars are the only reliable way to record an endangered language.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Endangered languages are best preserved through written records rather than mobile apps.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Linguists disagree about whether endangered languages should be preserved at all.

explanation: The passage presents linguists who argue that digital dictionaries and apps are the most useful tools because communities are more likely to use them and incorporate them into daily life. Thus the central idea is that digital tools may best preserve endangered languages through actual community use.

passage.text: Volunteers started the Hillcrest Community Garden in an empty lot with the goal of growing fresh vegetables for the neighborhood food pantry. Within two years, the garden succeeded in that goal, but gardeners say the more lasting effect is harder to measure. Neighbors who once passed one another without speaking now trade seedlings, borrow tools, and meet for weekend workdays. A member observed, "We came for the tomatoes, but we stayed for each other."

stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Hillcrest Community Garden has mostly been unsuccessful at providing vegetables to the food pantry.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The same neighbors who now trade garden tools once ignored one another completely.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The community garden’s most significant impact has been bringing neighbors together.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The garden’s volunteers prefer socializing to gardening.

explanation: The passage says the garden achieved its original food-pantry goal, but the "more lasting effect" is the new connection among neighbors. Answer C states this central idea; the other options are details, unsupported claims, or distortions.

passage.text: Researchers studying urban trees monitored air temperature and humidity in four city parks over one summer. They found that areas with dense tree cover were consistently cooler than open pavement, sometimes by more than 5°C. The trees also released moisture through their leaves, which increased humidity and made the air feel less dry. The study concluded that preserving mature trees is one of the cheapest ways for cities to reduce summer heat.

stem: Which choice best states the central idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mature trees help cool cities and make summer air less dry.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Four city parks have more tree cover than any other part of the city.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Open pavement becomes hotter than tree-covered ground because it absorbs moisture.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Urban trees are most valuable for the fruit and shade they provide to residents.

explanation: The passage focuses on how trees lower temperature and add moisture, concluding that preserving mature trees is a cheap way to reduce summer heat. Choice A matches this central idea; the other choices are unsupported or address details only.

passage.text: In the early twentieth century, DuPont scientists were trying to create a synthetic substitute for natural rubber because supplies of rubber were expensive and unreliable. In 1930, one attempt produced a polymer that was sticky and flexible, but it also resisted oil, sunlight, and heat far better than natural rubber. The company named this material neoprene. Today it appears in products such as wetsuits, laptop sleeves, and automotive hoses.

stem: According to the text, what was the original purpose of the research that led to neoprene?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To make wetsuits more resistant to saltwater

choices.label: B
choices.text: To find a product that could replace oil and sunlight

choices.label: C
choices.text: To improve the flexibility of natural rubber

choices.label: D
choices.text: To produce a synthetic alternative to natural rubber

explanation: The passage explicitly states that scientists were "trying to create a synthetic substitute for natural rubber." Therefore, the original purpose was to produce a synthetic alternative, making D correct.

passage.text: Desert tortoises cannot tolerate extreme body temperatures for long periods. To survive the scorching summers and chilly winters of the Mojave Desert, they dig deep burrows and remain inside for as much as 95 percent of their lives. The burrows keep temperatures stable and protect the tortoises from predators. After winter rains, they emerge briefly to drink and eat annual wildflowers, then return underground.

stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Desert tortoises use burrows mainly to hide from predators.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Desert tortoises spend most of their lives in burrows to cope with harsh desert conditions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Desert tortoises remain in their burrows for exactly 95 percent of each year.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Desert tortoises spend most of their lives above ground searching for food.

explanation: The passage explains that desert tortoises avoid extreme temperatures by staying in burrows most of their lives. Choice B captures this main idea; the other choices are either details taken out of context, imprecise, or contradicted by the passage.

passage.text: Data centers are packed with servers that generate so much heat that large cooling systems are needed to keep them from failing. In a warm climate, cooling can account for roughly 40 percent of a facility's electricity bill. Several companies have therefore built data centers near the Arctic Circle. The cold outside air can be used directly for cooling, lowering energy costs and reducing the carbon footprint of the facilities.

stem: Which choice best states the central idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Building data centers in cold regions can reduce the energy needed for cooling.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Data centers generate too much heat for the Arctic Circle.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cooling accounts for about 40 percent of a data center's total electricity bill.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Companies choose Arctic sites mainly to lower their carbon footprints.

explanation: The passage explains that cooling is a major cost in warm climates, so companies build data centers in cold regions where outside air can cool servers cheaply. Choice A states this central idea; choice C is a supporting detail, while B and D are unsupported.

passage.text: Community gardens in cities often do more than provide fresh produce. Researchers have found that these plots can lower neighborhood temperatures, absorb storm water, and offer green spaces that reduce stress. Because they are managed by residents, they also strengthen social ties and encourage cooperation among diverse groups. While food production is a clear benefit, many city planners now view community gardens as essential pieces of urban infrastructure that improve public health and community resilience.

stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Community gardens are mainly valuable for the fresh vegetables they supply to city residents.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Community gardens serve multiple important urban functions beyond growing food.

choices.label: C
choices.text: City planners are skeptical about the long-term benefits of community gardens.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Researchers have proved that community gardens reduce stress more effectively than other green spaces do.

explanation: The text lists several benefits of community gardens—temperature control, storm-water absorption, stress reduction, and social cohesion—and concludes that planners see them as essential urban infrastructure. Choice B captures this broader main idea. A is too narrow, C contradicts the text, and D overstates an example.

passage.text: Sea otters play a key role in kelp forest ecosystems. By eating sea urchins, they prevent urchins from overgrazing kelp, which provides habitat for fish and other marine life. In areas where sea otters have recovered, kelp cover has increased significantly. However, the otters' voracious appetites sometimes bring them into conflict with shellfish fisheries, since otters also eat crabs and clams. Scientists therefore study otter populations carefully, weighing ecological benefits against economic costs.

stem: According to the text, what is one reason scientists carefully study sea otter populations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To determine whether the ecological benefits of otters outweigh their effects on shellfish fisheries.

choices.label: B
choices.text: To develop ways to increase the number of sea urchins in kelp forests.

choices.label: C
choices.text: To confirm that sea otters are the only animals that eat sea urchins.

choices.label: D
choices.text: To measure how much kelp sea otters consume directly.

explanation: The final sentence states that scientists study otter populations carefully, weighing ecological benefits against economic costs. Choice A restates this reason. B is contradicted because sea urchins overgraze kelp, C makes an unsupported absolute claim, and D is wrong because the text says otters eat sea urchins, crabs, and clams, not kelp.

passage.text: Remote work has changed how companies measure productivity. Many managers once equated productivity with hours spent at a desk, but remote teams are often evaluated by completed projects and measurable outcomes. Supporters argue this shift benefits workers, who gain flexibility, and employers, who can hire talent from anywhere. Critics caution, however, that constant connectivity can blur the boundary between work and home life, and some employees feel isolated. Overall, the move to remote work has prompted a fundamental rethink of what workplace productivity means.

stem: Which choice best expresses the main idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Remote work benefits employees more than it benefits employers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remote work poses serious risks to employees' mental and physical health.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Remote work has led companies to define productivity differently.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Remote work is most successful when workers are evaluated by hours completed.

explanation: The passage opens with the claim that remote work has changed how companies measure productivity and closes by calling it a fundamental rethink of what productivity means. Choice C captures that main idea. A and B present one-sided views, and D contradicts the text.

passage.text: Dictionary entries include usage labels that tell readers how a word functions in current English. The label 'nonstandard' indicates that a word or sense is used widely but is not considered acceptable in formal writing. 'Slang' marks informal vocabulary often associated with a particular group, and 'archaic' describes words that were common in the past but are now rare. These labels are not meant to ban words; rather, they help writers choose language appropriate for a given situation.

stem: According to the text, what does the label 'archaic' indicate about a word?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is widely used but not considered acceptable in formal writing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It was common in earlier periods but is now rarely used.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is informal vocabulary associated with a particular group.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It should not be used in any spoken or written context.

explanation: The text explicitly states that 'archaic' describes words that were common in the past but are now rare, so B is correct. A describes 'nonstandard,' C describes 'slang,' and D contradicts the statement that labels are not meant to ban words.

passage.text: Migratory beekeeping is a largely invisible part of industrial agriculture. Each year, beekeepers load thousands of hives onto trucks and travel across the country to pollinate crops that bloom at different times, from California almonds to Maine blueberries. This practice supports many staple foods, but it also places stress on bees, which face diseases, pesticides, and limited natural forage. For growers, the transportation of hives has become as routine as irrigation, yet it depends on a fragile insect population.

stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Migratory beekeeping is essential to agriculture but places serious strain on bees.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Almond growers benefit more from migratory beekeeping than any other farmers do.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bees face more threats from transportation than from pesticides.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Crop pollination would be impossible without migratory beekeeping.

explanation: The passage explains both that migratory beekeeping supports many staple foods and that it stresses bees. Choice A correctly expresses this central idea. B is an unsupported comparison, C introduces a comparison not made in the text, and D is too absolute.

passage.text: Some cities now allow residents to keep beehives on rooftops and balconies. Supporters say urban beekeeping helps pollinate parks and gardens, while opponents worry about the safety of residents with allergies. Information gathered from community programs shows that most urban hives remain healthy and produce honey. The number of registered urban hives has tripled in the past five years.

stem: Which choice best states the central idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Urban beekeeping is opposed by many residents because of allergy risks.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rooftop and balcony beehives produce more honey than rural hives do.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Urban beekeeping has become more common and offers benefits even though some concerns remain.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cities that allow beekeeping should first survey residents who have allergies.

explanation: The passage notes both a benefit (pollination and healthy hives) and a concern (allergic residents) while reporting that the number of registered hives has tripled. This supports the central idea that urban beekeeping is becoming more common and has benefits despite concerns.

passage.text: Fireflies produce light through a chemical reaction in their abdomens. This ability, called bioluminescence, serves several purposes. Males flash distinctive patterns to attract females of their species. Some species also flash to warn predators that they taste unpleasant. Even larvae can emit light, perhaps to signal that they are dangerous to eat.

stem: According to the text, one function of firefly flashing is to

choices.label: B
choices.text: begin the chemical reaction that produces light.

choices.label: C
choices.text: frighten smaller insects away from feeding areas.

choices.label: D
choices.text: prevent larvae from wandering too far from their nests.

explanation: The text explicitly states that males flash distinctive patterns to attract females of their species. The other choices reverse the cause of light production or introduce unsupported claims.

passage.text: Polymetallic nodules on the ocean floor contain metals used in batteries, but large-scale mining could damage fragile deep-sea ecosystems that scientists still do not fully understand. Mining companies argue that the metals are essential for renewable energy technology. Conservation researchers respond that improved recycling could meet much of the demand. As a result, governments are divided over whether to allow commercial mining.

stem: Which choice best states the central idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deep-sea mining would completely eliminate the need for recycling.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The value of deep-sea minerals is in conflict with concern for fragile ocean ecosystems.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Governments should settle the mining debate by studying land-based metal deposits.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Batteries used in renewable energy are only produced from ocean-floor metals.

explanation: The passage presents two competing perspectives: minerals from the ocean floor are valuable for technology, but mining could harm little-understood deep-sea ecosystems. The central idea is therefore the conflict between economic value and ecological risk.

passage.text: Bamboo is often mistaken for a tree, but technically it is a grass. Some species can grow more than thirty meters tall, yet all bamboo stems are hollow and arise from underground roots called rhizomes. Builders use bamboo for scaffolding and flooring, while textile makers weave its fibers into fabric. Its young shoots are also a common food.

stem: According to the text, bamboo is best described as a

choices.label: A
choices.text: tree that can grow more than thirty meters tall.

choices.label: B
choices.text: material used by builders to create fabric.

choices.label: C
choices.text: kind of grass with hollow stems.

explanation: The passage explicitly says bamboo is technically a grass and that all bamboo stems are hollow. The other options combine details incorrectly or contradict the text.

passage.text: Strong winds lift billions of tons of desert dust into the atmosphere each year. This dust travels across oceans, carrying phosphorus and iron that fertilize plants in distant forests. However, human activities such as overgrazing can increase the amount of dust in the air, which may reduce rainfall and erode fertile soil. The movement of dust thus has both positive and negative effects.

stem: Which choice best states the central idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Plants in distant forests depend on desert dust for essential minerals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Desert dust is caused primarily by overgrazing and other human actions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The positive effects of desert dust are canceled out by its negative effects.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dust carried from deserts can have beneficial consequences but can also harm the environment.

explanation: The passage describes how desert dust fertilizes distant plants but also explains that increased dust from human activities can reduce rainfall and erode soil. This supports the central idea that desert dust has both benefits and harms.

passage.text: Although community gardens in cities are often described mainly as sources of fresh produce, their effects extend well beyond food. Researchers have found that these gardens reduce neighborhood heat, create habitat for pollinators, and give residents a place to exercise and socialize. Many participants say the sense of shared purpose, not the harvest, is what keeps them coming back. City planners increasingly treat such gardens as public-health infrastructure rather than as mere hobby spaces.

stem: Which statement best captures the central idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Community gardens provide a range of social, environmental, and health-related benefits.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Community gardens are most valuable for increasing nearby property values.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Urban residents prefer buying produce at farmers' markets over growing it themselves.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Community gardens should be replaced by public parks in crowded cities.

explanation: The passage lists several non-food benefits of community gardens—reducing heat, supporting pollinators, encouraging exercise and socializing, and promoting public health—so the best central idea is that they provide multiple social, environmental, and health-related benefits.

passage.text: The modern bicycle emerged from several nineteenth-century experiments, but it was not until the 1880s that the 'safety bicycle' became widely popular. Its two equal-sized wheels and chain drive made it much less likely to tip forward than earlier penny-farthings. Even more important, the new design allowed riders to keep both feet near the ground, which made stopping and starting far less intimidating. Newspapers and bicycle clubs spread word of these improvements, and sales rose sharply among both men and women.

stem: According to the passage, what was a major reason the safety bicycle became popular?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It was cheaper to manufacture than earlier penny-farthings.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It was safer and easier for riders to manage than earlier designs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It was the first vehicle ever to use a chain drive.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It was promoted by government health agencies.

explanation: The passage states that the safety bicycle 'made it much less likely to tip forward' and allowed riders to keep both feet near the ground, making stopping and starting less intimidating. This directly supports the idea that it became popular because it was safer and easier to ride.

passage.text: Eastern gray squirrels do not rely on a single strategy to survive winter. They bury thousands of acorns individually, and their excellent spatial memory helps them retrieve many of them later. Yet they also use smell to locate nuts buried by other squirrels, and they will raid their own caches when food is scarce. This combination of planning, memory, and opportunism makes the species remarkably adaptable to changing seasons and to city parks alike.

stem: Which of the following best describes the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Eastern gray squirrels are capable of remembering the locations of thousands of buried acorns.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Eastern gray squirrels in city parks are more adaptable than those in rural forests.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Eastern gray squirrels use memory, smell, and flexible feeding strategies to survive winter.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Eastern gray squirrels bury more acorns than they can retrieve each winter.

explanation: The passage begins by saying the squirrels 'do not rely on a single strategy' and then describes spatial memory, smell, and raiding caches. The best main idea is therefore that they combine memory, smell, and flexible feeding strategies to survive winter.

passage.text: Most land plants form partnerships with mycorrhizal fungi. The fungi grow through soil and absorb water and minerals such as phosphorus, which they trade to the plant in exchange for sugars produced by photosynthesis. In return for these nutrients, the plant supplies the fungus with a steady source of energy. This ancient exchange is so widespread that some scientists describe the network of fungal threads as a kind of underground circulatory system for forest ecosystems.

stem: According to the passage, which of the following do mycorrhizal fungi provide to plants?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Water and minerals such as phosphorus

explanation: The passage explicitly states that fungi 'absorb water and minerals such as phosphorus, which they trade to the plant.' Thus, the fungi provide water and minerals to plants.

passage.text: At first glance, a tide pool appears to be a small, self-contained world, but it is constantly shaped by the ocean. Twice a day, high tide brings in nutrients, plankton, and even predators, while low tide exposes the pool to sun and air. Animals such as sea anemones and crabs survive these shifts by clinging to rocks or closing their bodies tightly. Because the conditions change so dramatically, tide-pool organisms must be highly tolerant of stress and quick to adapt.

stem: Which statement best captures the central idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tide pools are fragile environments because few organisms can live there.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tide pools undergo dramatic changes that require organisms to be adaptable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Animals in tide pools are most active during low tide.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tide pools are self-contained worlds that are unaffected by the ocean.

explanation: The passage says the tide pool is 'constantly shaped by the ocean' and that conditions change dramatically, so tide-pool organisms must be tolerant of stress and quick to adapt. That matches the central idea that tide pools undergo dramatic changes requiring adaptability.

passage.text: Urban trees are increasingly recognized as essential infrastructure rather than mere decoration. Their canopies intercept rain, slowing stormwater runoff and lessening flood risk. They absorb carbon dioxide, filter airborne pollutants, and release oxygen. In summer, shade from trees reduces buildings’ cooling costs and lowers peak electricity demand. Some cities now map tree cover alongside roads and water lines, and planners assign dollar values to the ecosystem services trees provide. This shift reflects a broader understanding that green spaces are not optional extras but vital parts of a city’s functional system.

stem: Which statement best expresses the central idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Urban trees provide measurable environmental and economic benefits and are increasingly considered essential infrastructure.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cities should prioritize planting trees primarily to make streets more attractive.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stormwater runoff is the most serious environmental problem facing modern cities.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The main value of trees lies in their ability to reduce summer cooling costs.

explanation: The passage describes multiple benefits of urban trees and says planners now treat them as vital infrastructure, so A captures the central idea.

passage.text: Tracking bird populations across whole continents used to require so many professional ornithologists that comprehensive surveys seemed impossible. Citizen science projects have changed this picture. Through mobile apps, thousands of ordinary people record bird sightings and submit details about species, behavior, and location. Scientists combine these observations with training materials and automated filters to reduce misidentifications. Because volunteers can cover vast areas over many years, researchers now monitor migration patterns and population changes that would otherwise remain hidden. Conservation decisions increasingly depend on this data.

stem: According to the passage, what has made comprehensive bird surveys possible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mobile apps that automatically identify bird species

choices.label: B
choices.text: The participation of large numbers of volunteer observers

choices.label: C
choices.text: The training of many more professional ornithologists

explanation: The passage says comprehensive surveys became possible because volunteers can cover vast areas over many years, making B correct.

passage.text: The abyssal plains of the Pacific contain trillions of polymetallic nodules, rock formations rich in manganese, nickel, and cobalt. These metals are in high demand for batteries and electronics, making seabed mining commercially appealing. Yet the nodules grow extremely slowly, over millions of years, and each one serves as a habitat for specialized deep-sea organisms. Scientists warn that mining would destroy these communities across vast areas, and recovery would be effectively impossible on human timescales. For this reason, some argue that investments in recycling and alternative battery chemistries should reduce pressure to mine the ocean floor.

stem: Which statement best captures the central idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deep-sea mining is necessary because land-based sources of battery metals are nearly exhausted.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The slow growth of polymetallic nodules makes them worthless to mining companies.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deep-sea mining offers commercial opportunities, but scientists warn that it would cause severe and lasting environmental damage.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Battery recycling and alternative chemistries have already eliminated the need for seabed mining.

explanation: The passage balances the commercial appeal of seabed mining with warnings about irreversible environmental harm, so C states the central idea.

passage.text: The Romans of the early republic lived in the shadow of Etruscan city-states to the north. Roman priests adopted the Etruscan practice of inspecting the livers of sacrificed animals to interpret the gods' will. Etruscan engineers taught Roman builders techniques for arch construction and land drainage, which later made large public works possible. Roman political life also changed as magistrates adopted the Etruscan curule chair and the fasces, symbols of authority. These cultural borrowings, taken selectively and adapted, helped shape Roman institutions.

stem: According to the passage, which practice did Roman priests adopt from the Etruscans?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Using the curule chair as a symbol of office

choices.label: B
choices.text: Building arches for large public works

choices.label: D
choices.text: Examining animal organs to learn the gods' will

explanation: The passage explicitly states that Roman priests adopted the Etruscan practice of inspecting the livers of sacrificed animals, so D is correct.

passage.text: Desert plants employ a striking variety of survival strategies. The saguaro cactus stores water in its expandable trunk and extends shallow roots that capture even light rainfall. Many desert annuals follow a different path: their seeds stay dormant in the soil for years and germinate only after a heavy rain. Other plants drop leaves when water is scarce. Such diverse responses suggest a common lesson: in the desert, survival depends on making the most of unpredictable water.

stem: Which statement best expresses the central idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Desert plants survive by using various strategies to capture, store, or conserve water.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Saguaro cacti are better adapted than other desert plants.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most desert plants germinate only after a heavy rain.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Desert plants rarely need water because they remain dormant.

explanation: The passage presents several different desert-plant strategies and concludes that survival depends on making the most of unpredictable water, so A is correct.

passage.text: In many cities, summer temperatures can be several degrees higher in paved neighborhoods than in nearby parks. Trees help cool the air by shading surfaces and releasing water vapor through their leaves. However, not every tree produces the same effect: species with broad, dense canopies offer more shade, and trees planted near buildings can reduce air-conditioning use more than trees planted in open lots. City planners therefore need to think carefully about tree species and placement to get the greatest cooling benefit.

stem: Which choice best states the central idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All trees reduce surrounding air temperatures by the same amount.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Trees in parks are always cooler than trees planted near buildings.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Urban trees provide the greatest cooling benefit when their species and location are deliberately chosen.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Releasing water vapor is the only way trees lower temperatures in cities.

explanation: The text explains that trees vary in how much they cool their surroundings and concludes that planners should select tree species and locations carefully. Therefore, C states the central idea.

passage.text: Some ecosystems rely on soil seed banks—seeds buried in the ground that wait for favorable conditions. In fire-prone regions, many of these seeds remain dormant until heat or smoke from a wildfire triggers them to sprout. This adaptation allows plants to recolonize an area quickly after a blaze. Other seeds in the same soil may require years of cold before they can grow, while many are eaten by rodents or decay before they ever germinate.

stem: According to the text, what can cause some seeds in a fire-prone region to begin germinating?

choices.label: B
choices.text: A prolonged period of heavy rain

explanation: The text explicitly states that in fire-prone regions many seeds remain dormant until heat or smoke from a wildfire triggers them to sprout.

passage.text: The Inca used quipus, sets of colored, knotted cords, to keep records. Spanish chroniclers wrote that quipu specialists could record census data, tribute, and perhaps even narratives. Modern researchers have shown that the number and arrangement of knots encode numerical information, but they still debate whether quipus also conveyed nonnumerical meaning. Thus, quipus are best understood as complex information-storage devices, even if some details of their use remain uncertain.

stem: Which choice best states the central idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Quipus were purely decorative objects with no clear purpose.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Spanish chroniclers deliberately exaggerated what quipus could record.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Quipu readings were based mainly on the colors of the cords.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Quipus functioned as record-keeping tools whose full range of meaning is still debated.

explanation: The passage says quipus were information-storage devices and that scholars still debate whether they carried nonnumerical meaning, which matches D.

passage.text: Tide pools are small depressions in rocky shores that hold seawater when the tide recedes. At low tide, visitors can observe anemones, crabs, and small fish that remain hidden when waves cover the area. At high tide, many of these animals swim or wash out to feed, making them harder to see. Tide-pool life is especially visible on calm days, when water is clear and the pools are not stirred by rough surf.

stem: According to the text, when are tide-pool animals most likely to be seen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At high tide, when they swim out to feed

choices.label: B
choices.text: At low tide, on calm days

choices.label: C
choices.text: During storms, when waves stir the pools

explanation: The text states that at low tide visitors can observe tide-pool animals and that they are especially visible on calm days.

passage.text: Online platforms use algorithms to recommend content based on what users click, like, or watch. Over time, this can create a 'filter bubble' in which people see mainly posts that reinforce their existing beliefs. Some researchers argue that the platform is responsible for narrowing perspectives, while others point out that users' own choices, such as which accounts to follow, matter just as much. In practice, both algorithmic sorting and personal selection contribute to the range of information a person encounters online.

stem: Which choice best states the central idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Users have no control over what social media algorithms show them.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Filter bubbles are caused mainly by a failure in online advertising.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both algorithms and users' own selections help determine what information people see online.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Researchers agree that platforms are solely responsible for narrowing perspectives.

explanation: The final sentence states that both algorithmic sorting and personal selection contribute to the information people see, so C is the central idea.

passage.text: Urban community gardens do more than provide fresh produce. In many neighborhoods, they create shared spaces where residents of different ages and backgrounds interact regularly. Researchers have found that these gardens can lower crime rates, improve mental health, and increase food security in nearby households. Yet their long-term success depends on steady access to land, water, and volunteers. Without ongoing support from local organizations, even thriving gardens may disappear when a lease ends or funding dries up.

stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Researchers have found that urban community gardens can lower crime rates.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Community gardens offer several benefits, but their survival depends on continued resources.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Local organizations should provide every community garden with land, water, and volunteers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most community gardens close when their leases end or funding is reduced.

explanation: The text presents multiple benefits of community gardens, then qualifies that these benefits depend on ongoing resources such as land, water, and volunteers. Choice B captures both parts of that main idea.

passage.text: Desert tortoises are master water savers. They spend up to 95% of their lives in burrows, emerging mainly to eat or after rain. Their bodies can store water in the bladder, and they reabsorb it when necessary. Instead of drinking, they get most of their water from the plants they eat, especially wildflowers. During droughts, they may reduce activity to conserve energy and moisture, and some can survive more than a year without access to free water.

stem: According to the text, how do desert tortoises obtain most of their water?

choices.label: A
choices.text: By drinking from rain pools after storms

choices.label: B
choices.text: By storing large amounts of water in their burrows

choices.label: C
choices.text: From the moisture in plants they eat

choices.label: D
choices.text: By reducing their activity during droughts

explanation: The text explicitly states that desert tortoises get most of their water from the plants they eat, not from drinking free water.

passage.text: Slow reading, a deliberate practice of reading at a reduced pace, has gained attention as a counterweight to the rapid skimming encouraged by digital media. Advocates argue that slowing down allows readers to notice language, follow complex arguments, and retain information longer. Some studies link this practice to improved comprehension and empathy. However, researchers caution that it is not necessarily superior for all materials; quick scanning may be more effective when searching for a specific fact or deciding whether a source is useful.

stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Slow reading improves comprehension and empathy and should replace digital skimming.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Digital media has caused a decline in readers' ability to follow complex arguments.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Quick scanning is often more effective than slow reading when evaluating online sources.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Slow reading offers benefits, but rapid scanning also has appropriate uses.

explanation: The text presents the advantages of slow reading, then notes that quick scanning is better in some situations. Choice D captures this balanced central idea.

passage.text: Farmers' markets have become important sources of fresh food in many cities. One factor in their growth is the expansion of wireless payment terminals, which allow shoppers to use Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits to buy fruits and vegetables. Before these terminals, many markets could not accept SNAP because handling paper vouchers required extra staff and paperwork. Researchers note that markets with electronic benefit transfer (EBT) machines report higher sales and more low-income customers, making the machines a key tool for food access.

stem: According to the text, why were many farmers' markets unable to accept SNAP benefits in the past?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They lacked wireless payment terminals needed to process benefits efficiently.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They were not located in cities with SNAP programs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fresh fruits and vegetables were not covered by food assistance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: SNAP vouchers were only accepted at large grocery stores.

explanation: The text says that before wireless payment terminals, many markets could not accept SNAP because handling paper vouchers required extra staff and paperwork.

passage.text: Trees can substantially reduce summer temperatures in cities. Through shade and the release of water vapor, a mature tree can cool the air around it by several degrees. A 2019 study of 97 cities found that neighborhoods with more tree canopy had noticeably lower surface temperatures than nearby areas with sparse tree cover. Planting trees is therefore often proposed as a natural solution to extreme heat. Even so, city planners point out that trees require long-term care, including watering and pruning, if they are to survive urban conditions.

stem: Which statement best captures the central idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A single mature tree can cool the air around it by several degrees.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tree canopy helps cool city neighborhoods, but urban trees require ongoing maintenance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: City planners agree that trees are more effective than air conditioning.

choices.label: D
