passage.text: On the city's #12 airport bus, the fare is $2.50 for passengers who pay with coins and $2.75 for passengers who use the mobile app. The bus does not accept paper bills. Lena has exactly $2.50 in coins and wants to board the #12 bus.

stem: Which conclusion most logically follows from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lena must use the mobile app to ride the bus.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lena can ride the bus by paying the $2.50 coin fare.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lena has enough money for the app fare.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lena cannot ride the bus because she does not have $2.75.

explanation: The bus accepts coins, and the coin fare is $2.50. Lena has exactly that amount, so she can pay the coin fare and board. The other choices conflict with the fare information or add unsupported requirements.

passage.text: In a science class, students placed identical bean seeds in three trays. Each tray received the same amount of water, but Tray 1 was kept in a dark closet, Tray 2 on a windowsill with indirect light, and Tray 3 in direct sunlight. After two weeks, the seeds in Tray 2 had the greatest average height, Tray 3 had slightly shorter plants, and Tray 1 had no sprouts at all.

stem: Which conclusion most logically follows from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bean plants grow tallest when kept in a dark closet.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct sunlight prevents bean seeds from germinating.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bean seeds require water and fertilizer to germinate.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Under these conditions, bean seeds in darkness did not sprout.

explanation: Tray 1 was kept in darkness and had no sprouts, while the trays exposed to light produced plants. This directly supports the conclusion that, under these conditions, the seeds in darkness did not sprout. The other choices overstate or contradict the results.

passage.text: To plant vegetables in the Hillside Community Garden, a resident must attend a spring orientation and complete at least one volunteer shift. Amy is a resident who attended this year's orientation, but she has not yet completed any volunteer shift this season.

stem: Which conclusion most logically follows from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amy is allowed to plant vegetables because she attended orientation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Amy must attend next year's orientation before she can volunteer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Amy does not currently meet the requirements for planting vegetables.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Amy cannot satisfy the requirements this season.

explanation: The garden requires both orientation attendance and one volunteer shift. Amy has completed only the orientation, so she is missing a required condition and does not currently meet the requirements. The other choices are unsupported or contradicted by the passage.

passage.text: A small airline's overbooking policy states that when a flight is full, passengers holding flexible tickets may be moved to the next available flight at no charge. Passengers holding nonrefundable tickets are not eligible for that free rebooking; they are placed on a standby list and may fly only if a seat opens up. Marcus is holding a nonrefundable ticket for a flight that has just been announced as overbooked.

stem: Which conclusion most logically follows from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Marcus is not eligible for the airline's free rebooking option.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Marcus will be moved to the next available flight at no charge.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Marcus can board his flight by showing a flexible ticket.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Marcus will have to buy a new ticket before he can fly standby.

explanation: The policy says passengers with nonrefundable tickets are not eligible for free rebooking. Marcus has a nonrefundable ticket, so he is not eligible for that option. The other choices contradict the policy or add unsupported conditions.

passage.text: Some tiger moths produce clicking sounds when bats approach. Bats that had never encountered tiger moths initially attacked a dummy moth. But after the clicks were played alongside the dummy one or two times, the bats avoided the dummy even when later presentations were silent. The clicks therefore appear to act as ____.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: an instinctive warning that all bats are born recognizing

choices.label: B
choices.text: a loud noise meant to disorient bats and make them fly away

choices.label: C
choices.text: a signal that bats learn to associate with prey they should avoid

choices.label: D
choices.text: an imitation of the sounds made by a larger predator of bats

explanation: The bats' initial attacks show that the clicks did not trigger an innate avoidance response; because avoidance appeared only after the clicks had been paired with the dummy, the clicks act as a learned warning signal.

passage.text: At an ancient farming village, archaeologists found a large clay pot beside a grinding stone and a baking oven. The pot contained the charred remains of wheat and barley. It had no handles, and when filled with grain it would have been too heavy to lift. The archaeologists concluded that the pot was used for ____.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: storing grain before it was ground into flour

choices.label: B
choices.text: transporting harvested grain to distant settlements

choices.label: C
choices.text: mixing bread dough in large quantities

choices.label: D
choices.text: soaking seeds to make them sprout

explanation: The pot's location near grinding tools and its contents strongly suggest storage before processing; the statement that it was too heavy to lift rules out transporting it.

passage.text: Researchers trained bumblebees to fly to a feeder marked with a blue triangle. Half of the bees were then allowed to sleep overnight, while the other half were kept awake. The next morning, the rested bees found the correct feeder significantly more often than the sleep-deprived bees did. The researchers concluded that ____.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: bumblebees need more sleep than any other insect

choices.label: B
choices.text: sleep-deprived bees could not see the blue triangle

choices.label: C
choices.text: the blue triangle is a natural food cue for bumblebees

choices.label: D
choices.text: sleep helped the bumblebees consolidate their memory of the route

explanation: The only difference between the two groups was sleep, and the rested group performed better, so the results support a role for sleep in memory consolidation.

passage.text: When ocean temperatures rise, algae inside coral produce harmful substances, and the coral responds by expelling the algae. Corals that survived a period of unusually warm water were found to contain especially high levels of a pigment that absorbs sunlight. This pigment most likely helped those corals survive by ____.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: providing food for the coral after the algae were expelled

choices.label: B
choices.text: shielding the algae from some sunlight and thus reducing the production of harmful substances

choices.label: C
choices.text: attracting a new species of algae that can survive in warmer water

choices.label: D
choices.text: warning nearby fish to stay away from the coral

explanation: The coral with more pigment survived heat stress; since the pigment absorbs light, it likely reduced the light-triggered production of harmful substances by algae.

passage.text: Reed warblers sometimes raise cuckoo chicks whose egg has been laid in their nest. In an experiment, researchers added a foreign egg that looked very different from the warbler's own eggs to some nests; the warblers usually threw it out within hours. In other nests, researchers added a foreign egg that looked almost exactly like the warbler's own eggs; the warblers usually incubated it. The warblers' rejection behavior was therefore triggered mainly by ____.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the size of the foreign egg

choices.label: B
choices.text: the number of eggs already in the nest

choices.label: C
choices.text: the appearance of the foreign egg

choices.label: D
choices.text: the cuckoo's behavior after laying the egg

explanation: The warblers' behavior changed only with how much the eggs resembled their own, so egg appearance was the main factor triggering rejection.

passage.text: Nia hung a wet towel on a clothesline in her yard. The sun shone all day, the temperature stayed well above freezing, and no one touched the towel. By late afternoon, the towel was completely dry.

stem: Which conclusion is most logically supported by the information in the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The water in the towel evaporated.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The towel was taken inside by someone.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The water in the towel froze.

explanation: Since no one touched the towel, it did not rain, and the temperature stayed above freezing, the only logical conclusion is that the water evaporated.

passage.text: At Brookdale High School, every student who is on the honor roll has completed at least twenty hours of community service. Jordan is on the honor roll.

stem: Which conclusion is most logically supported by the information in the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Jordan is a senior at Brookdale High School.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Jordan has completed at least twenty hours of community service.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every student who has completed twenty hours of community service is on the honor roll.

explanation: The passage states that all honor roll students have completed at least twenty hours of community service. Since Jordan is on the honor roll, Jordan must have completed at least twenty hours.

passage.text: Every train on the Red Line stops at Central Station. The 7:30 express is a Red Line train. The station announcement said that all Red Line trains are running ten minutes late.

stem: Which conclusion is most logically supported by the information in the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The 7:30 express does not stop at Central Station.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The 7:30 express is running about ten minutes late.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The 7:30 express will arrive before its scheduled time.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The 7:30 express will not stop at Central Station today.

explanation: The 7:30 express is a Red Line train, and the announcement says all Red Line trains are running ten minutes late, so the 7:30 express must also be running about ten minutes late.

passage.text: According to a local gardening guide, every plant native to the Sonoran Desert requires very little water. The desert marigold is native to the Sonoran Desert.

stem: Which conclusion is most logically supported by the information in the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Only desert marigolds require very little water.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All plants that require very little water are native to the Sonoran Desert.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Desert marigolds are the most common plant in the Sonoran Desert.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Desert marigolds require very little water.

explanation: The guide says every native Sonoran Desert plant requires very little water. Since the desert marigold is native to the Sonoran Desert, it must require very little water.

passage.text: The sign outside the Rialto Theater reads: “No one under the age of 12 is admitted to the 9:30 showing.” Leah is 10 years old and wants to see the 9:30 showing.

stem: Which conclusion is most logically supported by the information in the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Leah will not be admitted to the 9:30 showing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Leah is too young to see any movie at the theater.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Leah can see the 9:30 showing if she arrives with an adult.

explanation: The sign says no one under 12 is admitted to the 9:30 showing, and Leah is 10, so she will not be admitted to that showing.

passage.text: Certain tomato plants release chemical compounds into the air when caterpillars begin eating their leaves. Researchers have observed that these airborne compounds attract parasitic wasps. The wasps lay their eggs inside the caterpillars, and the developing wasp larvae eventually kill the caterpillars. Thus, a tomato plant under caterpillar attack is best described as a plant that ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: directly poisons the caterpillars that feed on it

choices.label: B
choices.text: signals for help from an organism that can fight the caterpillars

choices.label: C
choices.text: produces chemicals that repel all insect visitors

explanation: The passage says the plant releases compounds that attract wasps, which kill the caterpillars. This is best described as signaling for help from an organism that can fight the caterpillars.

passage.text: A paleontologist uncovered a nearly complete fossil skeleton of a small dinosaur. The skull has very large eye sockets, and the hind limbs are long compared with the animal's body length. Among modern animals, large eye sockets are characteristic of species that are active at night, and relatively long hind limbs are characteristic of species that can run quickly. The paleontologist most reasonably concluded that this dinosaur was ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: active mainly at night and capable of quick running

choices.label: B
choices.text: active mainly during the day and slow-moving

choices.label: C
choices.text: unable to see and therefore dependent on touch

choices.label: D
choices.text: adapted for life in trees rather than on the ground

explanation: Large eye sockets suggest night activity, and long hind limbs suggest fast running. Combining these two observations supports the conclusion that the dinosaur was active mainly at night and capable of quick running.

passage.text: For years, the public library in a small town closed at 5 p.m. on weekdays. Last year, the library began staying open until 8 p.m. on Tuesdays and Thursdays. The library's records show that e-book borrowing increased sharply in that year, while borrowing of printed books stayed about the same. The director concluded that the extended evening hours most likely ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: discouraged residents from borrowing printed books

choices.label: B
choices.text: caused the library to purchase fewer e-books

choices.label: C
choices.text: reduced the total number of library visitors

choices.label: D
choices.text: increased use of the library's e-book collection

explanation: The only change mentioned is the added evening hours, and e-book borrowing increased sharply during that period. The most directly supported conclusion is that extended evening hours increased use of the e-book collection.

passage.text: A city bus route had ten stops and completed one loop in 50 minutes. The city then added two new stops on the same route but did not add any buses. Soon afterward, riders reported that the average wait for a bus was longer than before. Which conclusion is most directly supported?

stem: Which conclusion is most directly supported by the information in the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The new stops caused passengers to ride shorter distances.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The bus company increased the number of buses on the route.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The extra stops added time to each loop, so buses became less frequent.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The extra stops made the buses run faster between stops.

explanation: With more stops and the same number of buses, each trip around the route takes longer. This makes the interval between buses longer, which explains the longer average wait.

passage.text: In a memory experiment, two groups of students studied the same list of twenty words. One group then stayed awake for twenty minutes, while the other group took a twenty-minute nap. When tested later, the students who napped recalled significantly more words than those who stayed awake. Which conclusion is most directly supported by the experiment?

stem: Which conclusion is most directly supported by the experiment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The students who napped were given a shorter list of words.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The students who stayed awake studied the words for less time.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taking a short nap helped the students remember the words.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The nap improved the students' ability to see the words.

explanation: Both groups studied the same list for the same time, and the napping group recalled more words. The most direct conclusion is that the short nap helped the students remember the words.

passage.text: In a coastal grassland, researchers placed fine mesh bags over the flower heads of a native plant species before seeds matured. The bags let air and sunlight reach the flowers but kept all insects away. At the end of the season, the bagged plants produced fewer seeds than nearby unbagged plants of the same species. Since the only difference between the two groups was the absence of insects, the researchers concluded that __________.

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The mesh bags reduced the amount of sunlight reaching the flowers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Insect visits contributed to seed production in this plant species.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Unbagged plants produced fewer seeds because they were damaged by insects.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The bagged plants would produce more seeds in the following growing season.

explanation: The bagged plants differed from unbagged plants only in that insects could not reach them, and they produced fewer seeds. Therefore, the most directly supported conclusion is that insect visits contributed to seed production.

passage.text: A museum conservator tested a new cleaning gel on a small, damaged corner of a Renaissance painting. The gel removed the discolored varnish without lifting any pigment. Encouraged by this result, the conservator decided that the gel could be used on the rest of the painting because __________.

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The damaged corner had the same varnish and paint layer as the rest of the painting.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The entire painting was equally valuable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any cleaning method that works on old paintings works on all paintings.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The damaged corner was the only part of the painting that needed cleaning.

explanation: A successful test on one part of a painting supports using the same method elsewhere only if that part is representative of the rest. The answer identifies that necessary similarity.

passage.text: In a study of five neighboring lakes, scientists measured water temperature and counted the number of fish species in each lake. The two shallowest lakes had the warmest water and also supported the greatest number of fish species; the deepest lake had the coldest water and the fewest species. The other lakes fell in between. The scientists concluded that, in these lakes, water temperature is __________.

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The only factor that determines the number of fish species.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Positively associated with the number of fish species.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Caused by the number of fish species.

choices.label: D
choices.text: More important than depth in affecting the number of fish species.

explanation: The data show that warmer lakes tended to have more fish species, so the most directly supported conclusion is a positive association. The other choices claim causation, exclusivity, or relative importance not established by the data.

passage.text: A linguist recorded conversations among members of a remote community. She found that speakers over sixty used a set of traditional words for tools and plants, while speakers under thirty used borrowed words from a neighboring language for the same items. The middle-aged speakers sometimes used both. The linguist predicted that, if current patterns continue, the traditional words will eventually __________.

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Be used by all age groups again.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Become more numerous than borrowed words.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cease to be used in daily conversation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the meaning of the borrowed words.

explanation: With older speakers using traditional words and younger speakers using borrowed words, continuing this pattern would mean the traditional words gradually disappear from daily use.

passage.text: Astronomers monitoring a distant star noticed that its brightness decreased by 0.4 percent for exactly five hours and then returned to normal. The same decrease occurred again 3.2 days later, and then again after another 3.2 days. Because the dimming was regular and repeated, the astronomers concluded that it was probably caused by __________.

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An object passing in front of the star at regular intervals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Random changes in the star's internal temperature.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A single burst of dust between Earth and the star.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The star expanding and contracting unevenly.

explanation: A regular, repeated dip in brightness is best explained by an orbiting object passing in front of the star at regular intervals. The other choices involve irregular or one-time events.

passage.text: A museum owned a painting that was believed to have been completed in 1750. During a restoration, conservators found a pigment in the painting that was not synthesized until 1850. It is known that if a painting contains a pigment that was synthesized after the painting's presumed creation date, then the painting could not have been created on that date. Therefore, ______.

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The painting was likely completed in 1850.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The painting cannot have been completed in 1750.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The pigment must have been present in the original 1750 paint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The painting's presumed date is correct.

explanation: Since the pigment was not synthesized until 1850, it could not have been in a painting finished in 1750. Thus the painting cannot have been completed in 1750.

passage.text: An astronomer observed that a star dims slightly for two hours every 3.1 days. The size of the dip is too small to be caused by a planet, and the dimming is not caused by changes in the star itself. The astronomer hypothesizes that a clump of dust orbits the star. If this hypothesis is correct, then ______.

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the dust completes one orbit of the star every 3.1 days.

choices.label: B
choices.text: the dust is stationary in space.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the dip in brightness is caused by another star passing in front.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the star will stop dimming within a year.

explanation: A repeating dip every 3.1 days most directly implies that the orbiting dust completes an orbit in that same period, bringing it between the star and Earth every 3.1 days.

passage.text: A biologist studying a lake found that the population of a certain fish species declined sharply after a factory upstream began discharging warm water. The fish species is known to reproduce only in water below 20°C. Summer water temperatures near the discharge are now consistently above 20°C. Therefore, ______.

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The fish have moved to deeper, cooler water.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The factory discharge contains no chemical pollutants.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The warm water prevented the fish from reproducing successfully.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The fish population will recover naturally next year.

explanation: The fish can reproduce only below 20°C, and the discharge now keeps summer temperatures above that threshold. The most direct conclusion is that warm water interfered with reproduction, causing the decline.

passage.text: A road crew applies salt to roads only when the forecast calls for temperatures below -4°C with precipitation. One winter night, the temperature fell to -7°C but the road surface stayed dry. The crew did not salt the roads, and no ice formed. The crew's decision was justified because ______.

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: salt only works when temperatures are above -4°C.

choices.label: B
choices.text: icy conditions require moisture as well as low temperature.

choices.label: C
choices.text: road crews should never salt roads.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the forecast called for rain, not snow.

explanation: Since the road surface stayed dry, there was no moisture to freeze. Thus the lack of ice is explained by the absence of precipitation, meaning that low temperature alone did not justify salting the roads.

passage.text: A school board received a donation to buy either laptop computers or tablets for every student. The donation specifies that funds must be used for devices that allow students to type long essays. Tablets are lighter and have longer battery life, but most external keyboards for tablets are sold separately and are difficult to track. The board should buy laptops because ______.

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: B
choices.text: laptops are more suitable for the required activity of typing long essays.

choices.label: C
choices.text: tablets have longer battery life than laptops.

explanation: The donation's purpose is to support typing long essays, and laptops are directly suited for that task, whereas tablets require separate keyboards that are difficult to track. Therefore, laptops better match the stated requirement.

passage.text: Last fall, Greenville High School started recycling paper in the cafeteria. The cafeteria recycled 200 pounds of paper in October, 250 pounds in November, and 300 pounds in December. If this pattern continues, the most likely weight in January is...

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?
explanation: The monthly amounts increase by 50 pounds each month: 200, 250, 300. Continuing the pattern, January would be about 350 pounds.

passage.text: Biologists observed that a species of squirrel in a city park frequently tore open paper wrappers and plastic bags to eat leftover food. After the park replaced open trash bins with lidded bins that squirrels could not open, the number of squirrels seen eating leftover food dropped sharply. This change suggests that...

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: squirrels prefer pine cones to leftover food

choices.label: B
choices.text: the lidded bins caused squirrels to rely on other animals for food

choices.label: C
choices.text: squirrels had been taking food from people's hands

choices.label: D
choices.text: easy access to leftover food had been attracting squirrels to the trash

explanation: Because the only change was making trash bins closed and inaccessible, the drop in squirrels eating leftover food indicates that easy access to trash had encouraged the behavior.

passage.text: An average summer in the region brings about 12 inches of rain, and reservoirs usually drop during these months. Last summer, however, the region received 16 inches of rain, and one reservoir's water level rose slightly. This suggests that...

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the greater-than-usual rainfall likely contributed to the reservoir's rise

choices.label: B
choices.text: reservoirs in the region now rise every summer

choices.label: C
choices.text: rainfall has no effect on reservoir water levels

choices.label: D
choices.text: the reservoir would have risen even without the extra rain

explanation: The only notable change from a typical summer was higher rainfall, and the reservoir rose instead of following its usual pattern, so the extra rainfall likely contributed to the rise.

passage.text: The English word "silly" comes from the Old English word "sǣlig," which meant "happy" or "blessed." Over many centuries, its meaning shifted until it came to mean "foolish." Historical records show that this kind of meaning change happened to many other words as well. Therefore,...

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the meaning of a word today is always the same as its original meaning

choices.label: B
choices.text: Old English words cannot be understood by modern speakers

choices.label: C
choices.text: the present-day meaning of a word may be quite different from its earlier meaning

choices.label: D
choices.text: language change occurs only in English

explanation: The passage uses "silly" as an example of a word whose meaning changed over centuries, supporting the conclusion that current meanings can differ from earlier meanings.

passage.text: A researcher followed 500 high school students across one school year. Students who reviewed their class notes within 24 hours of a lecture scored, on average, 15 percent higher on exams than students who reviewed notes later. The groups were similar in prior grades and total study time. This suggests that...

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: students who wait longer than 24 hours always fail their exams

choices.label: B
choices.text: reviewing notes soon after a lecture is linked to stronger exam performance

choices.label: C
choices.text: reviewing notes within 24 hours causes an increase of at least 15 percent for every student

choices.label: D
choices.text: lecture notes are the only important study material

explanation: The passage describes an association between reviewing notes within 24 hours and higher exam scores, but it does not establish guarantee, universal causation, or exclusive method.

passage.text: The Oakville High garden club planted tomato seedlings in early April. By late May, the seedlings had grown into small plants with flowers. The club's advisor noted, "Tomato flowers must be pollinated before fruit can develop. Our school's only beehive was moved to a farm across town last month."

stem: Which conclusion is best supported by the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The tomato plants are unlikely to produce as much fruit as they would have if the beehive remained.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The tomato plants will never produce tomatoes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The garden club should have planted the tomatoes later in the spring.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The absence of bees will make the tomatoes larger.

explanation: Because tomato flowers must be pollinated to produce fruit and the school's only beehive is gone, the plants will likely receive less pollination and produce less fruit. Choice B is too absolute, while C and D are not supported.

passage.text: For the past fifty years, a beach town's seaside homes have been protected by tall sand dunes. Annual measurements show that the dunes have gradually lost about half their height during that period. Oceanographers also found that the average intensity of winter storms in the area has increased over the same fifty years. The town council is now debating whether to pay for a beach restoration project.

stem: The passage most strongly supports which conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The dunes are no longer as effective at protecting homes from storm waves as they once were.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The dunes will disappear completely within the next year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The dunes have grown taller because of stronger storms.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The sand dunes have never protected the town's homes.

explanation: The dunes have lost half their height while storms have become more intense, so the dunes are less effective as storm protection than they once were. The other choices either contradict the passage or make unsupported extreme claims.

passage.text: Maya lifted the cardboard box onto the kitchen table. A note taped to the top read, "For a rainy day." Inside, wrapped in brown paper, was a thick wool sweater and a pair of knit gloves. Maya lived in a city where the temperature rarely dropped below seventy degrees.

stem: Which conclusion about the sweater and gloves is most directly supported by the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are intended for use in cold weather.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They were knitted by Maya's grandmother.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They will be useful during Maya's daily commute.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They were purchased recently from a local store.

explanation: A thick wool sweater and knit gloves are typically made for cold conditions, so the most directly supported conclusion is that they are intended for cold weather. The other choices rely on information not given in the passage.

passage.text: Astronomers observed a distant star and recorded its brightness every few minutes. They found that the star's brightness decreased by about one percent at regular intervals, with each dip lasting roughly nine hours and repeating every twenty-seven days. Further observations revealed a large planet circling the star with an orbital period of twenty-seven days.

stem: Which conclusion is best supported by the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The planet passes in front of the star once every twenty-seven days.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The star's brightness changes because of activity inside the planet.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The planet emits its own visible light.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The dips are caused by the planet moving behind the star.

explanation: The brightness dips repeat every twenty-seven days, exactly matching the planet's orbital period, so the dips are best explained by the planet crossing in front of the star. A planet moving behind the star would not block the star's light, and the other choices are unsupported.

passage.text: For years, the Maple Street Library held a children's story hour on Wednesday mornings at 10:00. Attendance was low, so librarians sent a survey to local parents. Many parents said that the Wednesday time conflicted with school drop-off and asked for a later time. The library changed story hour to Wednesday at 4:30. Over the next two months, attendance more than tripled.

stem: The passage most strongly supports which conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Parents generally prefer all library programs to occur in the afternoon.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The later story hour time was more convenient for the families it serves.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Children in the area no longer attend school on Wednesday mornings.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The library added many new children's books during the two months.

explanation: The parents identified the morning time as a conflict, and attendance tripled after the library moved the event to the afternoon. This most directly supports the conclusion that the new time was more convenient. The other choices are either overgeneralized or not supported by evidence.

passage.text: Researchers studying a small lake recorded when winter ice melted and then counted young fish during a survey each summer. In years when ice melted early, the summer survey found more young fish than in years when ice melted late. Early melting gives young fish a longer growing season before the survey. Therefore, the timing of ice melt likely ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: affects how many young fish are present during the summer survey

choices.label: B
choices.text: is caused by the number of young fish found in the summer survey

choices.label: C
choices.text: has no effect on young fish populations

choices.label: D
choices.text: is less important than water temperature in determining fish growth

explanation: Earlier ice melt is followed by more young fish in the summer survey, and the text provides a plausible reason: a longer growing season. Thus the timing of ice melt likely affects how many young fish are present.

passage.text: After a volcano erupted, researchers measured the depth of ash deposited on farm fields. Bean plants in fields with a thin layer of ash grew slightly better than bean plants in fields with no ash, but plants in fields with a thick layer of ash grew much worse. Therefore, the effect of volcanic ash on bean growth ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: is always harmful to bean plants

choices.label: B
choices.text: is always helpful to bean plants

choices.label: C
choices.text: cannot be measured by field researchers

choices.label: D
choices.text: depends on the amount of ash present

explanation: Thin ash was followed by slightly better growth, while thick ash was followed by much worse growth. The most direct conclusion is that the effect depends on how much ash is present.

passage.text: A bookstore compared sales of a novel in paperback and electronic form. In months when the paperback was discounted, total sales of the novel rose, but sales of the electronic edition fell. Many customers bought the less expensive format. Therefore, the discount on the paperback likely ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: increased the sales of the electronic edition

choices.label: B
choices.text: persuaded some customers who would have bought the electronic edition to buy the paperback instead

choices.label: C
choices.text: had no effect on customers' format choices

choices.label: D
choices.text: was caused by a decrease in electronic edition sales

explanation: The electronic edition sold less during the same months the discounted paperback sold more, and customers favored the less expensive format. This best supports the conclusion that the discount led some customers to choose the paperback instead of the electronic edition.

passage.text: In a study of classroom noise, students took the same math test in a quiet room and in a room with intermittent traffic noise. Students' average scores were nearly identical in the two conditions. The researchers concluded that, for this test, intermittent traffic noise ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: B
choices.text: made the math test more difficult

choices.label: C
choices.text: did not significantly affect students' performance

choices.label: D
choices.text: affected students' scores more than quiet conditions did

explanation: Because scores were nearly identical in the quiet and noisy conditions, the most directly supported conclusion is that the intermittent traffic noise did not significantly affect performance on that test.

passage.text: In a coastal town, the population of a shorebird declined sharply after a beach renovation project removed large amounts of seaweed from the shore. These birds feed almost entirely on small insects that live in decaying seaweed. Therefore, the population decline was most likely caused by ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the beach renovation attracting more predators to the shore

choices.label: B
choices.text: the removal of the birds' main food source

choices.label: C
choices.text: the insects increasing in number after the renovation

choices.label: D
choices.text: the birds moving to inland forests because of the construction noise

explanation: Seaweed removal would remove the habitat of the insects that the birds depend on for food. The sharp decline is therefore most directly explained by the loss of the birds' main food source.

passage.text: Researchers studying honeybees found that bees prevented from sleeping for one night were significantly less likely than well-rested bees to perform the precise waggle dance that indicates the direction and distance of a food source. Their ordinary flying, feeding, and grooming behaviors were completely unchanged. The researchers concluded that, in honeybees, sleep serves a crucial role in ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
explanation: The observed deficit was specific to the waggle dance, a complex communication behavior, while basic behaviors such as flying, feeding, and grooming were unchanged. Thus the passage supports an inference about sleep's role in complex communication, not survival, appetite, or hierarchy.

passage.text: A mineral sample from a Martian crater contains a type of clay that, on Earth, forms only during prolonged contact with liquid water. The crater has no ancient riverbeds, lakebeds, or any other water-formed features. Planetary scientists concluded that the clay was not formed in this crater but was instead ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: B
choices.text: carried into the crater by wind.

explanation: Because the clay requires liquid water to form and the crater shows no sign of water, the clay could not have formed there. The most consistent explanation is that it formed elsewhere and was later moved, with wind being the transport mechanism implied by the lack of water features.

passage.text: Archaeologists found a wooden document in a medieval monastery and assigned a date of 1320 to the wood based on its tree rings. The ink used for the text, however, contains a chemical compound that was not used in ink production anywhere until the 1800s. Since the tree-ring dating is reliable, the most reasonable explanation is that ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the document's text was added many years after the wood was cut.

choices.label: B
choices.text: the tree-ring date was incorrectly calculated.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the compound occurred naturally in medieval ink.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the document was not made of medieval wood.

explanation: The wood reliably dates to 1320, but the ink could not have been made until the 1800s. Therefore the text must have been written later, onto a piece of wood that had been cut earlier.

passage.text: Rats raised in an enriched environment with toys and companions develop more synapses in the brain and learn mazes more quickly than rats raised in bare cages. The enriched rats also received extra handling and exercise, which could by themselves affect learning. To determine whether the extra synapses were the crucial factor, researchers would need to compare the enriched rats with rats that were given ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: extra handling and exercise but no toys or companions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: no handling or exercise but the same toys and companions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: larger cages but no toys or companions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the same maze but different rewards.

explanation: The enriched rats differed from the bare-cage rats in both environmental stimulation and handling/exercise. To rule out handling and exercise as the true causes of the learning advantage, researchers would need a comparison group that received the extra handling and exercise but not the toys and companions.

passage.text: In the decades after a large city introduced compulsory education for all children through age twelve, the number of public libraries in the city grew rapidly. Some historians argue that compulsory education caused this growth. This argument would be strengthened if it were shown that ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: families of newly enrolled students rarely owned books before the compulsory education law.

choices.label: B
choices.text: many public libraries were built in small towns before the law as well.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the law was passed in response to petitions from librarians.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the number of school-age children remained constant during the period.

explanation: If newly enrolled students came from families that owned few books, then compulsory education would have created a demand for library books, directly supporting the claim that the education law fueled library growth.

passage.text: Every spring, students at Westfield High conduct a survey about cafeteria food. This year, the survey team asked every student who ate lunch during the first lunch period which main dish they preferred. The team found that pizza was preferred by more of those students than any other main dish. Therefore, ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Students in the first lunch period are the only students who prefer pizza.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The survey results may not reflect the preferences of students in other lunch periods.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cafeteria staff should serve pizza every day to all students.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Students in other lunch periods dislike all cafeteria main dishes.

explanation: Because the survey was limited to students in the first lunch period, the results cannot reliably be generalized to all students at the school.

passage.text: A single fern plant can release millions of tiny spores into the air. These spores can travel long distances on wind. For a new fern to grow, a spore must land where there is enough moisture, light, and space. Most spores drift into dry, shaded areas or onto bare rock, where they cannot develop. Therefore, ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most fern spores eventually grow into mature ferns.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ferns would grow better if they released fewer spores.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most fern spores fail to find conditions needed for growth.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bare rock is the best place for fern spores to land.

explanation: The passage says that most spores land where they cannot develop, so the supported inference is that most spores fail to grow into new ferns.

passage.text: Last month, the city of Brooksville opened a new public pool. The pool director recorded visitor totals for the first week and noticed that the numbers increased each day from Monday through Friday. The director knows that one week of data is not enough to show a long-term attendance trend. Therefore, ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The director should gather more attendance data before drawing conclusions about future pool use.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The director should predict next month's attendance exactly from the first week's totals.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The director should assume that attendance will increase forever.

passage.text: A small town library began lending e-readers that come preloaded with popular books. Within the first month, every e-reader was checked out at all times, and the waiting list for e-readers had more than twice as many names as the library had devices. Therefore, ______.

passage.text: While excavating a hillside, paleontologists found that fossils of a small plant-eating dinosaur appear in the lower rock layer. stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.text: The larger dinosaur evolved directly from the smaller dinosaur.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The smaller dinosaur lived at the same time as the larger dinosaur.

choices.text: The larger dinosaur appeared in this region after the smaller species had lived there.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The smaller dinosaur appeared later than the larger dinosaur.

passage.text: A town library currently opens at 9 a.m. on weekdays. In a survey, 80 out of 100 library-card holders said they would visit the library more often if it opened at 7 a.m. on weekdays. explanation: The survey directly supports opening at 7 a.m. on weekdays: 80% of cardholders said they would visit more often then. The other options are not supported by the survey or conflict with the goal of increasing visits by current cardholders.

passage.text: Researchers studied two neighboring populations of desert mice. The researchers found that in the rocky, predator-rich population, mice with longer tails tend to survive longer. No such pattern was found in the grassy population. This difference in survival suggests that in the rocky population, _______________.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: C
choices.text: grass cover prevents mice from jumping between rocks.

choices.label: D
choices.text: tail length has no effect on survival in either population.

explanation: The rocky population depends on jumping between rocks to escape predators, and longer-tailed mice survive better only there. This most strongly suggests that longer tails aid jumping-based escape. The other choices contradict or are unsupported by the passage.

passage.text: An art museum recently changed the wall labels next to its paintings. The old labels listed only the artist's name and the painting's title. In the six months after the change, the average time visitors spent looking at each painting increased by 45 seconds. The museum cannot be certain that the new labels caused the longer viewing time, because _______________.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

passage.text: A company introduced a new training program for sales staff in January. Comparing the twelve months before and after the program, the company's total sales increased by 12 percent. passage.text: In a small coastal town, residents were asked whether they would support a wind farm. Among residents who had visited the coast and seen the proposed area, 70% supported it. passage.text: A botanist performed a controlled experiment in a greenhouse. passage.text: A marine biologist recorded the locations of sea stars on a rocky beach for two months. passage.text: While restoring an old house, workers discovered a thick layer of ash and charred wood sandwiched between two wooden floors. Among the items on the lower floor was a coin minted in 1714. Among the items on the upper floor was a newspaper dated June 1760. Therefore, ____.

passage.text: In a desert canyon, paleontologists found a layer of rock containing many fossils of fish and seashells. The same layer contained ripple marks exactly like those formed by waves in shallow water. The canyon is now hundreds of kilometers from any ocean. Therefore, ____.

passage.text:
Text 1
Working from home is less productive than working in a shared office. In an office, employees benefit from immediate access to managers and spontaneous conversations that solve problems quickly. At home, the absence of direct oversight allows distractions—household chores, personal errands, or streaming services—to compete with professional responsibilities. Companies that move to remote work should therefore expect output to decline.
passage.text_b:
Text 2
Studies of remote workers have repeatedly found that they complete assigned tasks faster and report higher job satisfaction than their in-office peers. The key is not physical oversight but autonomy: employees who control their schedules and work environments tend to take greater ownership of their work. What appears to be a lack of supervision is actually a more trusting relationship that motivates people to meet or exceed expectations.

stem: Which of the following best describes how the author of Text 2 would respond to the assertion in Text 1 that remote employees need direct supervision to remain productive?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Agree that remote workers face distractions, but propose stricter digital monitoring.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Concede that some employees cannot work without oversight, but insist that most can.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deny that direct supervision is necessary, arguing that autonomy itself improves motivation and performance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Claim that the real problem is not supervision but the types of tasks being assigned.

explanation: Text 2 directly counters Text 1's emphasis on oversight, stating that the key is autonomy and that remote workers often perform better when trusted. The author would therefore deny that supervision is necessary and point to autonomy as the source of improved motivation and output.

passage.text:
Text 1
Urban planners should treat community gardens as a primary food-security strategy. Vacant lots can be converted into vegetable plots that provide fresh produce to nearby residents, lower grocery costs, and strengthen social ties. Unlike remote distribution systems, these gardens put food decisions in the hands of neighborhoods and ensure that the most vulnerable communities have immediate access to healthy food.
passage.text_b:
Text 2
Community gardens are valuable for education and recreation, but they are not a serious food-security solution. Research on urban agriculture shows that typical plots produce only a few hundred pounds of vegetables per season—far less than what a neighborhood needs. Vertical farms, which use stacked growing trays in controlled environments, can generate high yields on small footprints and operate year-round, making them a more reliable way to feed cities.

stem: Based on the passages, the author of Text 2 would most likely criticize the proposal in Text 1 by arguing that community gardens

choices.label: B

choices.label: C
choices.text: are too expensive to maintain compared with vertical farms.

choices.label: D
choices.text: undermine social ties by making neighborhoods depend on outside organizations.

explanation: Text 2 claims that typical community gardens yield far less food than a neighborhood needs and argues that vertical farms are more reliable for urban food production. The author would therefore reject Text 1's proposal on the grounds that community gardens cannot produce enough to meaningfully address food insecurity.

passage.text:
Text 1
Standardized tests, for all their limitations, give colleges a common yardstick. High school grades vary widely from school to school, while a well-designed test measures the same skills under the same conditions for every student. If admissions decisions have to be made fairly among applicants from different backgrounds, a standardized score is one of the most defensible pieces of evidence available.
passage.text_b:
Text 2
The apparent fairness of standardized tests is an illusion. Performance on these tests is strongly correlated with family income and access to test preparation, and it predicts college success no better than high school grades do. Requiring test scores therefore penalizes students who lack resources, while adding little information about their readiness for college work.

stem: Which of the following is the most likely response by the author of Text 1 to Text 2's claim that standardized tests add little predictive information beyond high school grades?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The claim must be false because standardized tests are designed to be objective.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If that were true, colleges should rely primarily on grades rather than test scores.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The proper solution is to make tests optional for students from low-income families.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Even if tests add little predictive value, they still provide a common standard for comparing students from different schools.

explanation: Text 1 values standardized tests mainly because they provide a consistent basis for comparing applicants, since high school grades vary by school. The author would therefore argue that even if tests do not add predictive power, their role as a common yardstick remains important.

passage.text:
Text 1
Electric vehicles are the most practical route to reducing transportation emissions. Although producing lithium-ion batteries requires mining and manufacturing, recycling programs are improving rapidly. Spent batteries can be processed to recover lithium, cobalt, and nickel, reducing the need for new mining. With a robust recycling system, the lifetime environmental cost of electric vehicles will continue to fall.
passage.text_b:
Text 2
Electric vehicles still depend on huge batteries that require rare minerals and long charging times. Hydrogen fuel-cell vehicles offer a better alternative: they refuel in minutes, travel comparable distances, and use fuel cells whose main byproduct is water. The real obstacle to a zero-emission transportation system is not battery chemistry but the decision to invest in hydrogen production and refueling infrastructure.

stem: The author of Text 2 would most likely respond to Text 1's claim about battery recycling by arguing that

choices.label: A
choices.text: battery recycling is too expensive to be implemented on a wide scale.

choices.label: B

choices.label: C
choices.text: hydrogen production also requires mining, so it does not solve the environmental problem.

choices.label: D
choices.text: recycling programs should be combined with hydrogen production to create a hybrid system.

explanation: Text 2 argues that the fundamental problem with electric vehicles is their large batteries, rare minerals, and slow charging, and it presents hydrogen fuel-cell vehicles as the better alternative. The author would respond that recycling batteries does not address these underlying drawbacks.

passage.text:
Text 1
Moving school start times to 8:30 a.m. or later is one of the most effective changes a district can make for teenagers. Research shows that adolescents need about nine hours of sleep and that their natural sleep cycles shift later. When schools delay start times, students get more sleep, report less daytime sleepiness, and earn higher test scores. Districts should therefore adopt later start times even if it means rearranging bus schedules.
passage.text_b:
Text 2
The enthusiasm for later school start times ignores the real costs to communities. Many students rely on after-school jobs, sports, and family obligations; a later dismissal pushes these activities into the evening and reduces time for homework. Moreover, the apparent academic benefits fade when researchers control for family income and homework load. A better approach is to address the actual sources of sleep loss, such as excessive homework and screen time, rather than move the school day.

stem: Which of the following best describes how the author of Text 2 would respond to Text 1's claim that later start times improve test scores?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The test-score gains are genuine but too small to justify the costs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The claim is credible, but districts should also limit after-school jobs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The evidence is misleading because factors other than start time likely explain the improvement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Districts should first study whether students actually get nine hours of sleep.

explanation: Text 2 says the academic benefits 'fade when researchers control for family income and homework load,' suggesting that the test-score gains linked to later starts may be due to other factors. The author would therefore see Text 1's evidence as misleading rather than conclusive.

passage.text: Text 1: Community gardens should be judged primarily by their measurable economic impact. Gardeners consistently report that the most important outcome is not the vegetables but the relationships formed across generations and backgrounds. These spaces reduce isolation and create a shared sense of purpose that cannot be captured in an economic analysis. A garden that produces little food but brings a neighborhood together is still a success.

stem: The author of Text 2 would most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 that community gardens should be supported for their economic benefits by stating that

choices.label: B

passage.text: Text 1: Remote work has been a productivity boon. In a 2022 survey, 63% of managers reported that their teams were at least as productive working from home as in the office. passage.text_b: Text 2: Productivity statistics from the early remote-work period are not the whole picture. While individual focus may rise, collaborative projects often suffer because spontaneous conversations and informal mentoring disappear. A team can appear efficient in the short term while gradually losing the shared knowledge that drives innovation. Companies that treat remote work as an unqualified success may be trading today's output for tomorrow's creativity.

stem: Based on the texts, the author of Text 2 would most likely respond to the survey results cited in Text 1 by arguing that

choices.label: A
choices.text: they show only short-term individual productivity and do not account for harm to collaboration and innovation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: they are fabricated and should be ignored entirely.

choices.label: C
choices.text: they prove that remote work is beneficial for all teams in all circumstances.

choices.label: D

passage.text: Text 1: A live concert is a unique event: a performer takes risks, responds to the audience, and creates music in the moment. A recording, by contrast, can be spliced together from dozens of takes and digitally corrected. Audiences of recordings therefore hear an artificial product, not an authentic artistic expression. True music lovers should seek out live performances whenever possible.
passage.text_b: Text 2: Recordings are not a poor substitute for live music; they are a different kind of artistic achievement. A recording can preserve a particular interpretation indefinitely, letting listeners study details they would miss in a single hearing. Moreover, recordings make great performances available to people who cannot travel to concert halls. If an interpretation moves a listener, its authenticity does not depend on whether it was produced in one unedited take.

stem: The author of Text 2 would most likely respond to Text 1's claim that recordings are “an artificial product” by saying that

choices.label: A
choices.text: recordings are indeed artificial, but they are still useful for education.

choices.label: B
choices.text: the artistic value of a recording comes from the interpretation it preserves, not from whether it is a single live take.

choices.label: C
choices.text: live performances should be recorded and sold to help audiences appreciate them.

passage.text: Text 1: Daily homework is essential for academic achievement. passage.text: Text 1: Widespread adoption of electric vehicles could overwhelm the electrical grid. Charging a single EV can draw as much power as a typical home. choices.label: A

choices.text: evening charging is actually better for the grid than daytime charging.

passage.text: Rooftop gardens are often celebrated, but they are a poor use of urban resources. The costs of reinforcing rooftops, installing irrigation, and hiring gardeners are steep. Studies show that a typical rooftop garden lowers a building's energy use by only a small fraction, while the same money spent on improving building insulation would save far more energy. Cities should therefore stop subsidizing rooftop gardens and invest in proven efficiency measures instead.
passage.text_b: Energy savings alone are the wrong yardstick for rooftop gardens. In densely built neighborhoods, these gardens provide rare habitat for pollinators and birds, absorb stormwater, and give residents access to green space linked to lower stress. A garden does not have to outperform insulation on every metric to be worthwhile; it serves public health and ecological goals that insulation cannot. Funding decisions should weigh these benefits alongside energy costs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Argue that rooftop gardens are actually cheaper to install than building insulation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Contend that Text 1 overlooks other valuable benefits that cannot be captured by energy savings.

passage.text: Reading well means reading slowly. When we hurry through a novel or an essay, we miss the connotations of particular words, the rhythms of sentences, and the way arguments qualify one another. Speed-reading apps train people to skim, but skimming is not reading; it is scanning. The deepest understanding and the most lasting pleasure come from giving a text the time it demands.
passage.text_b: In a world of overwhelming information, the ability to read quickly is a practical necessity, not a defect. A lawyer scanning a contract for a key clause or a doctor reviewing the latest research does not need the aesthetic experience of a novel. Efficient readers extract the relevant facts, make a decision, and move on. Treating slow, immersive reading as the only true reading ignores the many purposes reading serves.

stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Text 1's assertion that skimming is “not reading”?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Agree that skimming has no value in professional contexts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Argue that all reading should be equally slow and careful.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Insist that speed-reading is superior for appreciating literary style.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Maintain that rapid extraction of information is a legitimate form of reading suited to certain goals.

passage.text: Remote work has proven its worth. Multiple companies have reported that employees working from home complete assignments faster and take fewer sick days. Freed from long commutes, workers say they are less exhausted and more focused. If the goal is measurable output, remote work is at least as productive as office work, and sometimes more so.
passage.text_b: Measurable output misses what happens when people share physical space. Innovation often emerges from unplanned conversations at the coffee machine, overheard problem-solving, and casual mentoring that cannot be scheduled over video calls. A team may check off tasks efficiently from home, but over time that efficiency can come at the cost of the spontaneous exchanges that generate breakthroughs. The long-term health of an organization depends on more than today's output numbers.

choices.text: Such gains may be real, but they are not a substitute for the unplanned interactions that drive future innovation.

choices.label: B

passage.text: Public libraries should become digital-first institutions. Unlike a website, a physical branch can connect neighbors to social services, children's literacy programs, and community meetings. Shrinking physical space to expand digital offerings would hurt the very people libraries exist to serve.
