Then an experimenter wearing a distinctive white lab coat trapped several crows, fitted them with small identification bands, and released them. From then on, when anyone wore a white lab coat, the crows avoided the lot; when people wore other clothing, the crows continued to visit. This change in behavior suggests that the crows ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Could recognize individual humans only when those humans were wearing lab coats.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Avoided the parking lot because they had learned to fear all humans.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Had learned to associate white lab coats with the danger of being captured.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stopped visiting the lot because food scraps were no longer available.

explanation: The crows avoided the lot only when someone wore a white lab coat, the same clothing worn during trapping. This strongly implies that they came to associate white lab coats with danger.

passage.text: At the ancient city of Ulmara, archaeologists found clay pits and kilns with fragments of pottery decorated with a serpent pattern. At Tamir, a distant trading post, they unearthed similar serpent-decorated pottery. No local clay sources suitable for pottery are known near Tamir, and chemical tests show the Tamir pottery's clay matches the Ulmara clay. Therefore, the serpent-decorated pottery from Tamir was most likely ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Made in Ulmara and transported to Tamir through trade.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Made independently at Tamir from a different kind of clay.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Brought to Ulmara from Tamir by traders.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Older than any pottery found in Ulmara.

explanation: Since Tamir had no suitable local clay and the Tamir pottery's clay matches Ulmara clay, the pottery was almost certainly made in Ulmara and carried to Tamir, probably through trade.

passage.text: On a small island, a deadly virus killed a large percentage of the island's rabbits in a single winter. The island's foxes depend on rabbits for almost all of their food and have no other abundant prey. Over the following months, the fox population dropped sharply. The next spring, the surviving rabbits began breeding, and within two years the rabbit population had returned to its former size. The rapid recovery of the rabbits was probably aided by __________.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the virus also immunizing the foxes against the rabbit disease

choices.label: B
choices.text: a sudden increase in the number of rabbits born during the first winter

choices.label: C
choices.text: an unusually large supply of food brought to the island for the rabbits

choices.label: D
choices.text: reduced hunting pressure while the fox population was low

explanation: Since foxes depend on rabbits and their population declined sharply, the recovering rabbits would have faced fewer predators, making reduced hunting pressure the most directly supported explanation.

passage.text: At one archaeological site, a single habitation layer dated to approximately 1200 BCE contains both plain gray pottery and red-slipped decorated pottery. Across the region, layers that contain only plain gray pottery are consistently older than layers that contain red-slipped pottery, and red-slipped pottery is never found in layers below plain gray pottery. This site therefore indicates that __________.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: red-slipped pottery was invented before plain gray pottery

choices.label: B
choices.text: red-slipped pottery was introduced at a time when plain gray pottery was still in use

choices.label: C
choices.text: plain gray pottery disappeared as soon as red-slipped pottery appeared

choices.label: D
choices.text: the plain gray pottery in the layer was made after the red-slipped pottery

explanation: The region-wide pattern shows red-slipped pottery appearing after plain pottery, and the 1200 BCE layer contains both types, so the most supported conclusion is that red-slipped pottery was introduced while plain pottery continued to be used.

passage.text: In a learning experiment, volunteers studied a list of forty unrelated word pairs. All volunteers could recall every pair immediately after studying. Half were then allowed to sleep for eight hours; the other half remained awake in the lab and played computer games during those eight hours. The next morning, the sleep group recalled significantly more word pairs than the no-sleep group. Neither group had been allowed to look at the word pairs during the interval. This outcome most strongly suggests that __________.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: playing computer games worsens memory even without new learning

choices.label: B
choices.text: sleep after learning helps to preserve newly formed memories

choices.label: C
choices.text: people remember best when they study immediately before bedtime

choices.label: D
choices.text: memory of word pairs depends entirely on how well they were learned initially

explanation: Both groups began with perfect recall and neither reviewed the list, but the sleep group later recalled more, so the difference is best explained by sleep helping preserve the newly formed memories.

passage.text: From 2015 to 2018, the number of ride-sharing trips in a major city nearly tripled. Many transit planners had expected subway ridership to drop, yet subway ridership rose by more than 10 percent over the same period. In a survey, a majority of subway passengers who used ride-sharing services said they used them to get to or from a subway station; before ride-sharing became common, these same passengers had often driven alone for the entire trip. The rise in subway ridership was therefore probably due in part to __________.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ride-sharing increasing access to subway stations

choices.label: B
choices.text: the construction of several new subway stations

choices.label: C
choices.text: subway riders abandoning buses in favor of trains

choices.label: D
choices.text: a decline in the cost of subway fares

explanation: The survey shows that ride-sharing passengers often used it to reach subway stations, and they previously drove alone for the whole trip, so ride-sharing plausibly helped increase subway ridership.

passage.text: Astronomers detected a large quantity of oxygen gas in the atmosphere of a rocky planet orbiting a nearby star. On Earth, oxygen gas is chemically reactive and is constantly replenished by living organisms; in the absence of such replenishment, it would quickly combine with rocks and disappear from the atmosphere. Although nonbiological chemical processes can also release oxygen, any plausible explanation for the planet's oxygen must involve __________.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: direct confirmation that photosynthetic organisms live there

choices.label: B
choices.text: an ongoing process that continually produces oxygen

choices.label: C
choices.text: the presence of large rocks that trap oxygen on the surface

choices.label: D
choices.text: a process that occurred only when the planet formed

explanation: Because oxygen gas would rapidly disappear unless it is continually replenished, detecting it requires an ongoing source, whether biological or nonbiological.

passage.text: The staff at a public library were surprised when monthly e-book checkouts rose sharply. Just before the increase, the library had installed touch-screen kiosks that allow visitors to search the catalog and place holds on e-books. During the six months after the installation, e-book checkouts increased by 45 percent, while the number of library visitors increased by only 3 percent and the library made no other changes to its online services.

stem: Which conclusion is most strongly supported by the information in the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The new kiosks were the sole reason for the increase in e-book checkouts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The increase in e-book checkouts was probably at least partly caused by the new kiosks.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Visitors used the kiosks more often than they used the library's online catalog.

choices.label: D
choices.text: E-book checkouts increased because the library reduced its print collection.

explanation: The installation of the kiosks is the only major change noted, and the increase in e-book checkouts coincided with it. The visitor increase was small, so the jump in checkouts was likely related to the kiosks, but the evidence does not justify claiming they were the sole cause.

passage.text: In a study, volunteers learned a list of word pairs and were then randomly assigned to either take a 90-minute nap or stay awake. Four hours later, both groups took a memory test. The napping group recalled significantly more word pairs than the awake group. Actigraphy monitors showed that the two groups did not differ in the amount of sleep they had obtained the previous night.

stem: Which conclusion is most strongly supported by the information in the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Taking a nap is always more beneficial than staying awake.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Staying awake for four hours causes permanent memory loss.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sleeping after learning can help strengthen memories.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only people who nap can remember word pairs.

explanation: The study found that the group that napped after learning performed better on the memory test, and prior sleep was controlled. This supports the conclusion that sleep after learning can aid memory, but it does not show that napping is always beneficial or that staying awake always causes memory loss.

passage.text: A botanist grew the same variety of tomato plants in two identical greenhouses. The plants in Greenhouse A received a standard synthetic fertilizer, while the plants in Greenhouse B received a new organic compost. All other conditions, including water, temperature, and light, were the same. After eight weeks, the tomato plants in Greenhouse B were 30 percent taller on average than those in Greenhouse A. A soil analysis revealed that the compost released higher levels of nitrogen into the soil than the synthetic fertilizer did.

stem: Which conclusion is most strongly supported by the information in the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The organic compost may have contributed to the greater height of the plants in Greenhouse B.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Organic compost is always better than synthetic fertilizer for growing tomatoes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The plants in Greenhouse A were shorter mainly because of a lack of light.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nitrogen is harmful to tomato plants.

explanation: The compost was associated with greater plant height and higher nitrogen levels, while other conditions were controlled. This supports a likely causal contribution, but not the claim that organic compost is always better or that nitrogen is harmful.

passage.text: Paleontologists discovered fossilized bones of a small dinosaur species in a rock layer dated to 70 million years ago. In a layer dated to 65 million years ago, they found fossilized footprints of a different dinosaur species. Extensive sampling of the older layer, along with older layers, has produced no trace of this second species.

stem: Which conclusion is most strongly supported by the information in the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The second species evolved directly from the first species.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The second species lived in the area at the same time as the first species.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The first species died out before the second species arrived.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The second species probably did not live in the area 70 million years ago.

explanation: The second species appears only in the younger layer, and extensive sampling of the older layer found no trace of it. This strongly supports the conclusion that the second species was absent from the area 70 million years ago, without justifying claims about evolution or the extinction of the first species.

passage.text: A homeowner compared her solar panels' electricity production for March and August. The panels produced more electricity in March, despite August having longer days and more direct sunlight. The homeowner knows that solar panels become less efficient as their temperature increases. Average daytime temperatures in the area were 20°C in March and 32°C in August.

stem: Which conclusion is most strongly supported by the information in the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Solar panels should not be used in hot climates.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The higher August temperatures may account for the lower August production.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sunlight is not the main factor in solar panel output.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The panels were defective in August.

explanation: August had more sunlight yet produced less electricity, and the homeowner knows high temperatures reduce panel efficiency. This makes the higher temperatures a likely factor, though other explanations are not completely ruled out. The passage does not support broad claims about hot climates or defects.

passage.text: In a controlled experiment, two groups of volunteers were taught the same set of twenty unfamiliar words. One group studied the words for twenty minutes immediately before going to sleep; the other group studied the words for twenty minutes immediately after waking. Both groups were then tested seven hours after waking, and the group that had studied before bed recalled on average 65 percent of the words, whereas the group that had studied after waking recalled on average 48 percent. Because the two groups experienced identical conditions apart from the placement of the study session, the researchers concluded that __________.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: sleep soon after initial learning can benefit later recall

choices.label: B
choices.text: studying vocabulary in the morning is generally ineffective

choices.label: C
choices.text: sleep is the only factor that determines how well new words are remembered

choices.label: D
choices.text: people who learn words at night concentrate better than people who learn words in the morning

explanation: The before-bed group slept soon after studying and had better recall. This directly supports the conclusion that sleep soon after learning can benefit later recall. The other choices are either contradicted by the passage, too absolute, or unsupported.

passage.text: Researchers studying color preferences in toddlers placed identical blue and yellow containers of the same plain yogurt in front of each child. The children were allowed to taste the yogurt from both containers during a brief practice session, and then they were asked to choose which container they wanted more yogurt from. On repeated trials, 78 percent of the children chose the blue container. Because the only difference between the two options was the color of the container, the researchers can most reasonably conclude that __________.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the toddlers preferred the yellow container because of its taste

choices.label: B
choices.text: the color of the container influenced the children's choices

choices.label: C
choices.text: all toddlers will choose a blue container over a yellow container

choices.label: D
choices.text: the blue yogurt was sweeter than the yellow yogurt

explanation: Since the yogurt was identical and the only difference was container color, the majority preference for blue shows that color influenced choices. The other choices claim differences in taste, absolute behavior, or contradicted outcomes.

passage.text: Biologists studying a species of tree frog noticed that individuals living near busy highways produce calls with a higher average pitch than frogs living in quiet forests. The two frog populations are genetically similar and eat the same kinds of insects. Recordings of highway noise show that the low-frequency rumble of traffic overlaps with the lower-pitched parts of the tree frog call. The biologists concluded that __________.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: traffic noise has caused forest-dwelling tree frogs to move closer to highways

choices.label: B
choices.text: lower-pitched calls are completely inaudible in the presence of traffic noise

choices.label: C
choices.text: tree frogs living near highways may have adjusted their calls to be heard over traffic noise

choices.label: D
choices.text: tree frogs in quiet forests should raise the pitch of their calls to avoid predators

explanation: The frogs near highways call at a higher pitch, and traffic noise overlaps the lower-pitched parts of the call. This supports the conclusion that highway frogs may have adjusted their calls to be heard over noise. The other choices make unsupported claims about movement, absolute inaudibility, or predator avoidance.

passage.text: An education researcher compared two similar elementary schools over one school year. At Eastwood School, all teachers received training in a new method of reading instruction and used that method in their classrooms. At Westbrook School, teachers used the district's standard reading curriculum. At the end of the year, students at Eastwood showed a significantly greater average improvement on the same standardized reading test than students at Westbrook did. Because the two schools had comparable class sizes, funding levels, and student demographics, the researcher concluded that __________.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: students at Eastwood School studied harder than students at Westbrook School

choices.label: B
choices.text: the standard reading curriculum harms students' reading development

choices.label: C
choices.text: the new method of reading instruction should be adopted by every school in the country

choices.label: D
choices.text: the new method of reading instruction was responsible for the difference in reading improvement

explanation: The two schools were comparable, and the only stated difference was the reading method. Thus, the most reasonable conclusion is that the new method was responsible for the greater improvement. The other choices rely on unsupported assumptions or overgeneralize too broadly.

passage.text: Archaeologists excavating beneath a later settlement in southern Italy found a layer of volcanic ash. Within this ash layer, they discovered fragments of pottery decorated with a distinctive spiral pattern. In a nearby region, the same spiral pattern has been found in deposits dating from the same period but in no earlier deposits. This pattern of evidence most strongly supports the conclusion that __________.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the spiral pattern originated in southern Italy and was later carried to the nearby region

choices.label: B
choices.text: the spiral-decorated pottery was in use in the region at the time of the volcanic eruption

choices.label: C
choices.text: the same potters made the spiral-decorated pottery found in both regions

choices.label: D
choices.text: the volcanic eruption buried all earlier pottery in the nearby region

explanation: Finding the spiral-patterned pottery in the ash layer and in deposits of the same age shows that this pottery was in use during that period. The other choices claim origins, shared makers, or burial of all earlier pottery, none of which is supported by the evidence.

passage.text: Researchers studied two adjacent forest plots with identical soil and rainfall. In Plot A, they removed all large herbivores; in Plot B, large herbivores remained. After five years, Plot A contained 40% more young trees of a rare species than Plot B. Because the two plots differed only in the presence of large herbivores, the researchers concluded that _______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the presence of large herbivores reduced the establishment of young trees of the rare species

choices.label: B
choices.text: removing large herbivores increased the number of every tree species in Plot A

choices.label: C
choices.text: the rare tree species requires soil and rainfall conditions found only in Plot A

choices.label: D
choices.text: large herbivores prefer to eat the rare tree species over all other plants

explanation: Because the plots had identical soil and rainfall and differed only in the presence of large herbivores, the most directly supported conclusion is that herbivores reduced establishment of the rare species. The other choices either overstate the findings or introduce unsupported claims.

passage.text: In a controlled experiment, caterpillars of the same species were raised on two artificial diets that were identical except for one ingredient: Diet X contained a chemical naturally found in the caterpillars' usual host plant, and Diet Y did not. Over the full larval period, caterpillars fed Diet X gained more mass and had higher survival rates than caterpillars fed Diet Y. From these results, the researchers concluded that _______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: caterpillars cannot survive unless their diet contains the chemical

choices.label: B
choices.text: Diet Y lacked several nutrients essential to caterpillar growth

choices.label: C
choices.text: the host plant chemical improves caterpillar growth or survival

choices.label: D
choices.text: caterpillars prefer the host plant to any artificial diet

explanation: Since the diets were identical except for the chemical, the observed difference in growth and survival is best attributed to that chemical. Choice A is too strong, B contradicts the design, and D is about preference, which was not tested.

passage.text: City planners compared summer temperature records for two neighborhoods with similar population density, building height, and amount of paved surface. Neighborhood A has 25% tree-canopy coverage and averaged 1.5 degrees Celsius cooler than Neighborhood B, which has 5% tree-canopy coverage. Since the neighborhoods were similar in the other measured factors, the planners concluded that _______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the lack of trees in Neighborhood B was entirely responsible for its higher temperatures

choices.label: B
choices.text: the greater tree canopy in Neighborhood A probably contributed to its lower average temperature

choices.label: C
choices.text: paved surfaces increase urban temperatures more than buildings do

choices.label: D
choices.text: adding trees to Neighborhood B would immediately lower its temperature by 1.5 degrees Celsius

explanation: The neighborhoods were similar in other measured factors, so the observed temperature difference is most directly explained by the difference in tree canopy. Choice A overstates certainty, and C and D introduce unsupported numerical or comparative claims.

passage.text: A newly described fossil from 150-million-year-old rock has a skull and wing structure resembling those of early birds, but it also has a long bony tail and clawed fingers characteristic of earlier nonbird dinosaurs. Paleontologists point out that this particular combination of features was previously unknown. They conclude that _______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: this fossil is the direct ancestor of all modern birds

choices.label: B
choices.text: the animal could fly only short distances

choices.label: C
choices.text: this fossil blurs the line between nonbird dinosaurs and early birds

choices.label: D
choices.text: feathers first evolved in animals of this species

explanation: The fossil combines features associated with two groups, so the most directly supported conclusion is that it makes the distinction less clear. The other choices make unsupported evolutionary or behavioral claims.

passage.text: Archaeologists compared trace-element signatures in ancient glass beads from three coastal sites. Beads from Site A and Site B had nearly identical signatures, while beads from Site C had a clearly different signature. Because the signature of a glass artifact reflects the source of the raw materials used to make it, the archaeologists concluded that _______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the beads from Site A and Site B were probably made from the same raw-material source

choices.label: B
choices.text: the beads from Site A were made in the same workshop as the beads from Site C

choices.label: C
choices.text: the beads from Site C are older than those from Sites A and B

choices.label: D
choices.text: the beads from Site A and Site B were made by different artisans

explanation: Because the signature reflects the raw-material source, the nearly identical signatures of beads from Sites A and B support a common raw-material source. The other choices involve claims about workshops, age, or artisans that the evidence does not directly support.

passage.text: In 2019, the city of Greenville introduced a voluntary curbside composting program. During the first year, only 18 percent of eligible households signed up. In 2021, the program became mandatory, and participation rose to 91 percent. Around the same time, a citywide survey found that 86 percent of residents reported composting regularly, while only 15 percent had reported doing so before the mandate.

stem: Which conclusion is most strongly supported by the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Requiring curbside composting was accompanied by a large increase in residents' reported composting.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The composting program was successful mainly because it educated residents about environmental benefits.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mandatory recycling programs are more successful than voluntary programs in every small city.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most residents of Greenville would prefer to get rid of their compostable waste in another way.

explanation: The passage reports that participation rose from 18% to 91% and that the percentage of residents reporting regular composting jumped from 15% to 86%. That directly supports the conclusion that the mandate was accompanied by a large increase in reported composting.

passage.text: Researchers compared fish species from two ocean environments. In well-lit surface waters, more than half of the species have large eyes, which help them detect predators and prey. In the permanently dark zone a kilometer below, fewer than 5 percent of species have large eyes; instead, the majority have specialized touch receptors and produce their own light.

stem: Which conclusion is most logically supported by the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The vast majority of fish living below one kilometer have no eyes at all.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Many fish in the dark ocean have adaptations suited to a world without sunlight.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fish in sunlit surface waters could survive equally well in the permanently dark zone.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only fish with large eyes are able to live in well-lit surface waters.

explanation: The passage shows that deep-water fish tend to lack large eyes and instead use touch receptors and bioluminescence. This supports the conclusion that they have adaptations suited to a lightless environment.

passage.text: Researchers asked volunteers to memorize a list of unfamiliar word pairs. Half the volunteers then slept for eight hours; the other half stayed awake. When tested after the eight-hour delay, the sleeping group remembered significantly more word pairs. In a second experiment, some volunteers heard a soft sound during sleep that had been played while they learned the material. Those volunteers recalled even more word pairs than sleepers who heard no sound.

stem: Which conclusion is most logically supported by the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Playing sounds while learning improves memory more than sleeping does.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sleep is necessary for any memory to be retained for eight hours.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sleep appears to help consolidate memories, and associated sensory cues during sleep can strengthen that process.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sounds heard during sleep weaken memories when those sounds were not present during learning.

explanation: The first experiment shows better memory after sleep than after wakefulness, and the second shows even better recall when a sound associated with learning is played during sleep. Together these findings support the conclusion that sleep aids memory consolidation and that associated cues can enhance it.

passage.text: Biologists studying polar bears in the Arctic have found that the survival rate of cubs in a given region is closely related to how long the region's sea ice remains each spring. When sea ice breaks up earlier, fewer cubs survive their first year. Satellite data from the past four decades show that the average length of the spring sea-ice season in many Arctic areas has been decreasing.

stem: Which conclusion is most logically supported by the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Polar bear cubs can survive only when sea ice remains throughout the entire year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Earlier sea-ice breakup has had no effect on polar bear cub survival.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The decline in spring sea ice is likely to affect only adult polar bears, not cubs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The trend toward earlier sea-ice breakup likely poses a difficulty for the survival of polar bear cubs.

explanation: The passage says that earlier sea-ice breakup is linked to fewer cubs surviving their first year, and that spring sea-ice season has been getting shorter in many Arctic areas. Thus, the trend likely makes cub survival more difficult.

passage.text: On hot summer afternoons, the demand for electricity in one city is at its highest, mainly because of air conditioning. Most electric vehicle owners in the city plug in their cars when they arrive home from work, during those same late-afternoon and early-evening hours. In a city-run pilot program, owners were asked to delay charging until after 10 p.m. During the pilot, electricity consumed for vehicle charging between 4 and 9 p.m. dropped by almost half.

stem: Which conclusion is most logically supported by the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Encouraging owners to charge after peak hours could reduce late-afternoon strain on the city's electric system.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Residents who participate in off-peak charging use more electricity overall.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Air conditioning is the only cause of high electricity demand in the city.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Delaying charging will be impossible once more residents buy electric vehicles.

explanation: The passage indicates that peak electricity demand occurs on hot afternoons and that EV charging currently adds to demand then. The pilot cut charging demand during those hours by nearly half, so the results support the conclusion that encouraging later charging could reduce late-afternoon grid strain.

passage.text: Bioluminescence—the production of light by living organisms—has many different functions in the ocean. In some shallow-water fish, for example, flashing is a way for many individuals to coordinate spawning at the same time. Some researchers have assumed that deep-sea fish use bioluminescence in the same way. Yet deep-sea fish are generally solitary for most of the year, and they are often far too dispersed to coordinate a synchronized spawning event. Moreover, producing light requires a meaningful expenditure of energy. If bioluminescence in a solitary deep-sea fish were primarily a spawning signal, one would expect it to be produced mainly during the brief mating season. But many such fish produce flashes all year long. Therefore,

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: year-round flashing in solitary deep-sea fish is probably not solely a reproductive signal.

choices.label: B
choices.text: deep-sea fish have no need to conserve energy while producing light.

choices.label: C
choices.text: shallow-water fish that flash all year are also solitary.

choices.label: D
choices.text: bioluminescence is less common in shallow water than in deep water.

explanation: The passage says that if flashing were primarily a spawning signal, it would be produced mainly during the mating season, yet many solitary deep-sea fish produce flashes all year. This directly supports the conclusion that such flashing is not solely a reproductive signal.

passage.text: Historians studying a Mesopotamian archive have found daily barley ration lists. Among the hundreds of tablets that survive, the lists record crews of 15, 30, 45, and 60 workers—but never crews of 20 or 25. One historian has argued that this proves work crews in the city were always organized in multiples of 15. However, the archive is not fully complete: a separate administrative letter from the same room mentions a “ration list for 25 laborers” that must have once existed. Therefore,

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the surviving ration lists by themselves cannot show that all work crews were multiples of 15.

choices.label: B
choices.text: the administrative letter proves that the 25-laborer list was a forgery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: work crews in the city were usually organized in groups of 25.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the archive contains no genuine lists of 30 or 45 workers.

explanation: Because the archive is incomplete and a lost 25-worker list is mentioned, the absence of such a list among surviving tablets cannot be used as proof that crews were always multiples of 15.

passage.text: Geologists have long debated whether a circular depression in the desert is an eroded volcanic crater or the remains of a meteorite impact. The volcanic hypothesis seemed attractive because the depression is surrounded by layered rocks that look like lava flows. But impact craters also often contain a distinctive kind of breccia: angular rock fragments fused together by glass. When geologists drilled into the center of the depression, they recovered exactly that kind of breccia from beneath the surface. Therefore,

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the depression was probably formed by an impact rather than by volcanic activity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: the layered rocks around the depression were also formed by impact.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the presence of breccia rules out any volcanic activity in the area.

choices.label: D
choices.text: meteorite impacts never produce circular depressions.

explanation: The breccia recovered is described as a distinctive impact product, so finding it at the center of the depression is evidence that the depression was formed by an impact rather than by volcanic activity.

passage.text: In an earlier psychology study, participants who briefly held a warm coffee cup rated an unfamiliar person as having a warmer personality than did participants who held an iced coffee cup. Researchers concluded that physical warmth promotes social warmth. But later experimenters suspected that participants might have guessed the point of the earlier study and behaved accordingly. When they repeated the study with identical cups outside the participants’ view, the effect disappeared. Therefore,

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the original result may have been caused at least partly by participants’ expectations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: physical warmth never influences judgments of other people.

choices.label: C
choices.text: participants who can see a warm cup are more likely to be suspicious of researchers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the later study did not actually measure social warmth.

explanation: The effect disappeared when participants could not see whether the cup was warm or cold, suggesting that the earlier result may have depended on participants’ expectations rather than on physical warmth alone.

passage.text: To reduce downtown traffic, a city imposed a daily fee on vehicles entering the central business district. In the year the fee took effect, vehicle entries decreased by 20 percent and average driving speeds rose. City officials credited the fee for the improvement. But during that same year, a new subway line opened with several stops in the downtown area. Many commuters who normally drove may have switched to the subway. Therefore,

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the fee clearly had no effect on downtown traffic.

choices.label: B
choices.text: the subway was the only cause of the decrease in entries.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the improvement cannot be attributed to the fee alone.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the fee caused an increase in subway ridership.

explanation: Since the new subway line opened at the same time and could have drawn former drivers away, the improvement cannot be credited solely to the fee; the subway provides an alternative explanation.

passage.text: Some archaeologists have argued that the ancient stone spheres of Costa Rica were created simply as status symbols. Recent surveys, though, have found that at several sites the spheres are arranged in patterns that align with sunrise on the summer solstice. If these alignments are intentional, the spheres cannot have served merely as status symbols, because ________.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: status symbols are rarely displayed outdoors

choices.label: B
choices.text: constructing such alignments would have required deliberate planning beyond what a purely symbolic purpose would demand

choices.label: C
choices.text: the spheres are too heavy for a single person to move

choices.label: D
choices.text: no written records explain why the spheres were built

explanation: If the alignments are intentional, the spheres served an astronomical or calendrical function as well as any symbolic function; therefore they were not made merely as status symbols.

passage.text: In an experiment, mice that ran on wheels for two weeks showed less anxiety in behavioral tests than mice that did not exercise. A second group of mice also ran on wheels but was given a drug that blocks the formation of new memories; these mice showed the same reduction in anxiety. The drug did not affect the mice's amount of running. Because the second group of mice could not remember having exercised, the anxiety-reducing effect of exercise must be ________.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: caused by the drug rather than by exercise

choices.label: C
choices.text: a result of the mice running less than the first group

choices.label: D
choices.text: produced by bodily processes that do not require memory

explanation: The second group ran normally and still showed reduced anxiety even though memory formation was blocked, so the effect cannot depend on remembering the exercise.

passage.text: A public library noticed that books shelved on the middle shelves were checked out far more often than books on the top or bottom shelves. When librarians randomly shifted the books to different shelves, the pattern disappeared. This outcome suggests that the original pattern was due not to the subjects of the books but to ________.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: changes in the library's opening hours

choices.label: B
choices.text: the number of copies the library owned

choices.label: C
choices.text: how easily the books could be seen and reached

explanation: Randomly shifting the books eliminated the pattern, showing that the original checkout pattern depended on shelf location, not on the content or subject of the books.

passage.text: In two similar forests, one with an established wolf population and one without, the forest with wolves had many more nesting songbirds. In the wolf-free forest, deer had eaten almost all of the low understory shrubs that these birds use for nesting. This comparison best supports the conclusion that wolves increased songbird numbers mainly by ________.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: reducing deer populations enough to allow the understory shrubs to recover

choices.label: B
choices.text: driving songbirds away from the wolf-free forest and into the wolf forest

choices.label: C
choices.text: adding nutrients to the soil through their droppings

choices.label: D
choices.text: keeping large carnivores away from the birds' nests

explanation: The key difference is heavy deer browsing in the forest without wolves; wolves most likely helped birds by limiting deer and allowing nesting shrubs to grow.

passage.text: Students who took a short walk before an exam scored higher, on average, than students who sat quietly before the exam. However, the walkers also reported higher confidence before the exam. Consequently, the difference in scores cannot be attributed solely to ________.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?
explanation: Because the walkers also differed in confidence, the observed score gap could have been caused by that difference rather than by the walking itself.

passage.text: On a small island, scientists studied a population of seed-eating birds over many years. During a severe drought, the supply of small, soft seeds dwindled, but larger, harder seeds remained available. Birds with larger, stronger beaks could crack the larger seeds more easily, so they survived and reproduced at higher rates than birds with smaller beaks. The next generation of birds had a noticeably larger average beak size than the generation before the drought. This change illustrates that

stem: Which statement most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: birds can deliberately change their beak shape when food becomes scarce.

choices.label: B
choices.text: natural selection can act on inherited variation in beak size when environmental conditions change.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the birds with the largest beaks always produce the most offspring, even when food is plentiful.

choices.label: D
choices.text: drought causes useful mutations that produce larger beaks in individual birds.

explanation: The passage says larger-beaked birds survived and reproduced at higher rates during the drought, and the next generation had a larger average beak size. This is a direct example of natural selection acting on inherited variation.

passage.text: Ancient Roman engineers made concrete by mixing volcanic ash with lime and seawater. This combination produced a rare mineral that helped the concrete grow stronger over time, even while submerged in seawater. Many Roman harbor structures made with this material are still standing after nearly two thousand years. Some modern concrete structures in seawater, by contrast, have required major repairs after just a few decades. This contrast suggests that

stem: Which statement most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Roman concrete was less susceptible to seawater damage than at least some modern concretes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: modern concrete is generally weaker than every type of concrete from the ancient world.

choices.label: C
choices.text: seawater gradually destroys all building materials.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Roman engineers were unable to make concrete for structures built on land.

explanation: The passage directly contrasts the durability of Roman harbor concrete with the need for repairs in some modern concrete marine structures. This supports the modest claim that Roman concrete was less susceptible to seawater damage than at least some modern concretes.

passage.text: In a memory experiment, participants studied a list of words. One group was allowed to take a ninety-minute nap immediately afterward, while the other group stayed awake watching a video. When tested the next day, the group that napped recalled significantly more words than the group that did not. Brain scans taken during the nap showed bursts of brain activity that matched the participants' earlier learning patterns, leading researchers to propose that the brain actively strengthens new memories during sleep. The findings support the hypothesis that

stem: Which statement most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: napping is the only way to improve memory.

choices.label: B
choices.text: watching a video after learning prevents memories from forming.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the brain's replay of newly learned patterns during sleep may contribute to better recall.

choices.label: D
choices.text: sleep has no effect on memory.

explanation: The passage reports both better recall after napping and matching replay activity during sleep. The most directly supported conclusion is that this replay may help strengthen memories.

passage.text: Researchers using satellite images found that over the past forty years, the area of Arctic sea ice at its summer minimum has shrunk sharply. During the same period, average Arctic temperatures have risen faster than the global average. Because bright sea ice reflects sunlight, its loss leaves more dark ocean exposed, and dark ocean absorbs more heat. These observations most directly support the conclusion that

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Arctic sea ice will continue to expand in future summers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: changes in Arctic temperatures are unrelated to changes in Arctic sea ice.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the loss of Arctic sea ice is caused mainly by increased shipping traffic.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the decline of Arctic sea ice is probably connected to rising Arctic temperatures.

explanation: The passage presents simultaneous trends in shrinking sea ice and rising temperatures and explains a mechanism linking them, so the most supported conclusion is that the decline of Arctic sea ice is probably connected to rising Arctic temperatures.

passage.text: Historians have often linked the invention of writing to the rise of complex government administration. However, the Inca Empire, which ruled millions of people across the Andes, used no known system of writing. Instead, officials used khipu, knotted and colored cords, to record census data, storehouse inventories, and tax obligations. These records were detailed enough to help administer a vast territory. Thus, the Inca example suggests that

stem: Which statement most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: administrative records cannot be accurate unless they are stored in written script.

choices.label: B
choices.text: complex societies can manage detailed recordkeeping without a written language.

choices.label: C
choices.text: khipu was a fully phonetic writing system.

choices.label: D
choices.text: only empires that use writing can collect taxes effectively.

explanation: The passage describes the Inca as a large, complex empire with detailed records but no known writing system. The best conclusion is that complex societies can maintain detailed recordkeeping without written language.

passage.text: In a dense city, rooftops made of dark waterproof materials absorb sunlight and become very hot. This heat radiates into streets and makes buildings warmer, so many residents rely on air conditioning during summer afternoons. Green roofs—covered with plants and a layer of soil—absorb less solar radiation, provide shade, and release moisture into the air, which has a cooling effect. In a simulation, covering all available downtown rooftops with green vegetation reduced predicted afternoon air temperatures by nearly 3°C.

stem: Which conclusion is most directly supported by the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Widespread installation of green roofs could reduce the need for air conditioning in downtown buildings.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Green roofs are effective only in cities with high pollution levels.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Conventional rooftops raise daytime temperatures but have no effect on buildings.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Air conditioning use is the main cause of high rooftop temperatures.

explanation: The passage says dark rooftops make buildings warmer and that green roofs have a cooling effect, so installing green roofs could reduce the need for air conditioning. The other choices either contradict the passage or introduce unsupported claims about climate, building effects, or causation.

passage.text: Scientists studying urban foxes attached GPS collars and tracked their movements. The foxes moved mainly at night, traveled farther in winter, and stayed close to railway lines. In areas with more parks, foxes traveled shorter distances, suggesting they found enough food close to their dens.

stem: Which conclusion is most logically supported by the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Urban foxes never hunt for food.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Foxes in winter travel less than they do in other seasons.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The availability of nearby food likely explains why foxes in park-rich areas traveled shorter distances.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Railway lines keep foxes from reaching parks.

explanation: The passage states that foxes in areas with more parks traveled shorter distances and that this suggested they found enough food close to their dens. Thus, nearby food availability most likely explains shorter travel distances. The other choices are contradicted by or unsupported by the passage.

passage.text: Some bats locate prey by echolocation, emitting high-frequency calls and listening to echoes. A moth that can hear those calls dives toward the ground when it detects them. Researchers found that bats in a region where such moths are common often fly more slowly and more quietly near potential prey than bats in other areas do. This quieter approach is thought to make it harder for the moths to hear the bats.

stem: Which conclusion is most logically supported by the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Moths that can hear echolocation calls are never captured by bats.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The bats' quieter approach is likely a way to hunt moths that are able to hear echolocation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bats that use echolocation cannot catch moths.

explanation: The passage explains that some moths can hear bat echolocation calls and that bats in areas with these moths fly more quietly, which is thought to reduce the moths' ability to hear them. This most directly supports the conclusion that the quiet approach is an adaptation for hunting such moths. The other choices are extreme or unsupported.

passage.text: A chemist measured the mass and volume of four liquids and found that some liquids contain particles that stay suspended and scatter light. Colloids have this property, while true solutions do not. In liquid P, a beam of light is clearly visible as it passes through the liquid, and particles settle only after being spun at very high speed. In liquid Q, a beam of light is not visible through the liquid, and particles do not settle even after high-speed spinning.

stem: Which conclusion is best supported by the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Liquid P is a true solution.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Liquid P has a greater mass than liquid Q.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Liquid P behaves like a colloid, while liquid Q behaves like a true solution.

explanation: Liquid P scatters a beam of light and contains particles that settle only under extreme force, which matches the passage's description of a colloid. Liquid Q does not scatter light and the particles do not settle, which matches a true solution. The other choices are contradicted or unsupported by the passage.

passage.text: A team of archaeologists found a workshop where glass and metal objects were once made. In one layer of ash, they uncovered broken molds, partly melted ingots, and fragments of finished objects. Tree-ring dates from timbers in a nearby well show that the workshop had been constructed by 1675. The last dated order recorded in the workshop's documents is from 1678, and the ash layer seems to be the result of a fire.

stem: Which conclusion is most logically supported by the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The workshop probably ceased operations sometime after 1678.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The workshop was deliberately destroyed by an earthquake.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The workshop produced only glass objects.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No workshops in the region were active before 1675.

explanation: The last dated order is from 1678, and the ash layer appears to be from a fire, so the passage most strongly supports the inference that the workshop stopped operating after 1678. The other choices introduce causes or claims about restricted production and regional history that are not supported by the passage.

passage.text: Urban planners in Aldergrove measured foot traffic in a commercial district before and after the opening of a new transit station. Before the station, weekend afternoons had the heaviest foot traffic. After the station opened, weekday evening traffic increased sharply and weekend afternoon traffic was unchanged. Surveys showed that nearly all of the new evening visitors arrived by train and lived outside the immediate neighborhood. Because the merchants’ goal is to benefit from the station’s presence, their promotion efforts should probably ____.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: focus on the weekday evening commuters attracted by the station

choices.label: B
choices.text: reduce weekday evening hours because weekend afternoons remain the busiest time

choices.label: C
choices.text: build a parking garage for customers who drive to the district

choices.label: D
choices.text: end weekend events because weekend traffic did not increase after the station opened

explanation: The new increase in traffic is specifically on weekday evenings and is made up of visitors arriving by train from outside the neighborhood. Since the merchants want to benefit from the station, the most directly supported conclusion is that they should target this new group of evening commuters.

passage.text: Scholars had assumed that an undated manuscript was copied in a single session by one scribe, since the handwriting looks identical from beginning to end. Chemical analysis of the ink, however, shows that the first half was written with an ink formula used in the early 1200s, while the second half was written with a formula not documented until the late 1200s. Therefore, the manuscript was most likely ____.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: written by one scribe in one continuous process

choices.label: B
choices.text: written at different times, though perhaps by the same scribe

choices.label: C
choices.text: written by two scribes working in the same room at the same time

choices.label: D
choices.text: written entirely in the late 1200s, with the first half added later

explanation: The ink formulas were used in periods about a century apart, so the two halves could not have been written in one continuous process. The evidence indicates different times, but identical handwriting does not rule out the same scribe working in two different periods, making B the best conclusion.

passage.text: Ecologists monitored two adjacent prairie fields for ten years. In Field A, they conducted a controlled burn every spring. Field B was left unburned. By the end of the study, Field A contained more native grass species than at the start, while Field B had fewer native grass species and many more woody shrubs. Since periodic fires are known to kill woody seedlings and create conditions that help native grasses germinate, this comparison most strongly supports the conclusion that ____.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: fire is the only factor capable of increasing plant species diversity

choices.label: B
choices.text: without annual fires, native grasses cannot survive in any prairie

choices.label: C
choices.text: periodic burning can help maintain native grasses by limiting woody shrubs

choices.label: D
choices.text: woody shrubs increase species diversity in the absence of fire

explanation: The burned field had more native grasses and fewer woody shrubs, while the unburned field had the opposite pattern. Combined with the known effects of fire, the comparison directly supports the conclusion that periodic burning helps maintain native grasses by limiting woody shrubs.

passage.text: An online news site tested two headline styles for the same set of articles. One style used emotionally charged words such as “shocking” and “incredible”; the other used plain, descriptive language. During the test, the emotional headlines drew twice as many clicks, but readers who clicked them stayed for an average of 40 seconds, whereas readers who clicked the plain headlines stayed for an average of two minutes. Since the site’s stated goal is to promote informed reading rather than merely attract clicks, these results suggest that ____.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the emotional headlines should be used exclusively

choices.label: B
choices.text: the plain headlines must have been read by more people overall

choices.label: C
choices.text: the higher click count of emotional headlines does not necessarily mean they better serve the site’s goal

choices.label: D
choices.text: time spent on a page is unrelated to how much readers understand

explanation: The site values informed reading, not just clicks. Since emotional headlines produced more clicks but much shorter reading times, their click advantage does not by itself show that they serve the site’s goal better.

passage.text: Small-business advisors compared two coffee shops in similar neighborhoods. Shop A introduced a mobile ordering app; Shop B did not. Over the next twelve months, Shop A’s total sales rose by 10%, while Shop B’s sales were flat. In a survey, three-quarters of Shop A’s customers who used the app said they visited the shop more often than they had before the app existed. Therefore, the sales increase at Shop A was most likely ____.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: caused by a general increase in coffee demand across the city

choices.label: B
choices.text: due at least in part to the mobile ordering app encouraging more visits

choices.label: C
choices.text: entirely the result of new customers who had never visited either shop before

choices.label: D
choices.text: smaller than the growth that would have occurred without the app

explanation: Shop A app users reported that they visited more often because of the app, and the comparison shop without an app had flat sales. This makes it most likely that the app contributed to the sales increase at Shop A.

passage.text: Researchers compared two wildlife preserves over three years using the same standard point-count methods. In the first preserve, which ran an active program to remove invasive predators, the number of breeding bird pairs fell from 240 to 190. In the second preserve, which had no predator-removal program and otherwise similar habitat and weather, the number rose from 225 to 250. The only known difference between the preserves was the predator-removal program. Therefore, the decline in the first preserve was most likely ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: an unintended harmful effect of the predator-removal program

choices.label: B
choices.text: caused by an unrelated bacterial infection that affected only the first preserve

choices.label: C
choices.text: a natural population cycle that the second preserve had already experienced

choices.label: D
choices.text: due to a change in the volunteers' bird-counting methods

explanation: Since the two preserves were identical in known ways except for the predator-removal program, the most logically supported conclusion is that the program caused the decline. The other choices introduce unsupported causes or contradict the information given.

passage.text: Archaeologists recovered a clay tablet from an undisturbed excavation unit. In the same soil layer were a coin bearing the portrait of a ruler known to have reigned from 430 to 450 CE and pieces of a pottery type that, according to independent dating, was produced only from 425 to 455 CE. No artifacts from other periods were present in the layer. Since the coin and pottery together date that layer, the tablet was most likely ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: made before the ruler took the throne

choices.label: B
choices.text: deposited while that ruler was governing the region

choices.label: C
choices.text: carried to the site by travelers after 455 CE

choices.label: D
choices.text: made from clay imported from another region

explanation: The coin dates from 430 to 450 CE and the pottery from 425 to 455 CE, so the only overlapping period is the ruler's reign. The undisturbed layer therefore most likely formed then, making it most logical that the tablet was deposited during that period.

passage.text: A 20-year study followed 1,500 adults. At the start, participants who reported eating at least five servings of vegetables per day were considerably less likely to develop heart disease than those who reported eating fewer vegetables. However, the high-vegetable group also had higher average incomes, were more likely to have health insurance, and exercised more regularly. Therefore, the lower rate of heart disease among the high-vegetable group ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: shows that eating vegetables causes good heart health

choices.label: B
choices.text: proves that income is the most important factor in heart disease

choices.label: C
choices.text: may be due to their overall healthier lifestyle, not to vegetables alone

choices.label: D
choices.text: was unrelated to their exercise habits

explanation: The high-vegetable group differed from the other group in several health-related ways, not just vegetable intake. Thus the most logical conclusion is that the lower heart-disease rate cannot be attributed solely to vegetables.

passage.text: In a controlled experiment, tomato plants were grown in two identical greenhouse sections. One section received a fertilizer containing added beneficial microbes; the other section received the same fertilizer without the added microbes. Water, light, temperature, and soil type were the same for both sections. After eight weeks, the plants in the microbe-treated section produced, on average, 18 percent more fruit by weight than the plants in the other section. Therefore, the higher fruit yield was most likely ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: too small to be considered a real effect

choices.label: B
choices.text: a consequence of the fertilizer itself

choices.label: C
choices.text: the result of differences in temperature between the sections

choices.label: D
choices.text: caused by the added microbes in the fertilizer

explanation: The only intentional difference between the two groups was the addition of microbes to the fertilizer, while all other conditions were controlled. The most logical inference is that the added microbes caused the observed increase in fruit yield.

passage.text: Linguists studying an ancient language noticed that the same root appears in words meaning 'grasp' in the oldest surviving texts and 'understand' in texts from several centuries later. In many languages around the world, words for physical actions regularly develop abstract meanings after the physical meaning is established. Since the later texts also use the root in a word meaning 'include,' the root's abstract uses probably ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: developed from the concrete sense of 'grasp'

choices.label: B
choices.text: existed in the oldest texts but were simply unrecorded

choices.label: C
choices.text: were borrowed from a neighboring language

choices.label: D
choices.text: caused the concrete meaning to disappear

explanation: The oldest texts show the concrete meaning 'grasp,' and later texts show abstract meanings. Given the pattern that concrete meanings regularly develop into abstract ones, the abstract uses most likely emerged from the concrete sense.

passage.text: In a 40-year study of a bird species on an isolated island, researchers recorded a steady increase in the average depth of the birds' beaks. Early in the study, a severe drought reduced the number of small, soft seeds, which were the food source most easily consumed by small-beaked birds. Large-seeded plants with tough, hard seeds became relatively common. Birds with deeper beaks were able to crack these hard seeds more efficiently than birds with shallower beaks. Therefore, the change in average beak depth was most likely driven by the fact that...

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Birds with deeper beaks had greater reproductive success because they could make use of the more abundant hard seeds.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The drought caused individual birds to develop deeper beaks during their lifetimes in response to eating hard seeds.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Birds with shallower beaks left the island in search of small seeds and never returned.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The hard seeds contained fewer nutrients, so birds needed larger beaks to consume enough of them.

explanation: The passage establishes that hard seeds became more common and that birds with deeper beaks could crack them more efficiently. Thus, deeper-beaked birds would be more likely to survive and reproduce, which best explains the observed increase in average beak depth.

passage.text: At an archaeological site, researchers excavated an undisturbed layer containing both cooking pots and storage jars. Milk-fat residue preserved on the cooking pots could be radiocarbon dated and was found to be about 6,000 years old. The storage jars had no such residue, so they could not be dated directly. Because the cooking pots and storage jars were found in the same undisturbed layer at the same depth, the most logical conclusion is that...

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The storage jars are certainly older than the cooking pots because they were not used for cooking.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The storage jars were probably manufactured in the last few hundred years and then buried in the ancient layer by later people.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The storage jars are likely to be about the same age as the cooking pots.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The age of the storage jars cannot be inferred at all because they lack organic material for radiocarbon dating.

explanation: Objects found in the same undisturbed archaeological layer are generally deposited at around the same time. Therefore, the storage jars, found alongside cooking pots dated to 6,000 years old, are likely to be about the same age.

passage.text: Astronomers monitoring a distant star observed a 1 percent dip in its brightness that lasted about four hours and recurred every 36 days. Over three years, the dip appeared hundreds of times with the same shape, duration, and depth. The star is similar in size to the Sun. Therefore, the periodic dimming is most likely caused by...

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Random explosions on the surface of the star.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Changing activity cycles in the star's atmosphere.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An unrelated star passing between Earth and this star.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A planet in a stable orbit passing in front of the star.

explanation: A highly regular, identically repeating dimming event at a fixed interval is the signature of an orbiting body transiting the star. The small, consistent 1 percent dip is consistent with a planet orbiting in front of the star.

passage.text: In an experiment, volunteers were shown a large jar of jelly beans and asked to estimate the number inside. choices.text: with encouragement of cycling through safer street design.

choices.label: D
choices.text: encourage cycling through safer street design.

explanation: The list follows the modal "can," so it should consist of bare infinitives: "expand," "impose," and "encourage." Only choice D uses the correct verb form.

passage.text: Rather than treating the archive as a static collection, the curator views it as a living resource that should be digitized, interpreted, and ___.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: B
choices.text: to make accessible to the public.

choices.label: C
choices.text: making it accessible to the public.

explanation: The list after "should be" contains past participles: "digitized," "interpreted," and "made accessible to the public." Only choice A maintains the parallel past-participle form.

passage.text: The park ranger urged the hikers to pack plenty of water, to carry a map of the trail, and ______ before setting out.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The sentence presents a list of infinitive phrases: to pack, to carry, and to check. Only the to-infinitive in choice B keeps the third item parallel to the first two.

passage.text: Under the new policy, the commission will evaluate each application, solicit public comment, and ______ its decision within thirty days.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The modal verb will governs the entire list: will evaluate, will solicit, and will announce. Choice A supplies the bare infinitive announce, matching the other two verbs.

passage.text: The coach advised her players to stretch before practice, to hydrate throughout the game, and ______ afterward.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The first two items in the list are infinitive phrases: to stretch and to hydrate. The third item must also be an infinitive phrase, to rest, to preserve parallel structure.

passage.text: The architect's design was praised for its bold geometry, its inventive use of natural materials, and ______.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: because it harmonized with the surrounding landscape

choices.label: C
choices.text: its harmonious connection to the surrounding landscape

choices.label: D
choices.text: to harmonize with the surrounding landscape

explanation: The list is made up of noun phrases introduced by its: its bold geometry, its inventive use, and its harmonious connection. Choice C is the only option that continues that structure.

passage.text: In her acceptance speech, the novelist thanked her editor for sharpening the manuscript, her agent for believing in the book, and ______.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: B
choices.text: her family for providing constant encouragement

choices.label: C
choices.text: her family, who provided constant encouragement

choices.label: D
choices.text: her family to provide constant encouragement

explanation: The sentence follows the pattern noun + for + gerund phrase: her editor for sharpening, her agent for believing, and her family for providing. Choice B is the only option that preserves that pattern.

passage.text: After months of planning, the community garden committee finally settled on a maintenance schedule that would be both practical and sustainable: volunteers would [blank], clear invasive weeds from the beds, and spread fresh mulch along the pathways.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: to rotate crops among the raised plots

choices.label: B
choices.text: rotate crops among the raised plots

choices.label: C
choices.text: rotating crops among the raised plots

choices.label: D
choices.text: rotation of crops among the raised plots

explanation: The list of actions after "would" consists of bare infinitives: "rotate," "clear," and "spread." Only "rotate crops among the raised plots" matches that form.

passage.text: The historian’s lecture was praised for its clarity, but her argument was compelling primarily because it wove together personal narratives, [blank], and archival photographs with unusual care.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The list items are noun phrases: "personal narratives," "statistical evidence," and "archival photographs." "Statistical evidence" is the only choice in the correct noun-phrase form.

passage.text: The advisory board concluded that the proposal should be judged not by the expense it would require immediately but by [blank].

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: its being valuable over the long term

choices.label: B
choices.text: to value it over the long term

choices.label: C
choices.text: that it is valuable over the long term

explanation: The sentence requires a noun phrase parallel to "the expense it would require immediately"; "its long-term value" provides that parallel form.

passage.text: The workshop taught participants how to draft a budget, [blank], and present their findings to stakeholders.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: After "how to," the listed verbs should be bare infinitives: "draft," "evaluate," and "present." Only "evaluate potential risks" fits.

passage.text: The selection committee admired the candidate not only for her composure under pressure but also for [blank].

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: she was willing to listen carefully

choices.label: C
choices.text: to be willing to listen carefully

explanation: The phrase after "but also for" must be a noun phrase parallel to "her composure under pressure"; "her willingness to listen carefully" is the only choice in that form.

passage.text: The restoration team’s plan for the old theater is notable for its attention to historical detail, ______, and its respect for modern safety standards.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: its use of traditional building methods

explanation: The list requires three noun phrases: “its attention to historical detail,” “its use of traditional building methods,” and “its respect for modern safety standards.” Choice A is the only noun phrase that keeps the parallel structure.

passage.text: The museum’s new app allows visitors to access audio guides, ______, and to locate interactive exhibits with ease.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: B
choices.text: to view high-resolution images of artworks

choices.label: D
choices.text: with high-resolution images of artworks to view

explanation: The item must be an infinitive phrase parallel with “to access audio guides” and “to locate interactive exhibits.” Only “to view high-resolution images of artworks” completes the parallel series of infinitives.

passage.text: City officials praised the new transit plan because it would reduce commute times, ______, and lower carbon emissions.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The list is made up of base verb phrases after “would”: “reduce commute times,” “decrease parking costs,” and “lower carbon emissions.” Only choice D maintains that parallel form.

passage.text: To prepare for the expedition, the team spent weeks reviewing satellite maps, ______, and practicing emergency protocols.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The sentence uses gerund phrases after “spent weeks”: “reviewing satellite maps,” “studying weather patterns,” and “practicing emergency protocols.” Only choice C is a gerund phrase parallel to the other items.

passage.text: A successful grant proposal must state the problem clearly, ______, and include a realistic budget.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The three items in the list must be base verb phrases after “must”: “state the problem clearly,” “propose a concrete solution,” and “include a realistic budget.” Choice A is the only base verb phrase.

passage.text: The success of a community garden depends on more than planting seeds. Volunteers must prepare the soil, choose crops suited to the local climate, and ___ throughout the growing season. Without this sustained effort, the garden quickly becomes overgrown and unproductive.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: D
choices.text: the regular watering of the plants

explanation: The modal "must" requires a series of bare infinitive verbs: prepare, choose, and water. Choice C maintains that parallelism; A uses the infinitive marker "to," B uses a gerund, and D uses a noun phrase.
