choices.text: The Alexandria Museum has a large collection of ancient Egyptian artifacts, including mummies and hieroglyphs, and it is less crowded than the Cairo Museum, so it is the better choice for the friend.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Cairo Museum has many ancient Egyptian artifacts, but it is often crowded, so the friend should expect long lines.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Alexandria Museum is located near the city center, making it easy for tourists to reach.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Both the Alexandria Museum and the Cairo Museum contain ancient Egyptian artifacts, though the Cairo Museum is more famous.

explanation: Choice A makes a clear recommendation for the Alexandria Museum and supports it with the friend's interests: ancient Egyptian artifacts and avoiding large crowds.

notes: Electric buses cost more to purchase than diesel buses.
Electricity is cheaper per mile than diesel fuel.
Electric buses have fewer moving parts and need less maintenance.
Cities may pay higher upfront costs for electric buses.
stem: A student is writing a paragraph arguing that electric buses can save a city money over time. Which sentence best supports this argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Electric buses cost more to purchase than diesel buses, which can strain a city's budget.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Although electric buses cost more to purchase, they are cheaper to fuel and maintain than diesel buses, so they can save a city money over time.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Electricity is cheaper per mile than diesel fuel, so electric buses are always better for the environment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Electric buses have fewer moving parts than diesel buses, so they require less maintenance.

explanation: Choice B acknowledges the higher upfront cost while explaining that lower fuel and maintenance costs make electric buses cheaper over time, directly supporting the argument.

notes: Many students do not eat all the food on their trays.
Food that is not eaten is usually thrown away.
Some schools set up share tables where students can leave unopened food for other students.
Share tables are inexpensive to set up and can reduce food waste.
stem: A student wants to propose a solution to reduce food waste in the school cafeteria. Which sentence best does so?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Many students do not eat all the food on their trays, so large amounts of food are thrown away every day.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Food waste is a serious problem in school cafeterias across the country.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Students should eat everything on their trays in order to avoid wasting food.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Setting up a share table, where students can leave unopened food for other students to take, is an inexpensive way for schools to reduce food waste.

explanation: Choice D proposes a specific solution, the share table, and explains why it works: it is inexpensive and reduces food waste.

notes: The Maple Street Community Garden was started in 2018 by volunteers in the Riverside neighborhood.
The garden grows tomatoes, peppers, and herbs for the local food pantry.
A compost bin at the garden turns leftover produce and kitchen scraps into fertilizer.
Last month, volunteers composted about 300 pounds of leftover produce and kitchen scraps.
The garden hosts free workshops on canning and pickling.
stem: The student is writing a city council proposal about community projects that reduce wasted food. Which sentence most effectively uses information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Maple Street Community Garden, founded in 2018 by volunteers, provides fresh tomatoes, peppers, and herbs to the local food pantry.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At the Maple Street Community Garden, a compost bin converts leftover produce and kitchen scraps into fertilizer, and volunteers composted about 300 pounds of scraps last month.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Maple Street Community Garden hosts free workshops on canning and pickling, which teach residents how to preserve food at home.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Maple Street Community Garden, located in the Riverside neighborhood, was established by volunteers who wanted to strengthen access to fresh vegetables.

explanation: Choice B directly supports the goal of reducing wasted food by describing how the garden composts leftover produce and kitchen scraps, including the 300 pounds composted last month. The other choices focus on the garden’s founding, food pantry donations, or workshops, none of which directly emphasize reducing wasted food.

notes: Students in the Eco Club launched a phone-battery recycling drive in September.
Collection bins are located in the main office and the library.
The club hopes to collect 500 batteries by the end of the semester.
Recycled batteries are processed by a certified company that recovers metals.
The club posts weekly updates to the school website.
stem: The student is writing an announcement to encourage students to recycle old batteries. Which sentence most effectively uses information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Eco Club launched a phone-battery recycling drive in September, and collection bins are in the main office and library.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Eco Club posts weekly updates to the school website about the battery recycling drive.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Eco Club hopes to collect 500 batteries by the end of the semester, with certified processors recovering metals from recycled batteries.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Eco Club’s battery recycling drive, started in September, has collection bins in the main office and library, and students can help the club reach its goal of 500 batteries by dropping off old batteries there.

explanation: Choice D is the most effective because it directly encourages students to act by telling them where to drop off batteries and why their participation matters. The other choices provide information but do not combine the goal, location, and call to action as effectively.

notes: The Tutoring Club has 20 student tutors who volunteer after school.
Tutors help with homework in math, science, and English.
Students can request a tutor online using a simple form.
Most tutoring sessions last 30 minutes and take place in the library.
The club is especially looking for students who need help with algebra.
stem: The student is writing a sentence for the school website to persuade students who are struggling in science to request a tutor. Which sentence most effectively uses information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Students who need help with science can request a Tutoring Club tutor online, and volunteer tutors are available after school to assist with science homework.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Tutoring Club has 20 student tutors who volunteer after school in the library.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Students can use a simple online form to request a tutor for math, science, or English homework.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Tutoring Club especially wants to find students who need help with algebra.

explanation: Choice A directly addresses the goal by naming science support, explaining how to request a tutor online, and noting after-school availability. The other choices either omit science, omit the action step, or focus on a different subject.

notes: The city installed 200 bike-share bikes in May.
Bike-share stations are placed near train stations and bus stops.
A city survey found that 1,500 car trips per month were replaced by bike-share rides.
The bikes are available 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
Riders use an app to unlock the bikes.
stem: The student is writing an article about the bike-share program’s effect on local transportation. Which sentence most effectively uses information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bike-share bikes are available around the clock, and riders use an app to unlock them.

choices.label: B
choices.text: After the city installed 200 bike-share bikes in May, stations were placed near train stations and bus stops.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The bike-share program has reduced driving: according to a city survey, 1,500 car trips per month were replaced by bike-share rides.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bike-share stations near train stations and bus stops make it easy for commuters to pick up or leave a bike.

explanation: Choice C is the only sentence that directly states an effect on transportation, using the survey data about replaced car trips. The other choices describe features of the program but do not emphasize its transportation impact as clearly.

notes: The Astronomy Club is hosting a public night at the school observatory on Friday.
Visitors can look through telescopes at Jupiter and the Moon.
Club members will give a short presentation about constellations.
The event is free and open to all ages.
Guests should arrive by 8 p.m. for the first telescope viewing.
stem: The student is writing a text message to a friend to persuade the friend to attend the astronomy event. Which sentence most effectively uses information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Astronomy Club is hosting a public night at the school observatory on Friday, and guests should arrive by 8 p.m. for the first telescope viewing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: You should come to the astronomy event on Friday: it’s free, and you can look through telescopes at Jupiter and the Moon.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Club members will give a short presentation about constellations at the event on Friday.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The event is open to all ages and will include telescope viewing and a constellation presentation.

explanation: Choice B is the most persuasive because it directly urges the friend to attend and gives appealing reasons: it is free and includes telescope viewing of Jupiter and the Moon. The other choices are more informational and do not effectively persuade the friend to come.

notes: Opened in 2019, Maple Street Community Garden provides free plots to local residents.
The garden is managed by volunteers and funded partly by city grants.
Each year, the garden donates about 400 pounds of produce to the neighborhood food shelf.
The garden also offers free gardening workshops every spring.
stem: The student wants to introduce the community garden to new residents by stating what it provides and one benefit of the garden. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Each year, Maple Street Community Garden donates about 400 pounds of produce to the neighborhood food shelf.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Free gardening workshops are offered every spring at Maple Street Community Garden.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Maple Street Community Garden, opened in 2019, provides free plots to local residents and each year donates about 400 pounds of produce to the neighborhood food shelf.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Maple Street Community Garden is a volunteer-managed space that opened in 2019 and offers free gardening workshops every spring.

explanation: Choice C is the only sentence that introduces the garden by naming its primary purpose—providing free plots—and also gives a concrete benefit through the annual produce donation.

notes: In 2023, the city of Fairview recycled 35 percent of its household waste.
In 2023, the city of Ashland recycled 52 percent of its household waste.
Ashland provides curbside recycling bins to every household, while Fairview requires residents to drop off recyclables at central sites.
Fairview has twice as many residents as Ashland.
stem: The student wants to compare the two cities' recycling rates and state a likely reason for the difference. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ashland recycled a higher percentage of its household waste in 2023 than Fairview did, likely because Ashland provides curbside recycling bins while Fairview requires drop-off.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fairview has twice as many residents as Ashland, which explains why Fairview recycled only 35 percent of its waste in 2023.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ashland provides curbside recycling bins to every household, while Fairview requires residents to drop off recyclables at central sites.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In 2023, Fairview recycled 35 percent of its household waste and Ashland recycled 52 percent.

explanation: Choice A is the only sentence that includes both recycling rates and a likely reason for the difference, using the note about curbside bins versus drop-off.

notes: Amara Okafor is a Nigerian American novelist born in 1985.
She grew up in Chicago and studied creative writing at Northwestern University.
Her debut novel, The Language of Roots, won the National Book Award in 2019.
The novel tells the story of a young woman exploring her family's history in Nigeria.
stem: The student wants to write a sentence for a literary magazine that introduces Okafor and states her most notable achievement. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amara Okafor grew up in Chicago and studied creative writing at Northwestern University.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Language of Roots tells the story of a young woman exploring her family's history in Nigeria.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Amara Okafor's debut novel, The Language of Roots, won the National Book Award in 2019.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Amara Okafor is a Nigerian American novelist whose debut novel, The Language of Roots, won the National Book Award in 2019.

explanation: Choice D is the only sentence that identifies who Okafor is and highlights her most notable achievement, the National Book Award-winning debut novel.

notes: The Riverfront Museum will host 'Altered Light,' an exhibit of photographs by Dana Reyes.
The exhibit will run from March 3 to July 14.
Admission is free for visitors under 18.
The exhibit includes an interactive room where visitors can experiment with colored filters.
stem: The student wants to announce the exhibit in a community calendar, including the exhibit's dates and one feature that would appeal to families. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Admission to 'Altered Light' is free for visitors under 18.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Riverfront Museum's 'Altered Light' exhibit runs from March 3 to July 14 and includes an interactive room where visitors can experiment with colored filters.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 'Altered Light' includes an interactive room where visitors can experiment with colored filters.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 'Altered Light' will be at the Riverfront Museum from March 3 to July 14.

explanation: Choice B is the only sentence that includes both the exhibit dates and the interactive room feature, which would appeal to families.

notes: Lincoln High School's student council organized a food drive in November.
The drive collected 1,200 canned goods and 350 boxes of cereal.
Donations will be distributed to three local food banks.
More than 200 students participated in the drive.
stem: The student wants to write a sentence for the school website summarizing what the food drive collected and how the donations will be used. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lincoln High School's student council organized a food drive in November, and more than 200 students participated.

choices.label: B
choices.text: More than 200 students participated in Lincoln High School's food drive, which collected 1,200 canned goods and 350 boxes of cereal.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lincoln High School's student council food drive collected 1,200 canned goods and 350 boxes of cereal, which will be distributed to three local food banks.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Donations from Lincoln High School's food drive will be distributed to three local food banks.

explanation: Choice C is the only sentence that states both what was collected and how the donations will be used, satisfying the student's goal.

notes: The school’s Environmental Club is organizing a community park cleanup.
The event will take place on Saturday, April 12, from 9 a.m. to noon.
Volunteers should bring gloves and reusable water bottles.
The club will provide trash bags and light refreshments.
Students can earn community service hours by participating.
stem: The student is writing an announcement to post on the school website. Which choice best uses the information in the notes to tell students that participating in the cleanup counts toward community service?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Students who join the park cleanup can earn community service hours.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The park cleanup will be held on Saturday, April 12, from 9 a.m. to noon.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Volunteers should bring gloves and reusable water bottles to the cleanup.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Environmental Club will provide trash bags and light refreshments.

explanation: The goal is to tell students that participating earns community service hours. Choice A directly states this, using the note about community service hours.

notes: The school library is extending its hours during exam week.
It will be open until 8 p.m. on Monday through Thursday.
On Friday, the library will close at 5 p.m. as usual.
Extra study tables and quiet rooms will be available.
Students must show their student ID to enter after 4 p.m.
stem: The student is writing an email to the student body. Which choice best uses the information in the notes to remind students about the library evening-entry rule?

choices.text: During exam week, the library will have extra study tables and quiet rooms.

choices.label: B

choices.label: C

choices.label: D
choices.text: On Friday, the library will close at 5 p.m. as usual.

Students interested in auditioning should sign up in the main office by Monday.

stem: The student is writing a newsletter article. Which choice best uses the information in the notes to tell students how to register for auditions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The talent show will take place in the auditorium.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Each act must be no longer than three minutes.

choices.label: C

choices.label: D

notes: An introductory sentence should clearly identify the essay's main topic.
It should be general enough to cover the whole essay, not just one detail.
Strong introductions often state the broader significance of the subject.
Avoid starting with a narrow anecdote or a fact that only supports one point.
stem: The student is writing an introductory sentence for an essay about the social benefits of community gardens in cities. Which sentence best accomplishes the goal of introducing the essay's main topic?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Community gardens are vacant lots that neighborhood residents convert into growing spaces.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Community gardens can be a source of fresh vegetables, but they also face challenges such as funding and maintenance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: By bringing diverse neighbors together and fostering cooperation, community gardens strengthen the social fabric of cities.

choices.label: D
choices.text: One gardener in Chicago says that her community garden has become her favorite place to relax.

explanation: Choice C directly states the essay's main topic—the social benefits of community gardens—by describing how they bring neighbors together and strengthen communities. Choice A offers only a definition, Choice B introduces unrelated problems, and Choice D focuses on a single anecdote.

notes: A transition sentence should connect the idea in the previous paragraph to the next paragraph's focus.
It should signal how the new idea follows from or contrasts with the prior one.
Avoid transitions that introduce a completely new topic without linking it to what came before.
Use clear reference to the previous point to make the shift smooth.
stem: The student is writing an essay about insect pollinators. The previous paragraph explains how bee populations have declined. The next paragraph discusses how this decline affects farmers and food prices. The student wants to add a transition sentence at the beginning of the next paragraph. Which choice best accomplishes this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bees are remarkable insects that communicate through a 'waggle dance.'

choices.label: B
choices.text: The decline in bee populations carries serious economic consequences for agriculture.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Many people are unaware that wasps, butterflies, and moths also pollinate crops.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Scientists continue to investigate the causes of colony collapse disorder.

explanation: Choice B links the previous paragraph's topic (declining bee populations) to the next paragraph's focus (economic effects on agriculture and food prices), making it the best transition. Choice A introduces unrelated biology, Choice C changes the subject to other pollinators, and Choice D repeats the previous paragraph's content.

notes: A concluding sentence should restate the main point without simply repeating it word for word.
It may offer a final judgment about the topic's importance.
Avoid introducing new evidence or subtopics in the conclusion.
The final sentence should give the reader a sense of closure.
stem: The student is writing a conclusion for an essay about the history of postal services. The essay argues that even in the digital age, postal services matter because they connect isolated communities and provide reliable delivery of essential items. Which concluding sentence best accomplishes the goal of summarizing this argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: For these reasons, postal services continue to serve as a vital link for communities that would otherwise be left behind.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The United States Postal Service currently delivers mail six days a week.

choices.label: C
choices.text: New technologies may someday change how people receive packages and letters.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the nineteenth century, mail delivery took weeks, but transcontinental railroads made it faster.

explanation: Choice A restates the essay's central argument that postal services remain important for isolated communities and essential delivery, providing a clear conclusion. Choice B is a factual aside, Choice C introduces a speculative new topic, and Choice D discusses historical detail not central to the argument.

notes: Supporting evidence should directly reinforce the claim being made.
Specific facts, statistics, or examples are more persuasive than vague statements.
The evidence should be relevant to the claim's subject and scope.
Personal opinions or unrelated details do not strengthen an argument.
stem: The student is writing to support the claim that local food festivals help small businesses. Which sentence best accomplishes this goal by providing a specific supporting detail?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Many people enjoy attending outdoor food festivals during the summer.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Food festivals are becoming increasingly popular across the country.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Small businesses at food festivals often gain new customers who return to their shops later.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At the Maple Street Food Festival, participating vendors reported an average 30 percent increase in sales.

explanation: Choice D provides a concrete statistic from a specific festival, directly showing how a local food festival boosted sales for small businesses. Choices A and B are general popularity statements, and Choice C is a vague claim without specific evidence.

passage.text: The group of hikers, despite the difficult terrain and unpredictable weather, ______ the summit before noon each year.

passage.text: By the time the museum opened on Saturday morning, the security team ______ the new exhibit's alarm system for over an hour, testing every sensor and camera.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

passage.text: According to the report, the development of new vaccines for viral diseases ______ considerable funding and years of clinical trials.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

passage.text: One of the dogs in the yard has managed to escape from ______ kennel by digging under the fence.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The singular pronoun 'one' requires the singular possessive pronoun 'its'; 'their' is plural, 'it's' is a contraction, and 'his or her' is inappropriate for an animal.

passage.text: The panel of judges, along with its guest commentator, ______ the finalists this afternoon.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the singular noun "panel" (the phrase "along with its guest commentator" does not make it plural), so the singular verb "is interviewing" is correct.

passage.text: Before launching the new software, the technology company revised ______ privacy policy to address users' concerns.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The singular noun "company" requires the singular possessive pronoun "its"; "it's" incorrectly means "it is."

passage.text: After months of testing, the engineers finally ______ the prototype in front of the review board, and the board unanimously approved it.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The past-tense verb "approved" later in the sentence establishes that the demonstration also happened in the past, so "demonstrated" is correct.

passage.text: Neither the project manager nor the software developers ______ satisfied with the revised deadline, though they agreed to try to meet it.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: With "neither...nor," the verb agrees with the nearer subject, "software developers," which is plural; the past tense "were" also matches "agreed."

passage.text: At the catered event, some of the fruit salad ______ still frozen when the first guests arrived.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Fruit salad" is a noncount noun, so "some of the fruit salad" takes the singular verb "was," matching the past tense of "arrived."

passage.text: The library’s collection of rare maps, assembled over decades by alumni and donors, _____ an invaluable resource for historians studying early navigation. Curators regularly supplement it with newly discovered charts.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the singular noun "collection," so the singular verb "offers" is required. The intervening phrase "of rare maps" contains a plural noun but does not control agreement.

passage.text: The company, along with its subcontractors, announced that _____ would honor all existing warranties after the merger. Customers were relieved by the promise.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject of the main clause is the singular noun "company," so the singular subject pronoun "it" is needed. The phrase "along with its subcontractors" does not make the subject plural.

passage.text: Though the botanist Yara Haddad is now celebrated for her discoveries in desert ecology, her early studies of cactus root systems _____ little notice until a university press republished them decades later.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The time marker "until a university press republished them" establishes a completed past situation, so the simple past "attracted" is required.

passage.text: The director was nervous, but every one of the actors in the play _____ ready when the curtain rose.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the singular pronoun "every one," not the plural noun "actors" in the prepositional phrase, so the singular past verb "was" is correct.

passage.text: After deliberating for nearly two days, the jury finally reached _____ verdict, prompting a hushed silence in the courtroom.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: In American Standard English, the collective noun "jury" is singular, so the singular possessive pronoun "its" agrees with it. "Their" treats the jury as plural, "it's" means "it is," and "its'" is not standard.

passage.text: The director of the summer program, accompanied by all of the camp counselors, ______ at the orientation meeting every June to outline safety procedures.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject of the sentence is “the director,” which is singular. The phrase “accompanied by all of the camp counselors” is parenthetical and does not change the number of the subject, so the singular verb “speaks” is correct.

passage.text: By next month, the company ______ three new branches in the western part of the state.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

passage.text: The number of visitors to the state park ______ dramatically since the new entrance road opened.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is “the number,” not “visitors,” so the verb must be singular. The present perfect “has risen” correctly links the past opening of the road to the current increase.

passage.text: The cost of the renovations, including labor and materials, ______ more than the committee had budgeted.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is “the cost,” which is singular; the intervening phrase “including labor and materials” does not make the subject plural. The past-tense singular verb “was” agrees with the subject and fits the sentence’s past-time context.

passage.text: The orchestra members tuned ______ instruments carefully before the conductor raised the baton.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the singular noun "collection"; the phrase "together with a lengthy introduction" does not change the number of the subject. Therefore, the singular present-tense verb "explains" is correct.

passage.text: When the committee members finish reviewing the applications, _______ must rank the finalists before the end of the week.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

passage.text: The two nations finally reached a cease-fire in 1921. By the time the treaty was signed, negotiations _______ for almost two years.

passage.text: Several of the witnesses were unable to recall _______ exact routes through the building.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

passage.text: Every spring, the committee of local residents reviewing the city’s budget ___ its recommendations to the mayor.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

passage.text: Last weekend, neither the manager nor the assistants ___ willing to work overtime on Saturday.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: With 'neither...nor,' the verb agrees with the closer subject, the plural 'assistants.' The phrase 'Last weekend' requires past tense, so 'were' is correct.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

passage.text: After the conference, the facilitators asked the participants to submit ___ evaluation forms before leaving the room.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The plural antecedent "participants" requires the plural possessive pronoun "their." The other choices are singular or a homophone used for a different meaning.

passage.text: By the time the train finally arrived at the station, the passengers ___ already missed two connecting buses.

passage.text: The basket of fresh peaches from the local orchard ___ next to the cash register.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

passage.text: According to the report, neither the proofreaders nor the editor ___ solely responsible for the publication delay.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: With "neither ... nor," the verb agrees with the nearer subject, "editor," which is singular. Thus, the singular present-tense verb "is" is correct.

passage.text: At the town library's annual fundraiser, each of the donated cookbooks from local chefs ___ a handwritten note in the margins describing a favorite family recipe.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the singular pronoun "each," not the plural noun "cookbooks" in the prepositional phrase. Therefore, the singular verb "has" agrees with the subject.

passage.text: The neighborhood committee, after months of discussion, announced ___ decision to oppose the proposed parking garage.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

passage.text: In a 2021 interview, the architect recalled that by the time construction on the community center began, the design team ___ already revised the floor plan three times.

passage.text: The collection of rare manuscripts, along with several annotated maps, _______ on display in the library's main hall until next month.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

passage.text: Because the hikers had forgotten to bring enough water, the group leader reminded _______ to refill their bottles at the mountain spring.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

passage.text: By the time the fire department arrived, the abandoned warehouse _______ beyond saving, and the only task left was to prevent the flames from spreading.

passage.text: The number of applicants _______ increased significantly since the scholarship was announced.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

passage.text: After four hours of deliberation last night, the panel of judges, having reviewed every submitted photograph, ___ ready to announce the winner of the community art contest.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the singular collective noun "panel." The intervening phrase "of judges" and the participial phrase do not change the number of the subject, so the singular past-tense verb "was" is correct.

passage.text: The musicians in the orchestra carefully tuned ___ instruments before the conductor raised her baton.

passage.text: By the time the fire department arrived, the sprinkler system ___ the flames in the storage room.

explanation: The action of the sprinkler system occurred before the arrival of the fire department, so the past perfect "had extinguished" is needed to show the earlier of two past events.

passage.text: The value of the rare stamps, especially the 1918 Inverted Jenny, ___ significantly over the past decade.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is "value," which is singular, and the time phrase "over the past decade" calls for the present perfect tense. Thus "has risen" is correct.

passage.text: Though the summit was still three days away, the expedition leader ___ every item on the emergency checklist by the time the porters finished loading the final crate.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

passage.text: Although many council members predicted a close vote, the number of residents at the hearing ___ far smaller than expected.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

passage.text: Before the tasting began, the judges agreed that ___ would not discuss any dish until all scores had been collected.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The pronoun must agree with the plural antecedent "judges," so the plural pronoun "they" is the only correct choice. The singular pronouns "he," "she," and "it" do not agree.

passage.text: After consulting the trail guide, the hikers concluded that neither of the two routes ___ safe to attempt in the dark.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

passage.text: Maya Lin, the architect who designed the Vietnam Veterans Memorial, ___ that a memorial should honor the lives lost rather than the conflict itself.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the singular proper noun 'Maya Lin,' so the verb must be singular: 'has argued.' The other options are either plural, nonfinite, or incorrectly tense the verb.

passage.text: Before the invention of mechanical clocks, medieval Europeans ___ time by the position of the sun, relying on sundials and canonical hours.

passage.text: Until the late nineteenth century, buildings taller than about ten stories were impractical. The introduction of electric lighting, together with the availability of cheap glass, ___ the development of the modern skyscraper.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The singular subject 'introduction' requires a singular verb, and the past-tense context established by 'Until' and 'were' calls for 'enabled.'

passage.text: Each of the studies conducted by the research team ___ a different demographic group, but all of them rely on the same survey method.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: 'Each' is singular, so the verb must be 'targets.' The other options use a plural verb, create a nonfinite phrase, or shift the tense without a past-time frame.

passage.text: When the symphony orchestra performs at the outdoor pavilion, ___ amplifiers are carefully adjusted to project the sound without overwhelming the audience.

explanation: The possessive adjective must agree with the singular collective noun 'orchestra,' so 'its' is correct. 'It's' means 'it is,' 'their' treats the orchestra as plural, and 'there' is an adverb.

passage.text: Every one of the apartments in the newly renovated building ______ a balcony that overlooks either the courtyard or the street.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the singular phrase Every one, not apartments, so the singular present-tense verb has is required.

passage.text: As soon as the orchestra had finished tuning its instruments, it ______ to play the opening movement.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The past perfect had finished establishes past time, so the finite past-tense verb began is needed.

passage.text: The collection of antique maps, spread across three display tables, has lost ______ original color in the areas exposed to sunlight.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The singular noun collection is the antecedent, so the singular possessive pronoun its is correct; it's is only a contraction of it is.

passage.text: Neither of the two proposals, in its current form, ______ the board's requirement that all projects include an exit plan.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The singular indefinite pronoun Neither is the subject, so the singular verb meets is required.

passage.text: By the time the tax returns are due, the accountants will have reviewed every ledger and ______ the discrepancies.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The verb phrase will have reviewed is completed with the past participle listed, so the sentence reads will have reviewed and listed.

passage.text: The museum’s collection of ancient coins, including several rare gold pieces from the reign of Augustus, _____ on the third floor.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

notes: Community garden established in 2015 with 20 plots

Garden donates roughly 4,000 pounds of produce each year to local food banks
Garden is maintained entirely by volunteers
Garden offers free workshops on composting and water conservation
stem: The student is writing a paragraph about the garden's role in addressing food insecurity. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: After beginning with 20 plots in 2015, the garden has grown to 120 plots and is maintained entirely by volunteers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run entirely by volunteers, the garden now has 120 plots and offers free workshops on composting and water conservation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: By donating about 4,000 pounds of produce each year to local food banks, the garden directly helps families experiencing food insecurity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The garden has a waiting list of 300 families, showing that demand for community gardening spaces is strong.

explanation: Choice C directly connects the garden's produce donations to local food banks, which is the clearest way to support a claim about addressing food insecurity.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the architect's innovative use of building materials in the Mapleton community center. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lena Ortiz designed the Mapleton community center, which opened in 2022 and hosts after-school programs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The community center Lena Ortiz designed in Mapleton cost 10 percent less to build than typical community centers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lena Ortiz's community center uses recycled steel beams and panels made from compressed straw, but it also hosts after-school programs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: By building the Mapleton community center with recycled steel beams and panels made from compressed straw, Lena Ortiz used materials in an innovative way.

explanation: The correct sentence explicitly ties the unusual materials to innovative use. The other options focus on opening date, programs, cost, or mix the materials with unrelated program information.

notes: Yuki started a neighborhood composting program in 2023.
The program distributed 500 free compost bins to residents.
Yuki's instructional videos about composting have been viewed 30,000 times.
The program has diverted 12 tons of food waste from landfills.
stem: The student wants to emphasize the environmental impact of Yuki's composting program. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yuki's neighborhood composting program has diverted 12 tons of food waste from landfills, showing a clear environmental impact.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yuki started a neighborhood composting program in 2023 and distributed 500 free compost bins to residents.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yuki's instructional videos about composting have been viewed 30,000 times, so her program has reached many people.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Yuki's composting program distributed 500 bins and diverted 12 tons of food waste from landfills, with videos viewed 30,000 times.

explanation: The correct sentence focuses on the 12 tons diverted, which directly demonstrates environmental impact. The other choices emphasize distribution, reach, or combine details without highlighting the environmental outcome.

notes: The community garden program began in 2018.
This year the program expanded into three new neighborhoods.
The program donated 2,000 pounds of produce last year.
Volunteers are needed to water plants on weekends.
Free produce is available at the downtown farmers market.
stem: The program director wants to write a sentence for the organization's newsletter announcing the expansion and asking for weekend watering volunteers. Which sentence best achieves the goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The community garden program, which began in 2018, donated 2,000 pounds of produce last year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Free produce is available at the downtown farmers market for community residents.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Because the program has expanded into three new neighborhoods, weekend watering volunteers are needed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Having begun in 2018, the program has grown to include both a farmers market and weekend watering.

explanation: Choice C directly links the program's expansion to the new need for weekend watering volunteers, fulfilling both parts of the announced goal.

notes: The debate team currently practices Tuesdays and Thursdays after school.
Regional competitions will be held in March this year.
The team captain wants to add weekly mock debates.
The team coach is available Saturday mornings.
Several team members also play spring sports.
stem: The team captain is writing an email to the principal to propose a schedule change that will help the team prepare for the regional competitions. Which sentence best achieves the goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because regional competitions are in March, the debate team should add Saturday morning practices.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Several team members play spring sports, but the team still practices after school on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The team captain wants weekly mock debates even though the coach is available Saturday mornings.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Regional competitions are held in March, so team members must manage spring sports commitments.

explanation: Choice A is the only option that proposes a specific schedule change—Saturday morning practices—and justifies it by the upcoming regional competitions.

notes: The bakery has a new loyalty program.
Customers receive a free coffee after every 10 purchases.
The loyalty program starts this month.
The loyalty card can be used at any of the bakery's three locations.
The bakery recently introduced a chocolate croissant.
stem: The bakery owner wants to write a sentence for the store's website encouraging customers to sign up for the new loyalty program. Which sentence best achieves the goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A chocolate croissant is now available at the bakery's three locations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The new loyalty program starts this month and gives customers a free coffee after 10 purchases.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Customers who sign up for the loyalty program can also buy the new chocolate croissant.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Starting this month, customers who sign up can use the new loyalty card at all three bakery locations and receive a free coffee after 10 purchases.

explanation: Choice D most completely encourages sign-ups by specifying the program's start date, the free-coffee reward, and the card's availability at all locations.

notes: Bike lanes cost the city roughly $500,000 per project.
The city has a $2 million budget surplus this year.
Residents' use of bicycles has increased by 25% in the past five years.
Adding bike lanes has been shown to reduce traffic congestion.
A recent poll found that most residents support expanding bike lanes.
stem: A city planner wants to write a sentence for a city council report recommending that the city use its budget surplus to expand bike lanes. Which sentence best achieves the goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because residents' bicycle use has increased by 25%, expanding bike lanes would address the growing demand.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Given the city's $2 million budget surplus, the city should use some of those funds to expand bike lanes and reduce traffic.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The city has a $2 million budget surplus, while residents' use of bicycles has increased by 25%.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Although bike lanes cost $500,000, the city already has enough surplus to reduce traffic congestion.

explanation: Choice B directly recommends spending part of the surplus on expanding bike lanes and states the benefit of reducing traffic; the other choices omit a clear recommendation or alter the notes.

notes: The photography exhibit 'Flora in Focus' is currently at the city museum.
The exhibit remains on view through Sunday.
It features 40 large-format photographs of flowers.
Admission is free on Saturday.
On Sunday at 2 p.m., the photographer will give an artist talk.
stem: The museum's communications coordinator wants to write a sentence for a social media post encouraging people to visit during the exhibit's final weekend. Which sentence best achieves the goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Visit 'Flora in Focus' this final weekend: admission is free Saturday, and the photographer speaks Sunday at 2 p.m.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 'Flora in Focus' features 40 large-format photographs of flowers and is currently at the city museum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The city museum's current exhibit includes photographs and an artist talk this Sunday.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Because 'Flora in Focus' has been at the museum, visitors can see the photographs before the museum closes.

explanation: Choice A is the only sentence that tells readers the exhibit is in its final weekend and gives two concrete reasons to visit: free Saturday admission and Sunday's artist talk.

notes: In 2021, researchers identified an enzyme, PETase, that can break down PET plastic.
PETase is most effective at around 30°C (86°F).
PETase activity declines sharply above 40°C.
Industrial plastic recycling usually requires temperatures above 70°C.
Scientists are engineering PETase variants that can withstand higher temperatures.
stem: A student is writing a paragraph for a science report about plastic recycling. The student wants to emphasize the principal barrier to using PETase in industrial recycling. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Although PETase can break down PET plastic, it performs best at about 30°C and loses activity above 40°C, while industrial recycling usually runs above 70°C, so the enzyme's current temperature range is a major obstacle.

choices.label: B
choices.text: PETase was identified in 2021 and is most effective at around 30°C, which is equivalent to 86°F.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Researchers are engineering PETase variants that can withstand higher temperatures, and such variants could prove useful in a number of industries.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Industrial recycling requires temperatures above 70°C, so PETase's ability to break down PET plastic is not useful in any practical setting.

explanation: Choice A directly combines the key facts about PETase's temperature limits and industrial recycling temperatures, clearly stating that the mismatch is a major obstacle. The other choices omit the temperature mismatch, focus only on a side detail, or overstate the enzyme's uselessness.

notes: A 2023 city report found that neighborhoods with more tree canopy are up to 4°C cooler in summer.
The city restricts watering of public landscaping during summer droughts.
Native oak trees, once established, require little supplemental water.
Several non-native ornamental trees need frequent watering in dry summer months.
The city plans to plant 10,000 trees over the next five years.
stem: A student is writing a letter to the city council arguing that the city should plant native oak trees. The student wants to show that this choice would address both summer heat and summer water restrictions. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to support this argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Native oak trees require little water once established, which makes them a good choice for public landscaping under the city's water restrictions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because neighborhoods with more tree canopy can be up to 4°C cooler and native oaks require little supplemental water once established, planting native oaks could reduce summer heat while staying within the city's watering restrictions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The city plans to plant 10,000 trees over the next five years, and a 2023 report measured the effect of tree canopy on summer temperatures.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Non-native ornamental trees require frequent watering during dry summers, so the city should avoid planting them in favor of native oaks.

explanation: Choice B uses the notes about tree canopy cooling and native oaks' low water needs to connect both goals: reducing heat and respecting water restrictions. The other choices address only one of the two goals or fail to mention native oaks and water restrictions together.

notes: The podcast episode begins with the host describing how public libraries have become community hubs.
Libraries now offer free workshops on digital skills, job applications, and small-business planning.
The guest is Nina Alvarez, the librarian at the downtown branch.
Nina directs the downtown branch's Digital Skills program.
In the episode, she talks with the host about how the program's technology classes help residents apply for jobs online.
stem: A student is editing a podcast script. After the host's opening remarks about libraries' expanded role, the student wants to introduce the guest and the upcoming interview topic. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Libraries now offer free workshops on digital skills, and the downtown branch's Digital Skills program has helped many residents apply for jobs online.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Our next guest is Nina Alvarez, who is the librarian at the downtown branch.

choices.label: C
choices.text: To explore how this expanded role works in practice, the host welcomes Nina Alvarez, the downtown branch librarian who directs the Digital Skills program and will discuss how its classes help residents apply for jobs online.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nina Alvarez directs the Digital Skills program at the downtown branch, and she has worked at the library for many years.

explanation: Choice C both introduces Nina Alvarez and states the interview topic, connecting her role to the library's expanded community mission. The other choices either omit the guest, omit the topic, or add unsupported information.

notes: Cognitive science research indicates that retrieving information from memory strengthens long-term retention.
A one-week study found that students who took practice quizzes recalled about 30% more material than students who reread the text.
Practice quizzes can include flashcards, old exam questions, or self-written questions.
Rereading is a common strategy but often gives only a false sense of familiarity.
stem: A student is writing advice for classmates about preparing for a cumulative exam. The student wants to convince readers that practicing retrieval is more effective than rereading. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to make this recommendation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Students often reread material because it feels productive, but taking practice quizzes is another way to study.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because practice quizzes can include flashcards, old exam questions, or self-written questions, they are convenient to create.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cognitive science research has shown that retrieving information from memory strengthens long-term retention, which is why rereading is a common strategy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: To prepare for a cumulative exam, you should test yourself with practice quizzes rather than only rereading the text: in one study, students who used retrieval practice recalled about 30% more material a week later than students who reread.

explanation: Choice D gives a clear recommendation and supports it with the study's comparative result. The other choices either fail to recommend retrieval over rereading, highlight convenience instead of effectiveness, or illogically link rereading to retrieval research.

notes: The northeast district of Fairview has no full-service grocery store.
Many Fairview residents in that district have to ride a bus for more than 30 minutes to buy fresh produce.
A vacant lot in the district is zoned for community use.
Studies show that community gardens are associated with increased vegetable consumption and stronger neighbor relationships.
A nearby city's community-garden program currently has a waiting list of 200 families.
stem: A student is writing a proposal to convert a vacant lot in Fairview into a community garden. The student wants to emphasize that the garden would meet two local needs at once. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to support this proposal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because the northeast district lacks a full-service grocery store and many residents travel more than 30 minutes by bus for fresh produce, converting the vacant lot into a community garden could improve food access while also strengthening neighbor relationships.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The vacant lot in the northeast district is zoned for community use, and the nearby city's garden program has 200 families on its waiting list.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Community gardens are associated with increased vegetable consumption and stronger neighbor relationships, so Fairview should start a program like the one in the nearby city.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Many residents of the northeast district spend more than 30 minutes riding the bus to buy fresh produce, and studies have shown that community gardens increase vegetable consumption.

explanation: Choice A identifies the local lack of grocery access and the long bus ride, then links the garden both to improved food access and to stronger neighbor relationships. The other choices omit one of the local needs, fail to connect both benefits, or do not mention the specific vacant lot.

notes: Maple Street Community Garden produced 340 pounds of vegetables in 2023 and 510 pounds in 2024.
The number of garden beds increased from 12 to 15.
Volunteer hours grew from 210 in 2023 to 290 in 2024.
The garden donated 180 pounds of vegetables to the food bank in 2023 and 300 pounds in 2024.
The garden began a composting program in 2024.
stem: The student is writing a report about the Maple Street Community Garden. The student wants to emphasize the increase in the garden's vegetable production from 2023 to 2024. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Maple Street Community Garden produced 510 pounds of vegetables in 2024 and started a composting program.

choices.label: B
choices.text: With 15 beds and 290 volunteer hours, the garden donated 300 pounds of vegetables to the food bank in 2024.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In 2024, the garden produced 510 pounds of vegetables, 170 pounds more than in 2023, and donated 300 pounds to the food bank.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The number of garden beds increased from 12 to 15, enabling the garden to donate more vegetables.

explanation: Choice C states the 2023 and 2024 production amounts and explicitly highlights the 170-pound increase, directly fulfilling the student's goal. The other options mention facts but do not emphasize the increase in production.

notes: The Book Club collected 80 books in the fall and 150 in the spring.
The Debate Club collected 120 books in the fall and 200 in the spring.
The Sports Club collected 90 books in the fall and 140 in the spring.
The Art Club collected 100 books in the fall and 190 in the spring.
stem: The student is writing a summary of a school book drive. The student wants to identify which club showed the greatest improvement from the fall to the spring collection. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Debate Club collected the most books overall, with 200 books in the spring and 120 in the fall.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Sports Club showed the smallest increase, collecting 90 books in the fall and 140 in the spring, a gain of 50.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Art Club showed the greatest improvement, increasing from 100 books in the fall to 190 in the spring, a gain of 90.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Book Club improved from 80 to 150 books, an increase of 70 books.

explanation: The Art Club's gain of 90 books is greater than the Book Club's 70, the Debate Club's 80, and the Sports Club's 50. Choice C identifies the Art Club and quantifies the largest improvement.

notes: Eagle Trail is 5.2 miles and features a waterfall overlook.
Lake Loop is 3.0 miles and circles a lake.
Ridge Trail is 7.8 miles and ends at a mountain summit.
The group wants to hike at least 4 miles and no more than 6 miles.
The group wants a trail with a distinctive scenic feature.
stem: The student is helping friends choose a hiking trail. The student wants to recommend Eagle Trail because it fits the group's distance range and scenic interest. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Eagle Trail is the best choice: at 5.2 miles it is within the group's 4-to-6-mile range and offers a waterfall overlook.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lake Loop is too short for the group, but it does circle a lake and offers an easy walk.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ridge Trail has a mountain summit, but at 7.8 miles it exceeds the group's maximum distance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Eagle Trail is exactly the same distance as Ridge Trail and has a waterfall overlook.

explanation: Choice A directly recommends Eagle Trail and connects its length and waterfall feature to the group's stated needs. The other options discuss other trails or misstate Eagle Trail's distance.

notes: School A moved its start time from 7:30 to 8:30 and saw attendance rise from 91% to 95%.
School B kept a 7:30 start time, and attendance remained at 92%.
School C moved its start time from 7:30 to 8:00 and saw attendance rise from 89% to 93%.
School D kept a 7:45 start time, and attendance fell from 90% to 88%.
stem: The student is writing a paragraph arguing that later school start times improve student attendance. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to support this argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: School A's attendance increased from 91 percent to 95 percent after moving its start time to 8:30.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both schools that adopted later start times saw attendance rise, while schools with unchanged early start times did not.

choices.label: C
choices.text: School C's attendance rose from 89 percent to 93 percent, four percentage points higher.

choices.label: D
choices.text: School D experienced a drop in attendance from 90 percent to 88 percent while keeping an early start.

explanation: Choice B synthesizes the comparative evidence: schools that moved start times later improved attendance, while schools that did not change their start times did not improve. The other choices report isolated cases without supporting the broader argument.

notes: The proposed downtown mural would cost $250,000 to create.
The city's annual arts budget is $300,000.
A survey found that 48% of residents support the mural and 45% oppose it.
Annual maintenance for the mural would cost $20,000.
The city council is scheduled to vote on the proposal next month.
stem: The student is speaking at a city council meeting. The student wants to argue against approving the mural because it would consume too much of the arts budget and because public opinion is divided. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The mural would cost $250,000 and require $20,000 per year in maintenance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because the mural would use most of the arts budget and split public opinion almost evenly, the city should not approve it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Public opinion on the mural is divided, with 48 percent supporting and 45 percent opposing it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The city council should vote on the mural next month so that residents can hear the final proposal.

explanation: Choice B combines the cost concern and the divided public opinion, supporting both reasons for the student's objection. The other choices address only one reason or an irrelevant detail.

notes: Summer reading program launched in 2019
Participation has grown from 300 to 1,200 students
Program costs the city about $4,800 per year in staff time and materials
Program has saved residents more than $200,000 in library late fees
Teachers report improved reading stamina among participants
stem: A student is writing a paragraph about the summer reading program for a city council report. The student wants to emphasize the program's financial benefit to the city. Which sentence best accomplishes this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because participation has grown from 300 to 1,200 students, the program clearly meets a community need.

choices.label: B
choices.text: With teachers reporting improved reading stamina, the program strengthens students' academic habits.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The program's $4,800 annual price tag is modest for an initiative that has grown every year since 2019.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Since the program costs the city only $4,800 per year while saving residents more than $200,000 in late fees, it is a net financial win for the city.

explanation: Choice D directly pairs the program's cost with the savings for residents, emphasizing the financial benefit to the city. The other choices focus on popularity, academic benefits, or cost alone.

notes: Proposal to add protected bike lanes on Maple Avenue
Current bike lane is a painted line only
Over the past five years, 14 bicycle-car collisions occurred on Maple Avenue
Eight of the injured riders were under age 18
A school district survey found that 60% of parents would allow children to bike to school if protected lanes existed
Protected lanes would cost $1.2 million
stem: A student is drafting a proposal about adding protected bike lanes on Maple Avenue. The student wants to emphasize the safety benefit for child cyclists. Which sentence best accomplishes this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Although protected lanes would cost $1.2 million, they could prevent the kinds of collisions that have occurred on Maple Avenue.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because eight of the fourteen riders injured on Maple Avenue in the past five years were under eighteen, a protected lane would directly address the greatest danger to child cyclists.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A school district survey found that 60% of parents would allow their children to bike to school if protected lanes were built.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Replacing a painted line with a physical barrier would reduce the total number of bicycle-car collisions on Maple Avenue.

explanation: Choice B highlights that most injured riders were under eighteen, making the safety benefit for child cyclists explicit. The other choices refer to cost, parental willingness, or collisions in general without focusing on children.

notes: Opened a specialty tea shop in 2018
In-person sales were steady but limited to local customers
Added an online store in 2021
Online orders now account for 45% of total revenue
Packaging and shipping orders added 12 extra hours of work per week
Hired a part-time fulfillment assistant in 2023
stem: A student is writing a case study about a small tea shop's expansion into online sales. The student wants to emphasize that the online store created an operational burden for the owner. Which sentence best accomplishes this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: By adding an online store, the tea shop increased its revenue, with online orders now accounting for 45% of total sales.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In-person sales have remained steady, but online customers have made the brand known outside the local community.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Online sales now account for 45% of revenue, yet packaging and shipping orders added twelve hours of work each week, a burden the owner had not anticipated.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hiring a part-time fulfillment assistant in 2023 gave the owner time to develop new tea blends and manage the shop.

explanation: Choice C explicitly identifies the extra twelve hours of work as an unanticipated burden, directly supporting the goal. The other choices emphasize revenue growth, brand reach, or a later solution rather than the operational burden.

notes: Novel is set in Kansas City during 1920s Prohibition
Critics praise detailed depictions of speakeasies, jazz clubs, and streetcars
Plot follows a young journalist investigating a missing musician
Some readers find the mystery predictable
Book club discussions often focus on historical accuracy
Voted 'best historical atmosphere' by a local literary society
stem: A student is writing a review of a historical novel for a literature blog. The student wants to suggest that the novel is valued more for its historical detail than for its plot. Which sentence best accomplishes this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Although some readers find the mystery predictable, the novel's detailed depictions of speakeasies and streetcars are what make it a favorite in book clubs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The young journalist's search for a missing musician drives a plot that keeps readers guessing until the final chapter.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Set in Kansas City during Prohibition, the novel combines a compelling mystery with carefully researched historical settings.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The novel was voted 'best historical atmosphere' by a local literary society, demonstrating its appeal among general readers.

explanation: Choice A contrasts a weak plot with the novel's praised historical detail, directly suggesting that the historical detail matters more. The other choices celebrate the plot, present the elements as equally strong, or mention only the historical atmosphere without contrasting it with the plot.

notes: Recycling contamination rate rose from 12% to 25% between 2019 and 2024
Most contaminated items are greasy pizza boxes and plastic bags
Single-stream recycling was introduced in 2019
A neighboring city using dual-stream recycling has a contamination rate of 8%
Residents surveyed: 70% are unsure which items can be recycled
The mayor wants to reduce contamination
stem: A city council member is reviewing notes about the city's recycling program. The member wants to propose the single most effective policy for reducing contamination. Which sentence best accomplishes this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The city should keep single-stream recycling because residents value the convenience of putting all recyclables in one bin.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The city should teach residents which items can be recycled, since 70% are unsure what belongs in the bin.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The city should ban greasy pizza boxes and plastic bags, because they are the most common contaminants.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The city should adopt dual-stream recycling, as the neighboring city's 8% contamination rate shows that separating materials can sharply reduce contamination.

explanation: Choice D uses the neighboring city's much lower contamination rate to support a concrete policy change. The other choices either are unsupported, address a possible cause without comparative evidence, or fail to propose a policy likely to reduce contamination.

notes: Community gardens increase access to fresh produce in urban areas.
They also provide spaces for neighbors to interact and build social ties.
A study in Cleveland found that more neighborhood green space is linked to lower stress.
The presentation will first discuss health benefits, then social benefits, and finally policy suggestions.
The speaker wants to persuade the audience to support local community garden projects.
stem: The student is writing the introductory sentence of a presentation about community gardens. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to introduce the topic, identify the main benefits, and preview the structure of the presentation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Community gardens provide fresh produce in food deserts, making them essential for reducing food insecurity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Neighbors who garden together report stronger social ties, but more research is needed on long-term effects.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Because community gardens improve both health and social cohesion, local officials should fund them.

choices.label: D
choices.text: After examining the health and social benefits of urban community gardens, this presentation will recommend ways to help them expand.

explanation: Choice D is the only option that both names the benefits covered in the notes (health and social) and previews the presentation's structure (examining benefits before recommending policies). The other choices focus on one benefit, state a conclusion too early, or introduce an unsupported caveat.

notes: Researchers surveyed 500 high school students about their sleep habits and academic performance.
Sleep data were based on student self-reports, so some reporting errors are possible.
The study followed the same students for four years.
Even with self-reported sleep, the study found a strong association between sleep and grade-point average.
A large, long-term sample makes the study's main finding persuasive.
stem: The student is writing a paragraph about a study on sleep and academic performance. Which choice best concedes the study's weakness while still defending its overall value?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Although the study relied on self-reported sleep, the large, four-year sample makes its conclusion about sleep and GPA still persuasive.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because the sleep data were self-reported, the study cannot tell us anything reliable about sleep and GPA.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The study found a strong association between sleep and GPA, and it followed the same students for four years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The study's large sample is helpful, but its reliance on self-reported sleep is a serious flaw that researchers must address.

explanation: Choice A acknowledges the weakness of self-reported data while immediately defending the study by citing its large, long-term sample. B discards the study's value, C ignores the weakness, and D emphasizes the flaw rather than defending the study's overall contribution.

notes: Some critics argue that electric vehicle charging infrastructure is too sparse for widespread adoption.
A 2023 federal program provides funds for charging stations in both rural and urban areas.
Fast chargers now can add about 200 miles of range in 15 minutes, down from hours earlier.
Electric vehicle sales increased by 40% in the last year.
These facts indicate that the infrastructure gap is closing quickly.
stem: The student wants to introduce a counterclaim and then signal that it will be refuted. Which choice best accomplishes this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Some critics claim that a lack of charging stations prevents widespread EV adoption, and they may be correct in remote areas.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some critics claim that a lack of charging stations prevents widespread EV adoption, but this objection ignores recent federal investment and faster charging technology.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Recent federal investment and faster charging technology show that the charging infrastructure gap is closing quickly.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Although electric vehicle sales rose 40% last year, many buyers still worry about finding a charger on long trips.

explanation: Choice B presents the critics' counterclaim about sparse infrastructure and immediately indicates how it will be refuted by citing federal investment and faster charging technology. A partially agrees with the counterclaim, C gives evidence without introducing a counterclaim, and D introduces a different concern rather than refuting the original one.

notes: Mixed-use developments combine homes and small businesses in a single neighborhood.
Residents of mixed-use neighborhoods walk about 30% more than residents of single-use areas.
Higher foot traffic increases sales for local shops.
Cities that allow mixed-use zoning report lower rates of car commuting.
The zoning board is revising the city's land-use rules.
stem: The student is writing to a zoning board. Which choice best synthesizes the notes into a recommendation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mixed-use developments are neighborhoods that combine homes with small businesses, such as shops and cafes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Residents of mixed-use neighborhoods walk 30% more than residents of single-use areas.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Because mixed-use developments encourage walking, strengthen local businesses, and reduce car commuting, the board should permit more of them.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cities that allow mixed-use zoning report lower commuting rates, but more research is needed before changing rules.
