choices.text: Urban beekeeping has grown by roughly 30 percent since 2016, but the resulting high hive densities can reduce the food available per colony, contributing to urban honey yields that are about 25 percent lower than rural yields.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Because high hive densities reduce food per colony and urban hives produce 25 percent less honey, cities should ban beekeeping despite the 30 percent growth since 2016.

explanation: Choice C connects the 30% growth in urban beekeeping to two negative outcomes: increased hive density and lower per-hive honey yields. The other choices either omit the growth, omit the downside, or recommend an unsupported policy.

notes: Riparian buffers are strips of vegetation along rivers and streams.
They trap nitrogen fertilizer runoff from farmland.
They shade water, keeping it cool for fish such as trout.
In one study, 30-meter buffers removed 90% of nitrogen from runoff; 10-meter buffers removed only 50%.
stem: The student wants to write a sentence that emphasizes how much the effectiveness of riparian buffers depends on buffer width. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A riparian buffer's width strongly affects its effectiveness: in one study, 30-meter buffers removed 90 percent of nitrogen from farmland runoff, whereas 10-meter buffers removed only 50 percent.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Riparian buffers are strips of vegetation along waterways that trap nitrogen from farmland runoff and shade water, keeping it cool for trout.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Wider buffers are more expensive, but 30-meter buffers remove 90 percent of nitrogen compared with 50 percent for 10-meter buffers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Although 30-meter buffers remove 90 percent of nitrogen, 10-meter buffers also remove 50 percent, so even narrow buffers are sufficient.

explanation: Choice A directly compares the 30-meter and 10-meter buffer results from the study, making the width-dependence explicit. Choice B describes benefits generally, D misreads the data, and C adds unsupported cost information.

notes: Vacant lots can be turned into community gardens.
These gardens reduce neighborhood blight.
They provide fresh produce in areas without grocery stores (food deserts).
A city survey found 70% of participating gardeners reported eating more vegetables.
The city plans to expand its community garden program.
stem: The student wants to write a sentence recommending that the city expand its community garden program based on the evidence in the notes. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Community gardens reduce blight and provide fresh produce, but the survey finding that 70 percent of gardeners eat more vegetables suggests that expanding the program would have little effect.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because 70 percent of gardeners surveyed reported eating more vegetables, the city should expand only the parts of the program that produce vegetables.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Although community gardens reduce blight, supply fresh produce, and increase vegetable consumption for 70 percent of participating gardeners, the city should not expand the program.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The city should expand its community garden program: the gardens reduce blight, bring fresh produce to food deserts, and 70 percent of participating gardeners reported eating more vegetables.

explanation: Choice D directly recommends expansion and supports it with evidence from the notes. Choices A and C draw conclusions contrary to the evidence, and Choice B adds an unsupported limitation about only vegetable-producing parts of the program.

notes: Electric school buses cost more upfront than diesel buses.
They save on fuel and maintenance over their lifetime.
Federal credits can cover 30% of the purchase price.
A district estimate: diesel bus costs $120,000; electric bus costs $230,000 upfront.
The same estimate projects $60,000 in lifetime savings per electric bus.
stem: The student wants to argue that, despite the higher upfront cost, electric school buses are financially viable. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because electric school buses cost $230,000 upfront, $110,000 more than diesel buses, they are not financially viable despite federal credits and lifetime savings.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Though electric school buses have a higher upfront cost than diesel buses, federal credits covering 30 percent of the purchase price and an estimated $60,000 in lifetime fuel and maintenance savings make them financially viable over time.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Electric school buses save $60,000 over their lifetime and federal credits cover 30 percent, so they cost less than diesel buses before they are even purchased.

choices.label: D
choices.text: School districts should choose electric buses only if they can receive federal credits and save at least $60,000, since the upfront cost is $230,000.

explanation: Choice B acknowledges the higher upfront cost and combines two financial offsets—federal credits and lifetime savings—to support financial viability. Choice A concludes the opposite, C misrepresents the timing of costs, and D adds an unsupported condition.

notes: Coral restoration projects use underwater nurseries to grow coral fragments.
Transplanted corals have a 65% survival rate after one year.
Restored reefs attract 50% more fish within three years.
Large restoration projects can cost about $200,000 per hectare.
Project costs vary widely depending on location and methods.
stem: The student wants to present a balanced view of coral restoration, acknowledging both its promise and its limitations. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coral restoration is a complete success because transplanted corals have a 65 percent survival rate and restored reefs attract 50 percent more fish, so costs should not be considered.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Large coral restoration projects can cost $200,000 per hectare, proving that they are too expensive to be worth funding.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coral restoration can help rebuild reefs—transplanted corals show 65 percent one-year survival, and restored reefs attract 50 percent more fish—but with high costs such as $200,000 per hectare, it is a promising yet not simple solution.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Although restored reefs attract 50 percent more fish, only 65 percent of transplanted corals survive, so coral restoration should be abandoned.

explanation: Choice C presents both benefits and costs, matching the goal of a balanced view. Choice A overstates success, B ignores benefits, and D recommends abandonment despite evidence of positive outcomes.

notes: Evening events in the school garden are popular but the space is too dark.
Solar-powered lights would illuminate paths and seating areas.
The lights require no connection to the school's electrical grid.
Installation costs are covered by a community grant.
The science club will maintain the lights each semester.
stem: The student government president wants to convince the school board to approve the solar-lighting project by emphasizing both safety and cost savings. Which choice best uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because the garden is too dark for evening events, the student council requests permission to install solar-powered lights that require no wiring and will be maintained by the science club.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Solar-powered lights would make the garden safer for after-school gatherings, and since they do not connect to the electrical grid, they will not increase the school's electricity bill.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The science club's willingness to maintain the lights shows that students support both the garden and the community grant that covers installation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Although the grant would pay for installation, the school board should still consider whether the lights will be bright enough for evening events.

explanation: Choice B directly combines safety (safer for after-school gatherings) and cost savings (no connection to the grid, no higher electric bill), matching the president's stated goal.

notes: Students grew bean plants in compost-amended soil and regular soil.
Plants with compost averaged 38 centimeters taller.
The study included only 20 plants, all grown in a single greenhouse.
The researchers did not test other soil amendments.
Most growth difference appeared in the first four weeks.
stem: A student wants to write a conclusion that accurately presents the main result while acknowledging that the evidence is limited. Which choice best uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The experiment proved that all gardeners should use compost, because the compost-amended plants showed the greatest growth in the first month.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Compost increased bean plant height by 38 centimeters, so the researchers recommend compost over all other soil amendments.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Although compost-amended plants grew 38 centimeters taller on average, the small sample and single greenhouse suggest that further study is needed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Because the study used only 20 plants, the results cannot be used to draw any conclusion about compost's effect on plant growth.

explanation: Choice C states the main finding (38 cm average difference) and appropriately limits the claim by noting the small sample and single greenhouse, exactly what the goal requires.

notes: Downtown merchants report that bike lanes increased foot traffic by nearly 20 percent.
Protected bike lanes reduce collisions between cars and cyclists.
The proposed lanes would run along Fourth Street for two miles.
Federal transportation grants can fund up to 80 percent of construction costs.
Most business owners on Fourth Street signed a letter in support.
stem: A city council member wants to end a debate by urging approval of the bike-lane plan and stressing its economic advantages. Which choice best uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because the lanes would bring more customers downtown and federal grants would cover most of the cost, the council should approve the Fourth Street bike lanes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Protected bike lanes reduce collisions, and Fourth Street merchants have signed a letter supporting the plan.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Federal transportation grants can fund the project, so the city should proceed with the two-mile lane before the application deadline.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Fourth Street merchants' support and the reduced collision rate demonstrate that the plan is safe and popular.

explanation: Choice A urges approval and explicitly emphasizes economic advantages: more customers and federal grants covering most of the cost. The other choices either omit an economic point or do not urge a decision.

notes: The protagonist, Elena, is a prison guard who writes poetry in secret.
Her poems celebrate freedom and open spaces.
She wins a national poetry prize under a pen name.
Her daily life is governed by rigid routines and surveillance.
Elena never recognizes the contradiction between her poetry and her job.
stem: A literary critic wants to highlight the central irony of Elena's situation in one sentence. Which choice best uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elena's prize-winning poems celebrate freedom, yet she fails to see that her own life is confined by the same rigid routines she enforces.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Elena writes poetry in secret and wins a national prize, but she works as a prison guard rather than as a full-time writer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The surveillance that surrounds Elena in her job is contradicted by the open spaces in her poems.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Although Elena's poems won a national prize, they were published under a pen name to keep her job safe.

explanation: Choice A captures the irony: Elena writes about freedom while unknowingly living under the same rigid routines and confinement she helps enforce. The other choices present facts without developing the contradiction.

notes: Riverfront cleanup is scheduled for Saturday at 9 a.m.
Volunteers will meet at the boathouse pavilion.
Gloves, bags, and grabbers will be provided.
One volunteer typically collects about 10 pounds of trash in two hours.
Volunteers should register online to reserve a spot.
stem: An environmental group wants to post a message that motivates people to sign up by showing how a single morning can make a meaningful difference. Which choice best uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Volunteers who meet at the boathouse pavilion on Saturday will receive gloves, bags, and grabbers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Register online now to join Saturday's riverfront cleanup—in just two hours, one volunteer can remove ten pounds of trash from the river.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The riverfront needs help, and Saturday's event will provide all necessary equipment, so please attend.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Those who cannot volunteer on Saturday can still support the group's efforts by registering online for future events.

explanation: Choice B urges immediate action (register online now) and gives a concrete, meaningful outcome: in just two hours, one volunteer removes ten pounds of trash. This directly satisfies the goal of motivating sign-ups.

notes: The Parkside Community Garden started in 2016 on a vacant lot.
It now has 120 plots, 40% reserved for first-time growers.
Membership fees support workshops and a tool-sharing program.
A 2021 survey found that 85% of members reported improved access to fresh produce.
Monthly cooking demonstrations use vegetables grown on site.
stem: A student is writing a paragraph about the benefits of the Parkside Community Garden. Which sentence most effectively uses the notes to support the claim that the garden improves both food access and gardening or cooking skills?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The garden improves food access, with 85% of members reporting improved access to fresh produce, and builds skills through workshops and monthly cooking demonstrations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because the garden began as a vacant lot in 2016, it demonstrates how unused land can become a source of fresh produce.

choices.label: C
choices.text: With 120 plots, 40% reserved for first-time growers, the garden has helped more people learn to grow food.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Membership fees fund workshops and a tool-sharing program, and monthly cooking demonstrations feature vegetables grown on site.

explanation: Choice A is the only option that directly addresses both parts of the claim: food access (the 85% survey result) and skill-building (workshops and cooking demonstrations). The other choices mention only one benefit or do not connect the notes to the claim.

notes: Electric vehicle charging stations in Millbrook doubled from 15 in 2018 to 30 in 2023.
In the same period, electric vehicle registrations in Millbrook tripled from 200 to 600.
Charging stations are used more often in commercial districts than in residential areas.
A city program offers rebates for home charger installation.
Planners predict that demand for public charging will soon exceed capacity.
stem: A student wants to argue that the Millbrook City Council should expand public charging infrastructure. Which sentence best uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Charging stations in Millbrook doubled from 15 to 30, and electric vehicle registrations tripled from 200 to 600.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because electric vehicle registrations tripled while charging stations only doubled, and planners predict demand will exceed capacity, Millbrook should expand public charging infrastructure.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Since charging stations are used more often in commercial districts than in residential areas, new stations should be built only in commercial districts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The city's rebates for home charger installation show that private charging is sufficient, so expanding public stations is unnecessary.

explanation: Choice B provides a logical argument for expansion by comparing the slower growth of stations with the faster growth of electric vehicles and citing the predicted capacity shortfall. The other choices either fail to make a recommendation, draw an unsupported conclusion, or contradict the notes.

notes: In a study, students who ate breakfast before an exam scored on average 12% higher than those who did not.
The study controlled for sleep and prior grades.
The average score for breakfast-eaters was 82%; for non-breakfast-eaters, it was 70%.
Researchers suggest the effect may be due to glucose availability in the brain.
Some nutritionists caution that the type of breakfast matters.
stem: A student wants to present the study's central finding while also noting the caveat raised by nutritionists. Which sentence best uses the notes to do so?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because researchers believe the effect may be due to glucose availability, students should eat breakfast before exams.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The study controlled for sleep and prior grades, and breakfast-eaters averaged 82% while non-breakfast-eaters averaged 70%.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Students who ate breakfast before an exam scored 12% higher on average than those who did not, but nutritionists caution that the type of breakfast matters.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The higher average scores among breakfast-eaters prove that eating breakfast causes better exam performance.

explanation: Choice C gives the main finding (the 12% score difference) and the nutritionists' caveat (that breakfast type matters), satisfying both parts of the goal. Choice A makes a recommendation, B omits the caveat, and D overstates the finding as proof of causation.

notes: The town of Alden installed solar panels on the roof of its public library in 2021.
Annual electricity costs for the library dropped from $24,000 to $18,500.
The panels generate about 70% of the library's electricity needs.
The installation cost $60,000, which was funded by a state grant.
The library used the savings to extend its hours on weekends.
stem: A student is writing a paragraph about the effects of the solar panel installation at the Alden Public Library. Which sentence best uses the notes to describe the installation's effects?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The solar panels generate 70% of the library's electricity, so the installation has been a success.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Although the panels cost $60,000, the state grant covered the cost.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Since the state grant paid for the panels and the library saves $5,500 per year, the town should install solar panels on all public buildings.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Installing solar panels in 2021 lowered the library's annual electricity costs from $24,000 to $18,500, and the savings allowed the library to extend weekend hours.

explanation: Choice D directly describes two concrete effects of the installation: reduced electricity costs and expanded weekend hours. The other choices either make a recommendation, focus only on funding, or offer a vague judgment rather than describing effects.

notes: Pocket Tutor pairs high school students with volunteer college tutors.
Students using the app for at least two hours per week improved their math grades by an average of half a letter grade.
The app is free for students and funded through donations.
Teachers report that students who use the app are more confident when asking questions in class.
Some users say the video chat feature sometimes freezes.
stem: A student is writing a proposal recommending that the school promote the Pocket Tutor app. Which sentence best uses the notes to support the recommendation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because students who use Pocket Tutor for at least two hours per week improve their math grades by half a letter grade and teachers report that these students are more confident in class, the school should promote the app.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pocket Tutor pairs high school students with volunteer college tutors and is funded by donations, so it is worth recommending.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Although some users report that the video chat sometimes freezes, Pocket Tutor has helped many students, making it the best free tutoring app available.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The app is free for students and funded through donations, so the school should use it instead of hiring more teachers.

explanation: Choice A supports the recommendation with concrete positive outcomes from the notes: improved math grades and increased confidence in class. The other choices rely on vague praise, unsupported claims, or recommendations that do not follow from the notes.

notes: Monarch butterflies can travel up to 3,000 miles during their annual migration.
Completing the journey takes several generations; no single butterfly makes the entire round trip.
Butterflies born in late summer are the ones that fly back to overwintering sites in Mexico.
They navigate using the sun’s position and the earth’s magnetic field.
stem: The student is writing a report about monarch butterflies. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to emphasize that the monarch migration is a multi-generational accomplishment rather than a single butterfly’s journey?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Although no single monarch makes the entire 3,000-mile migration, the annual journey is completed through a relay of three to five generations of butterflies.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Monarch butterflies travel up to 3,000 miles, and late-summer butterflies use the sun and magnetic field to find their overwintering sites in Mexico.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The 3,000-mile migration of monarch butterflies is an impressive feat because each butterfly navigates by the sun and the earth’s magnetic field.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Because no single monarch makes the entire migration, late-summer butterflies must use the sun and magnetic field to reach overwintering sites in Mexico.

explanation: Choice A correctly emphasizes the multi-generational nature of the migration: no single butterfly completes the full journey, but the overall migration is finished through a relay of generations. The other choices either omit that idea or incorrectly imply that individual butterflies complete or navigate the entire journey.

notes: Wind and solar power generate electricity only when conditions are favorable, so energy storage is crucial for a reliable renewable grid.
Some renewable grids need to store energy for several days, not just a few hours.
Pumped hydro can store large amounts of energy for long periods but depends on specific geography and large water supplies.
Iron-air batteries are being developed for multiday energy storage and can be located in many more places than pumped hydro.
stem: The student is writing an essay on renewable energy. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to recommend iron-air batteries as the more practical technology for long-duration storage in regions that lack suitable terrain for pumped hydro?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Although iron-air batteries are a newer technology, pumped hydro remains the more practical choice for long-duration storage because it can hold large amounts of energy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because solar and wind power are intermittent, any reliable renewable grid must include both pumped hydro and iron-air batteries to overcome geographic limitations.

choices.label: C
choices.text: For regions without the specific geography or large water supplies needed for pumped hydro, iron-air batteries offer a practical way to provide the multiday storage that a renewable grid requires.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Since pumped hydro requires large water supplies and specific geography, iron-air batteries cannot yet provide enough long-duration storage for regions without suitable terrain.

explanation: Choice C directly recommends iron-air batteries for the stated condition: regions lacking the terrain and water needed for pumped hydro. It accurately synthesizes the notes about multiday storage and the geographic limits of pumped hydro. The other choices either recommend against iron-air batteries, propose an unsupported combination, or contradict the notes.

notes: Road traffic noise is linked to sleep disruption and cardiovascular problems.
Tall sound walls can reduce traffic noise near highways, but they are expensive and block views.
Dense rows of trees and shrubs, called vegetative barriers, can absorb sound and are cheaper than sound walls.
Vegetative barriers need space and regular maintenance, so they work best in suburban or rural areas.
stem: The student is writing about highway noise reduction. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to argue that vegetative barriers are a better option than sound walls in suburban areas?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Although sound walls are expensive and block views, they reduce traffic noise more effectively than vegetative barriers in suburban areas.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because traffic noise is linked to sleep disruption and cardiovascular problems, sound walls should be built along all highways.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vegetative barriers can reduce traffic noise but require space and regular maintenance, so sound walls are the better choice in suburban areas.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In suburban areas, where space is available, cheaper vegetative barriers can reduce highway noise without the expense and visual drawbacks of sound walls.

explanation: Choice D most effectively argues for vegetative barriers in suburban areas: it notes that space is available there and contrasts their lower cost and lack of visual drawbacks with sound walls. The other choices either oppose vegetative barriers, overgeneralize, or fail to make the suburban comparison.

notes: Octopuses can instantly change the color and texture of their skin to match rocks, coral, or sand.
Their soft bodies have no skeleton.
Because they have no skeleton, octopuses can squeeze through very small openings to escape predators.
When threatened, some octopuses release a cloud of ink to confuse predators.
stem: The student is writing an article about octopus defense strategies. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to describe how an octopus’s body structure and behavior both help it escape predators?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Octopuses can escape predators by changing the color and texture of their skin to match rocks or coral and by releasing ink to confuse attackers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: An octopus’s lack of a skeleton allows it to squeeze through tiny openings, and it can also avoid predators by changing color and texture to blend in with its surroundings.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Although an octopus can change color and texture, it needs to release ink to escape because its soft body without a skeleton cannot squeeze through small openings.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Octopuses rely on camouflage rather than their soft, skeletonless bodies because changing color and texture is their only effective way to avoid predators.

explanation: Choice B includes both elements requested by the goal: the structural advantage of having no skeleton, which lets octopuses squeeze through small openings, and the behavioral advantage of camouflage through color and texture change. The other choices omit one of these elements or contradict the notes.

notes: Many students lack reliable internet access at home.
The school library is open until 6 p.m. on weekdays.
The library has desktop computers that students can use.
A volunteer club has offered to provide after-school homework help.
stem: The student is writing a proposal to the school principal. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to propose an after-school homework-help program that addresses the lack of reliable home internet access?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because many students lack reliable internet at home, teachers should reduce the number of internet-based homework assignments they give.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The school could address the lack of reliable home internet by creating an after-school homework-help program in the library, where students can use the available computers and work with volunteer tutors.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Although the library has computers and volunteer tutors, an after-school program would do little to help students who lack reliable internet at home.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Students without reliable home internet should use library computers and volunteer tutors instead of doing internet-based homework at home.

explanation: Choice B best meets the goal: it proposes a specific program, ties it directly to the lack of reliable home internet, and uses the notes about library computers and volunteer tutors. The other choices either suggest a different policy, reject the program, or give advice to students rather than proposing a school program.

notes: Phoenix, Arizona, experiences summer temperatures that often exceed 40°C.
A mature palo verde tree provides light shade and uses less than 30 liters of water per week.
A mature mulberry tree provides dense shade but uses more than 200 liters of water per week.
City officials are evaluating tree-planting programs to reduce urban heat.
Desert-adapted trees such as palo verde have small leaves that let more sunlight through.
stem: The student is writing a paragraph about choosing trees for a desert city. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to contrast the cooling benefits of the two tree species with their water needs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Palo verde trees use less than 30 liters of water per week, so city officials should plant only palo verde trees to reduce urban heat.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Although palo verde trees use less than 30 liters of water per week, their small leaves let more sunlight through, so they provide only light shade.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Palo verde trees offer light shade while using less than 30 liters of water per week, but mulberry trees offer dense shade while using more than 200 liters, presenting a trade-off between water use and cooling.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Because mulberry trees use more than 200 liters of water per week, city officials should prioritize them over palo verde trees despite their dense shade.

explanation: Choice C directly contrasts the palo verde's low water use and light shade with the mulberry's high water use and dense shade, capturing the trade-off the prompt asks for.

notes: Before the 1870s, most rural families bought goods at local general stores with limited inventory.
Aaron Montgomery Ward launched the first general merchandise mail-order catalog in 1872.
The catalog allowed rural customers to order many products by mail and have them delivered by railroad.
Some local merchants criticized mail-order companies for taking business away.
By 1900, mail-order catalogs were common in many rural households.
stem: The student is writing a paragraph about the rise of mail-order shopping in the United States. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to explain how Montgomery Ward's catalog changed rural shopping?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Montgomery Ward's 1872 catalog changed rural shopping by letting families order a wide array of goods by mail instead of relying on the limited stock at local general stores, with delivery handled by railroad.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Local merchants criticized mail-order companies for taking business away, but by 1900 mail-order catalogs were common in many rural households.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Montgomery Ward launched the first general merchandise mail-order catalog in 1872, and by 1900 many rural households regularly used mail-order catalogs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rural families could order products by mail and have them delivered by railroad, which is why local merchants criticized mail-order companies for taking business away.

explanation: Choice A explains the mechanism of change: catalog ordering replaced reliance on limited local store inventory and used railroad delivery. The other choices focus on popularity, chronology, or criticism rather than the explanatory change.

notes: Humpback whale songs are made of repeated sound units called phrases and themes.
Researchers have found that whales combine these phrases in ordered, predictable patterns.
Certain phrase transitions in whale songs are much more likely than others.
Human languages use grammar, or rules for combining words into sentences.
Whale songs gradually change over time within a population.
stem: The student is writing an essay about animal communication. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to support the claim that humpback whale songs are rule-governed like human language?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Humpback whale songs consist of repeated phrases and themes, and human languages also use grammar.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Like human languages, which use grammatical rules to combine words, humpback whale songs combine phrases in ordered, predictable patterns, with some transitions more likely than others.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Because whale songs change gradually over time within a population, human language and whale song both evolve through use.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Researchers have found certain phrase transitions that are more likely than others, but this does not prove that whales follow grammatical rules similar to humans.

explanation: Choice B draws the parallel between human grammatical rules and the ordered, predictable phrase combinations found in whale songs, directly supporting the claim. Choice A is too vague, and C and D shift focus away from rule-governed structure.

notes: The exhibition will display ancient textiles that can be damaged by bright light.
Visitors who use wheelchairs need wider pathways and lower display cases.
The exhibition space has large windows that let in strong sunlight.
Curators want to protect the textiles without making the space feel closed off.
Adjustable filtered window film can reduce bright light while still letting in daylight.
stem: The student is writing a proposal for a museum exhibition. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to recommend a layout that addresses both accessibility and preservation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because the ancient textiles can be damaged by bright light, the museum should cover the large windows with opaque curtains and install artificial lighting.

choices.label: B
choices.text: To make the exhibition fully accessible, the museum should install wider pathways and lower display cases, but this may require reducing the number of textiles displayed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The exhibition space has large windows and many visitors who use wheelchairs, so curators should install adjustable filtered window film to block all sunlight.

choices.label: D
choices.text: To protect the ancient textiles from strong sunlight while keeping the space open, curators could install adjustable filtered window film and also provide wider pathways and lower display cases for visitors who use wheelchairs.

explanation: Choice D combines the preservation solution (adjustable filtered film) with the accessibility solution (wider pathways and lower display cases) and respects the curators' wish to keep the space open.

notes: One hundred college students memorized 40 word pairs.
Half of the students napped for 60 minutes after learning; the other half stayed awake.
On a memory test one hour later, the napping group recalled more word pairs than the non-napping group.
The researchers did not measure how much sleep the students had gotten the night before.
All participants were college students; no older adults were included.
stem: The student is writing a report on a sleep and memory study. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to identify the most serious weakness in the researchers' conclusion that the nap caused the better recall?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because the study included only college students, the results cannot be generalized to older adults.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The researchers measured recall only one hour after the study session, so they cannot know whether napping improves long-term memory.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Since the researchers did not measure how much sleep the participants had gotten the night before, students in the nap group may have started the experiment with different levels of sleep debt, making the nap an unreliable explanation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Memorizing 40 word pairs is an artificial task, so the study probably does not reflect how memory works in everyday life.

explanation: Choice C identifies a confounding variable: without measuring prior sleep, the researchers cannot rule out preexisting differences in sleep debt as the cause of the recall difference. The other choices raise external-validity concerns but do not directly undermine the causal claim.

notes: Reintroduction of gray wolves to Yellowstone National Park began in 1995 after a nearly 70-year absence.
Wolves reduced elk populations, allowing overgrazed willow and aspen to recover.
Recovering plants stabilized riverbanks and created habitat for birds and beavers.
Changes in wolf numbers also affected coyotes, which allowed smaller predators and rodents to increase.
Some ranchers near the park report occasional livestock losses, though compensation programs exist.
stem: The student wants to write a concluding sentence that emphasizes how the reintroduction of wolves illustrates broad ecological interconnectedness. Which choice best achieves this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because compensation programs exist, ranchers in the area should not be concerned about livestock losses.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The recovery of plants and animals at many levels shows that removing one top predator can reshape an entire ecosystem.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Wolves are large carnivores that typically hunt elk and deer in packs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The 1995 reintroduction of wolves was a controversial decision with many supporters and critics.

explanation: Choice B is the only sentence that draws a broad conclusion about ecological interconnectedness from the notes' chain of effects. The other choices either mention unrelated details, state characteristics of wolves, or focus on controversy rather than ecosystem relationships.

notes: Gutenberg developed movable type around 1440 in Mainz, Germany.
The Gutenberg Bible, printed in 1455, was among the first major European books mass-produced with movable type.
Printing lowered book prices, supporting wider literacy and the spread of Reformation ideas.
Printers combined text and images, encouraging new forms of reading.
By 1500, press output across more than 200 cities totaled millions of volumes.
stem: The student wants to begin an essay with a sentence that characterizes the printing press as a catalyst for an information revolution rather than merely a technological invention. Which choice best achieves this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Gutenberg Bible, printed in 1455, was one of the first major books created using movable type.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A printing press works by applying pressure to transfer ink from movable type to paper.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gutenberg's device changed how information was created, shared, and consumed throughout Europe.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Many early printers were also booksellers who traveled to regional trade fairs.

explanation: Choice C directly frames the printing press as a transformative force in information exchange, matching the goal of emphasizing an information revolution. The other choices describe mechanical details, specific products, or business practices without making that broader characterization.

notes: During sleep, the brain replays and strengthens neural connections formed during waking hours.
In studies, people who nap after training on a new skill perform better on later tests than those who stay awake.
Sleep deprivation reduces activity in the hippocampus, which is important for forming new memories.
These effects appear consistently across age groups, from children to older adults.
stem: The student wants to write a concluding sentence that states the practical significance of the findings for students. Which choice best achieves this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The hippocampus, a curved structure deep in the temporal lobe, is especially active during sleep.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Thus, getting enough sleep should be treated as an essential part of preparing for a test or learning a new skill.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some students report that they can manage with very little sleep, but scientific evidence suggests otherwise.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A short daytime nap of twenty minutes can improve alertness more effectively than a cup of coffee.

explanation: Choice B draws a direct practical conclusion from the notes, translating the research findings into an actionable recommendation for students. The other choices either provide anatomical background, rely on unsupported student anecdotes, or introduce details not present in the notes.

notes: The Seneca Falls Convention of 1848 issued the Declaration of Sentiments that called for women's right to vote.
The Nineteenth Amendment, ratified in 1920, prohibited denying the right to vote on account of sex.
African American women activists such as Ida B. Wells continued to face poll taxes, intimidation, and other racial barriers after 1920.
The Voting Rights Act of 1965 removed many remaining legal obstacles to voting for people of color.
stem: The student wants to make the point that the fight for voting rights did not end in 1920. Which choice best uses the notes to express that point?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Declaration of Sentiments closely followed the language of the Declaration of Independence.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ida B. Wells was an African American journalist and teacher who campaigned against lynching.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Voting rights movements in Britain and the United States influenced each other in the nineteenth century.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Nineteenth Amendment was a key victory, yet secure voting access required further activism and legislation.

explanation: Choice D directly synthesizes the notes by acknowledging the Nineteenth Amendment as a milestone while pointing to the continued barriers and later legislation. The other choices focus on unrelated historical details, individual biography, or cross-national influences rather than the ongoing struggle after 1920.

notes: A 2021 study of 12 cities found neighborhoods with a park within a 10-minute walk had lower average summer temperatures.
People living near green spaces report lower stress and higher levels of physical activity.
Access to parks is unequal: lower-income neighborhoods often have fewer and smaller parks.
Cities that invest in park maintenance see higher nearby property values and more local business activity.
stem: The student wants to recommend a policy that follows directly from the evidence in the notes. Which choice best does so?

choices.label: A
choices.text: City governments should prioritize park creation and maintenance in neighborhoods that currently lack them.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Parks are most valuable when they are located near residential property rather than commercial areas.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The 2021 study showing temperature differences proves that all cities will experience the same effects.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Residents who do not use parks cannot benefit from the environmental and health advantages they provide.

explanation: Choice A follows logically from the notes: parks provide measurable benefits, but access is unequal, so a reasonable policy recommendation is to focus on underserved neighborhoods. The other choices make unsupported generalizations, introduce value judgments not in the notes, or contradict the documented environmental benefits.

notes: The city spent $180,000 to create 12 community gardens.
A study found that nearby property values rose by 31% over five years after the gardens were established.
Residents living near the gardens reported 25% more weekly outdoor physical activity.
Garden plots are assigned by lottery each spring.
Researchers controlled for other neighborhood improvements when analyzing property values.
stem: The student is writing a paragraph for a city council report about the municipal benefits of community gardens. Which choice most effectively uses information from the notes to support the stated goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Community gardens created a measurable benefit for the city: in a controlled study of 12 gardens, nearby property values rose 31% and nearby residents reported 25% more weekly outdoor physical activity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Although the city spent $180,000 to create the gardens, property values rose only among the 12 neighborhoods studied, so the program is probably not worth repeating.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Because garden plots are assigned by lottery each spring, community gardens have become increasingly popular across the city.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A controlled study of 12 community gardens found that property values rose 31%, but there is no evidence that residents became more physically active.

explanation: The goal is to describe municipal benefits. Choice A combines the controlled study's findings of increased property values and physical activity, directly supporting benefits. The other choices introduce unsupported claims or contradict the notes.

notes: The Aqua Appia was built in 312 BCE and was Rome's first aqueduct.
Its water came from a spring about 16 kilometers from Rome.
The channel was mostly underground, with only a short above-ground section.
It delivered about 75,000 cubic meters of water per day.
The water was used mainly for public fountains, not private homes.
stem: The student is writing a description of the Aqua Appia as an engineering system. Which choice most effectively uses information from the notes to achieve this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Built in 312 BCE as Rome's first aqueduct, the Aqua Appia was an important symbol of Roman engineering.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Drawing on a spring about 16 kilometers away, the Aqua Appia ran mostly underground and delivered about 75,000 cubic meters of water per day to public fountains.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Although the Aqua Appia was Rome's first aqueduct, its water was used mainly for public fountains rather than private homes, which limited its usefulness.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Because the Aqua Appia's source was 16 kilometers from Rome and it was built in 312 BCE, it was older than most other aqueducts.

explanation: The goal is to describe the Aqua Appia as an engineering system. Choice B gives concrete engineering details: water source, underground channel, daily capacity, and end use. The other choices focus on symbolism, unsupported judgment, or age rather than how the system worked.

notes: In a two-year pilot, 1,000 adults received $500 per month with no work requirements.
Employment among participants remained stable during the pilot.
Average household debt among participants fell by 18%.
Participants were more likely to report being able to cover an unexpected $400 expense.
Administrative costs were 6% of total program expenditures.
Some participants used extra funds to pay for transportation to job interviews.
stem: The student is writing an evaluation of a universal basic income pilot's economic effects on participants. Which choice most effectively uses information from the notes to achieve this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The pilot's administrative costs were only 6% of total expenditures, proving the program would be equally effective in other cities.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Participants used some extra funds to pay for transportation to job interviews, which proves that unconditional cash transfers always improve employment outcomes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In the pilot, participants received $500 per month with no work requirements; employment remained stable, average household debt fell by 18%, and more participants could cover unexpected expenses, suggesting positive economic effects.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Although employment remained stable and average household debt fell by 18%, participants still had difficulty covering unexpected expenses, so the pilot had little economic benefit.

explanation: The goal is to evaluate economic effects on participants. Choice C reports stable employment, reduced debt, and improved ability to handle unexpected expenses, all directly relevant. The other choices make unsupported generalizations or contradict the notes.

notes: Seagrass meadows cover less than 0.2% of the ocean floor.
They store about 10% of the carbon buried in ocean sediments each year.
Carbon can remain stored in seagrass roots and soils for centuries.
Seagrass meadows are being lost at a rate of about 7% per year globally.
Protecting existing meadows is often cheaper than planting new trees.
Seagrass species are found along coastlines in more than 150 countries.
stem: The student is writing an essay arguing that protecting seagrass meadows is an effective climate strategy. Which choice most effectively uses information from the notes to support this argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Seagrass meadows cover less than 0.2% of the ocean floor, so they cannot be an effective climate strategy despite storing carbon for centuries.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because seagrass meadows are found in more than 150 countries and are being lost at a rate of about 7% per year, countries should prioritize mapping them rather than protecting them.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Protecting seagrass meadows is often cheaper than planting trees, so protecting them is more cost-effective than any other climate strategy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Protecting seagrass meadows is an effective climate strategy because, although they cover less than 0.2% of the ocean floor, they store about 10% of the carbon buried in ocean sediments each year and can hold carbon for centuries.

explanation: The goal is to support seagrass protection as an effective climate strategy. Choice D uses the notes' strongest carbon-related evidence: high proportional carbon storage and long-term carbon retention. The other choices contradict the notes or rely on unsupported overgeneralizations.

notes: LED lighting emits very little heat and no ultraviolet radiation.
Fiber-optic lighting can create dramatic highlights but requires more maintenance.
Visitors rated exhibits lit with warm-color LEDs higher than exhibits lit with standard fluorescent light.
Oil paintings can be damaged by prolonged exposure to ultraviolet radiation.
A study found that visitors spent 40% more time looking at artworks lit by LEDs.
stem: The student is writing a proposal recommending a lighting system for a museum's oil painting gallery. Which choice most effectively uses information from the notes to support the recommendation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The museum should use LED lighting because it emits very little heat and no ultraviolet radiation, protecting oil paintings, and because visitors rated LED-lit exhibits higher and spent 40% more time viewing them, improving visitor experience.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The museum should use fiber-optic lighting because it can create dramatic highlights, even though LEDs emit no ultraviolet radiation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Because oil paintings can be damaged by ultraviolet radiation, the museum should avoid all artificial lighting and rely only on natural light.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Visitors spent 40% more time looking at LED-lit artworks, so LED lighting is clearly superior to fiber-optic lighting for creating dramatic highlights.

explanation: The goal is to recommend a lighting system for an oil painting gallery. Choice A directly supports LED lighting with both preservation benefits (no UV, little heat) and visitor experience benefits (higher ratings, more viewing time). The other choices are unsupported or misrepresent the notes.

notes: Major causes: dark surfaces and lack of vegetation absorb and re-emit heat.
Cities can be 1–3°C warmer than surrounding rural areas.
Heat islands increase energy demand for air conditioning.
Heat-related illness and death are more common in vulnerable populations.
Mitigation: cool roofs, urban tree canopy, green spaces.
stem: The student is writing a report about urban heat islands. The student wants to emphasize that urban heat islands are a serious public health issue, not just an environmental curiosity. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because dark roofs and asphalt absorb heat during the day, a city can be several degrees warmer than the nearby countryside.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Among older adults and people without air conditioning, the stronger heat island effect leads to higher rates of heat exhaustion and death.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reducing the urban heat island effect would require a combination of cool roofs, more trees, and expanded green spaces.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The temperature gap between a city and its surrounding rural areas influences how much energy residents use to cool their homes.

explanation: The goal is to present urban heat islands as a public health concern. Choice B directly names vulnerable people and severe health outcomes, while the other choices focus on causes, mitigation, or energy use.

notes: Teenagers' circadian rhythms shift: they naturally fall asleep later and need about 8–10 hours.
Early start times cause chronic sleep deprivation.
Later starts are associated with better attendance and fewer tardies.
Studies link later starts to modest improvements in grades and test scores.
After a later-start policy, some districts reported fewer car crashes involving teen drivers.
stem: The student is preparing an oral presentation to parents at a school board meeting. The student wants to open with a sentence that connects a later school start time directly to parents' concerns about their own teenagers. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: School boards across the country are reconsidering start times because the evidence about adolescent sleep is compelling.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When a teenager cannot get out of bed on time, the problem is not laziness but a biological shift in circadian rhythms.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Imagine fighting less with your teenager every morning and seeing better grades; that is what later start times have produced in other districts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Teens involved in car crashes are often sleep-deprived because of early school schedules.

explanation: Choice C directly addresses parents by evoking a relatable daily struggle, then links later start times to improved grades, a central parental concern. The other options are informative but less personal and immediate.

notes: Volunteers at the food pantry report a stronger sense of community connection.
Local nonprofits need steady help, especially on weekends.
One-time tasks, such as sorting donations, require no specialized skills.
Food insecurity in the county has risen by 12% in the past two years.
River Park Cleanup will take place this Saturday from 9 a.m. to noon.
stem: The student is writing the final sentence of a post encouraging classmates to volunteer. The student wants to inspire immediate action and give readers a specific way to participate. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sign up for this Saturday's River Park Cleanup before the volunteer slots fill up.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Volunteering can be a rewarding way to meet neighbors and make a difference in your community.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Because food insecurity in the county has risen sharply, local nonprofits need more help than ever.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Even a few hours of sorting donations can provide meaningful support to families facing hunger.

explanation: Choice A is the only option that does both required things: it urges immediate action and names a concrete event. The other choices motivate or describe needs but give readers no specific way to act now.

notes: After Reconstruction, several states imposed poll taxes and literacy tests.
Grandfather clauses allowed white voters whose grandfathers had voted to skip these requirements.
Some jurisdictions used violence and intimidation to prevent Black citizens from voting.
The Voting Rights Act of 1965 ended many of these practices.
New voting procedures today continue to be debated in courts.
stem: The student is writing a history paper about voting rights in the United States. The student wants to give a concrete example of how Southern states obstructed Black voting after Reconstruction. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Although the Reconstruction amendments granted new rights, those rights were often undermined in practice.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Voting Rights Act of 1965 is widely regarded as one of the most important pieces of civil rights legislation in American history.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Historians continue to study how voter participation changed after major federal legislation was enacted.

choices.label: D
choices.text: State laws requiring poll taxes and literacy tests, along with grandfather clauses, made it nearly impossible for many Black citizens to cast a ballot.

explanation: The goal asks for a concrete example of obstruction after Reconstruction. Choice D names specific mechanisms from the notes, while the other choices are either vague or focus on later legal change.

notes: Coral polyps receive sugars produced by photosynthetic zooxanthellae living in their tissues.
The algae receive a protected environment and nutrients from the coral's waste.
Clownfish live within sea anemone tentacles and gain protection from predators.
The anemone is kept clean by the clownfish and may receive food scraps.
Cleaner shrimp remove parasites from fish at 'cleaning stations'.
stem: The student is writing a biology essay about symbiotic relationships in coral reef ecosystems. The student wants to illustrate mutualism—a relationship in which both organisms benefit—using a specific example. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Zooxanthellae use sunlight to produce sugars, which is why they are often described as microscopic algae.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In exchange for protection inside the anemone's stinging tentacles, the clownfish helps keep the anemone clean and may provide food scraps.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cleaner shrimp remove parasites from fish at cleaning stations, a behavior that is one of the most popular attractions for divers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Coral polyps receive sugars from zooxanthellae, showing that algae are essential to reef ecosystems.

explanation: Mutualism requires both organisms to benefit. Choice B explicitly describes benefits for both the clownfish and the anemone. The other choices focus on a single organism's gain or miss the required emphasis on mutual benefit.

notes: Renovation of the North Branch Library was completed in August.
Average weekly visitors increased from about 3,000 to 5,200 after the renovation.
Local small businesses contributed $80,000 toward a new technology center.
Participation in the library's after-school tutoring program doubled.
Library staff collaborated with schools to design the tutoring spaces.
stem: The city council is writing a report recommending that the renovation program be expanded to other branch libraries. Which sentence best uses the notes to emphasize that the renovated facilities were responsible for increased community engagement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Local businesses donated $80,000 to renovate the North Branch Library, and the branch now attracts 5,200 weekly visitors, so the renovation should be expanded to other branches.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because the renovation at North Branch included technology and tutoring spaces funded by local businesses, the branch saw weekly visits rise to 5,200 and after-school participation double, showing that improved facilities can directly boost community engagement.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The North Branch Library had 3,000 weekly visitors before renovation and 5,200 after, while local business donations made the new technology center possible and after-school participation doubled.

choices.label: D
choices.text: After the North Branch Library was renovated, average weekly visits rose to 5,200 and participation in tutoring doubled; in addition, local businesses donated $80,000 for the project.

explanation: Choice B is the only option that links the renovated facilities to the observed increases in visits and tutoring participation, rather than merely listing facts or implying that donations alone caused the change.

notes: EcoPack produces packaging made from mushroom roots.
Its material currently costs about 30 percent more than conventional foam.
The company expects unit costs to fall as production scales up.
A major shipping retailer has agreed to a one-year pilot using EcoPack boxes.
EcoPack's current facility can produce 2 million boxes per month.
stem: An article about sustainable packaging ends with a look at EcoPack's future. Which sentence best presents the company's main challenge while giving a concrete reason for optimism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Although EcoPack's packaging still costs 30 percent more than foam, the one-year pilot with a major shipping retailer suggests that its market can grow enough to lower costs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because EcoPack expects costs to drop as production scales, it has signed a one-year pilot agreement with a major shipping retailer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: EcoPack currently makes 2 million boxes per month at a 30 percent higher cost than foam, so the company will focus on increasing production.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The 30 percent cost premium is EcoPack's main challenge, but the company already produces 2 million boxes per month and will soon use mushroom roots.

explanation: Choice A is the only sentence that identifies the cost premium as the main challenge and offers the pilot agreement as a concrete reason for future cost reductions through growth.

notes: Clay tablets were excavated at the site of Tell Marid.
The tablets mostly list rations of barley and wheat.
Radiocarbon analysis dates the tablets to roughly 1200 BCE.
No large storage buildings have been found at the site.
Scholars disagree about whether the tablets show palace-controlled distribution or local exchange.
stem: A museum curator is writing a placard about the Tell Marid tablets. Which sentence best conveys the tablets' significance while acknowledging scholarly uncertainty?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Excavated at Tell Marid, clay tablets from around 1200 BCE list barley and wheat rations, proving that palace officials controlled grain distribution.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because no large storage buildings were found at Tell Marid, scholars now know that the clay tablets recording rations reflect local exchange rather than palatial control.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The clay tablets found at Tell Marid record rations of barley and wheat around 1200 BCE, but scholars are divided on whether the rations indicate centralized control or local exchange.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dated to roughly 1200 BCE, the Tell Marid tablets list barley and wheat rations, yet the absence of large storage buildings suggests they tell us little about economic life.

explanation: Choice C accurately reports the tablets' content and date while noting the scholarly disagreement, unlike the other choices which overstate certainty or draw unsupported conclusions.

notes: A common assumption is that urban noise harms birdsong and reduces bird populations.
Researchers studied great tits in noisy and quiet areas of the same city.
Birds in noisy areas produced songs with lower minimum frequencies.
These birds did not have lower reproductive success than birds in quiet areas.
The researchers concluded that some birds can adjust their songs to cope with noise.
stem: A science writer wants to introduce a summary of this research. Which sentence best presents the research as overturning a common assumption?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Researchers found that great tits in noisy areas sang at lower minimum frequencies, which challenges the assumption that urban noise necessarily reduces bird populations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because great tits in noisy areas produced songs with lower minimum frequencies, the common assumption that urban noise harms birdsong has been proven correct.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The assumption that urban noise harms birdsong has led researchers to study great tits, whose lower-frequency songs in noisy areas show why city birds have smaller populations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Although urban noise is commonly thought to harm birdsong, great tits in noisy areas sang at lower frequencies and reproduced just as successfully as birds in quiet areas, suggesting that the assumption is too simple.

explanation: Choice D directly contrasts the common assumption with the key findings—altered songs without a reproductive cost—making it the clearest introduction that presents the research as overturning that assumption.

notes: Installing dedicated bus rapid transit (BRT) lanes would cost about $12 million.
Dedicated BRT lanes can reduce average commute times by up to 25 percent.
Cities with dedicated BRT lanes report about 40 percent fewer bus-related accidents.
Projected maintenance costs for BRT are lower than for equivalent light rail over 20 years.
The mayor's priorities are improving road safety and reducing congestion.
stem: A city official is writing a statement in support of the BRT project. Which sentence best uses the notes to connect the project to the mayor's two stated priorities?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The BRT project deserves support because dedicated lanes reduce commute times by up to 25 percent and, unlike light rail, carry a lower twenty-year maintenance cost.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dedicated BRT lanes would meet the mayor's goals of improving safety and reducing congestion: cities with such lanes see about 40 percent fewer bus-related accidents and commutes up to 25 percent faster, all for a lower projected maintenance cost than light rail.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Although the BRT project would cost $12 million and reduce bus-related accidents by 40 percent, it would only slightly reduce commute times, so the city should study light rail instead.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Because BRT lanes can reduce average commute times by 25 percent and are cheaper to maintain than light rail, they would eliminate most bus-related accidents and congestion problems.

explanation: Choice B explicitly links both of the mayor's priorities—safety and congestion—to the relevant evidence from the notes, while also offering a cost advantage. The other choices omit at least one priority or overstate the project's effects.

notes: Study 1: In a controlled experiment, adults who slept 8 hours remembered 40% more word pairs than those who slept 4 hours.
Study 2: Across 12 high schools, students who averaged 8 or more hours of sleep had GPAs about 0.5 points higher than those averaging less than 7 hours.
Study 2 adjusted the GPA comparison for family income and time spent studying.
The high school study found an association, not proof that sleep caused the GPA difference.
stem: The student wants to use the notes to support the claim that getting more sleep can improve academic outcomes. Which sentence best accomplishes this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because the sleep study proved that sleep causes better memory, students ought to be forced to sleep at least eight hours a night.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The memory advantage found in the experiment and the higher GPAs among students who slept more suggest that additional sleep may help students do better in school.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The association between sleep and GPA disappears once family income and study time are taken into account.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Since some researchers worry about the cost of later school start times, the evidence about sleep and academic performance should be ignored.

explanation: Choice B carefully combines the experimental finding on memory with the observational GPA finding, using cautious language ('suggest that... may help') that matches the evidence. A overstates both the proof and the policy recommendation; C contradicts the notes, which say the GPA comparison was adjusted; D introduces an irrelevant concern about cost.

notes: EVs emit no tailpipe gases, but mining and manufacturing lithium batteries creates significant carbon emissions.
A lifecycle analysis shows that in regions powered largely by coal, an EV's overall emissions can be about the same as a hybrid car's emissions.
The same analysis finds that after about 20,000 miles driven, EVs emit less greenhouse gas than comparable gasoline cars.
Many states offer rebates for EV purchases.
stem: The student wants to qualify another debater's claim that electric vehicles are always cleaner than gasoline vehicles, without rejecting the claim entirely. Which sentence best accomplishes this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The debater's claim is false, because battery manufacturing and coal-powered electricity can make an EV just as polluting as a hybrid.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Government rebates for EV purchases show that policymakers believe electric vehicles are cleaner, so the claim is correct.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Although electric vehicles can have higher emissions during production and in coal-heavy regions, they generally become cleaner than gasoline cars after about 20,000 miles, so the original claim needs this qualification.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Because EVs have no tailpipe emissions, they are clearly cleaner than gasoline vehicles from the moment they enter the road.

explanation: Choice C preserves the debater's overall point while adding necessary conditions from the notes, which is exactly what qualifying means. A rejects the claim entirely; B relies on an irrelevant policy fact; D repeats the overly absolute claim the student wants to qualify.

notes: In the tutoring program, average reading scores of participating students rose by 12 percent in one year.
Membership at the center has grown from 300 to 900 households over the past five years.
In a recent survey, 94 percent of members said they would recommend the center to a neighbor.
The center has received grant applications from two other nonprofits for similar tutoring programs.
stem: The student wants to write a concluding sentence for a grant proposal that emphasizes the center's proven effectiveness and community support. Which sentence best accomplishes this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: With measurable literacy gains, growth in membership from 300 to 900 households, and strong endorsement from current members, the center has shown it is ready to expand its services.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because other nonprofits are applying for grants to copy the tutoring program, the center is the most successful organization in the state.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The 12 percent rise in reading scores proves that every student who completes the program will read at grade level.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The center's membership grew over five years, showing that community support has been increasing, though the tutoring program itself may not be effective.

explanation: Choice A directly combines the measured reading improvement, membership growth, and member endorsement to support the grant proposal's goal. B overstates the evidence ('most successful organization in the state'); C overgeneralizes test-score data; D contradicts the notes about the tutoring program's effectiveness.

notes: Study A found that adults living within 300 meters of a park had anxiety rates 25 percent lower than those living farther away, after controlling for income.
Study B found that in a city where violent crime had made parks unsafe, adults living near those same parks reported slightly higher stress levels.
Study A measured anxiety through clinical interviews; Study B used a brief self-report checklist.
Study A did not examine crime rates, and Study B did not control for income.
stem: The student wants to reconcile the two studies' conflicting findings about nearby parks and mental health. Which sentence best accomplishes this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Study A is more reliable than Study B because it controlled for income, so policymakers should focus only on building more parks.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The conflicting findings show that mental health is impossible to measure accurately.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The studies agree that parks affect mental health, so their different methods do not matter.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The conflicting results are likely due to context: a safe, accessible park may reduce anxiety, but a park perceived as dangerous could increase stress, and the two studies measured anxiety in different ways.

explanation: Choice D uses details from both studies to explain why their findings differ rather than dismissing one study. A rejects Study B and makes an unsupported policy claim; B overgeneralizes; C ignores the genuine disagreement between the results.

notes: Paperback sales at the publishing company stayed flat between 2021 and 2023.
Audiobook downloads rose from 50,000 to 120,000 per year over the same period.
In a customer survey, 70 percent of audiobook listeners bought another book in the same series.
Focus group participants said they liked audiobook narration and found listening convenient.
stem: The student wants to use quantitative and qualitative evidence to argue that audiobooks are the company's most promising growth area. Which sentence best accomplishes this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Flat paperback sales show that print is not growing, so the company should abandon print.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Audiobook downloads more than doubled while paperback sales stayed flat, and listeners praised the convenience, making audiobooks the company's clearest area of growth.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Because 70 percent of audiobook listeners bought another book in the same series, audiobooks are the only format that builds customer loyalty.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Focus group comments about audiobooks are encouraging, but without data on production costs, the company cannot determine which format sells best.

explanation: Choice B combines the strong sales growth, the flat print sales, and listener praise in one concise argument. A draws an extreme and unsupported conclusion; C overstates what the survey shows; D fails to take a position about audiobooks being the most promising growth area.

notes: A 2019 study in Portland compared green roofs with conventional roofs over a 12-month period.
Green roofs retained 62% of rainfall on average, while conventional roofs retained only 8%.
Retention rates were highest in summer (78%) and lowest in winter (43%).
Green roofs delayed peak stormwater runoff by up to 25 minutes during heavy storms.
City officials highlighted the flood-reduction benefits of green roofs, despite higher maintenance costs than conventional roofs.
stem: The student wants to emphasize the main environmental benefit of green roofs over conventional roofs using the evidence gathered. Which sentence best accomplishes this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because green roofs retained 62% of rainfall on average, compared with only 8% for conventional roofs, they can substantially reduce stormwater entering urban sewer systems.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Although green roofs cost more to maintain than conventional roofs, they are a worthwhile investment because they make cities more attractive.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Since green roofs retained 78% of summer rainfall but only 43% in winter, they are not effective at reducing stormwater in colder months.

choices.label: D
choices.text: City officials who emphasized flood reduction have proposed installing green roofs on every building in Portland.

explanation: Choice A directly uses the study's retention data to highlight the central environmental benefit: reducing stormwater runoff. The other choices either introduce unsupported claims, misinterpret the seasonal data, or overstate the officials' proposal.

notes: Roman harbor structures built with a type of concrete have survived for more than 2,000 years in seawater.
Modern concrete usually deteriorates in seawater within decades.
Researchers discovered aluminum tobermorite, a rare mineral, within the Roman concrete.
Aluminum tobermorite forms when seawater reacts with lime and volcanic ash, reinforcing the concrete.
Roman builders obtained volcanic ash from the Bay of Naples.
stem: The student wants to explain the primary cause of Roman concrete's unusual durability in seawater. Which sentence best does so?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Roman concrete is more durable than modern concrete because Roman builders used volcanic ash from the Bay of Naples.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The key to Roman concrete's longevity is aluminum tobermorite, a reinforcing mineral that forms when seawater interacts with the lime and volcanic ash in the concrete.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Roman concrete survived for 2,000 years, which proves that modern engineers should abandon conventional building materials.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Because aluminum tobermorite is a rare mineral, Roman concrete is more expensive to reproduce today than modern concrete.
