stem: A plant growing in a research lab increases in height linearly with time. At 2 weeks after the start of the study, the plant is 18 centimeters tall. At 10 weeks, it is 50 centimeters tall. Based on this linear model, how tall is the plant at 7 weeks?
explanation: The growth rate is \(\frac{50-18}{10-2}=4\) cm/week, so the height is modeled by \(h(t)=4t+10\). Thus \(h(7)=4(7)+10=38\).

stem: A freelance illustrator charges a flat project fee plus an hourly rate. A project that takes 5 hours costs $80, and a project that takes 12 hours costs $136. What is the flat project fee?
explanation: The hourly rate is \(\frac{136-80}{12-5}=8\), so the flat fee is \(80-5(8)=40\).

stem: A plumber charges a fixed visit fee plus a constant hourly rate. A 3-hour job costs \(\$215\), and a 7-hour job costs \(\$455\). What is the cost, in dollars, for an 8-hour job?
explanation: Let \(C(x)\) be the cost for \(x\) hours. The slope is \((455-215)/(7-3)=60\), so the hourly rate is \(\$60\). The fixed fee is \(215-3(60)=35\). Thus \(C(8)=60(8)+35=515\).

stem: A tutoring service charges a one-time registration fee plus a fixed amount per session. A student who attends 4 sessions pays \(\$210\), and a student who attends 9 sessions pays \(\$385\). What is the registration fee?
explanation: Let \(C(s)=ms+b\) be the total cost after \(s\) sessions. The slope is \((385-210)/(9-4)=35\), so each session costs \(\$35\). Then \(210=4(35)+b\), so \(b=70\). The registration fee is \(\$70\).

stem: A catering company charges a setup fee plus a constant amount per guest. A 100-guest event costs \(\$1,700\), and a 160-guest event costs \(\$2,360\). What is the cost, in dollars, for a 200-guest event?

A graphic designer charges a fixed project fee plus a constant hourly rate. A 5-hour project costs \(\$325\), and a 9-hour project costs \(\$485\). Which equation represents the total cost \(y\), in dollars, for a project that takes \(x\) hours?
explanation: The slope is \((485-325)/(9-5)=40\), so the hourly rate is \(\$40\). Then \(325=5(40)+b\), so \(b=125\). Therefore \(y=40x+125\).

stem: A charity fundraiser sells tickets to a dinner. The profit \(P\), in dollars, is a linear function of the number of tickets sold, \(x\). When 100 tickets are sold, the profit is \(\$400\); when 300 tickets are sold, the profit is \(\$1,600\). How many tickets must be sold for the profit to be \(\$2,500\)?
explanation: The slope is \((1600-400)/(300-100)=6\), so each ticket contributes \(\$6\) of profit. Using \(P=6x+b\), \(400=6(100)+b\), so \(b=-200\). Thus \(2500=6x-200\), which gives \(x=450\).

stem: A taxi company charges a flat pickup fee plus a constant rate per mile. A 5-mile trip costs \(\$14.50\), and a 9-mile trip costs \(\$22.50\). If the fare \(F(d)\) in dollars is a linear function of the trip distance \(d\) in miles, what is the fare for a 12-mile trip?

A cloud storage service charges a fixed account fee of \(\$3.00\) per month plus a constant amount per gigabyte stored. A customer who stores 50 gigabytes pays \(\$13.00\) in total for a month. Which function \(C(g)\) gives the total monthly cost, in dollars, for storing \(g\) gigabytes?
explanation: The cost per gigabyte is \(\frac{13.00-3.00}{50}=0.20\). Adding the fixed \(\$3.00\) monthly fee gives \(C(g)=0.20g+3.00\).

stem: The number of miles remaining on a road trip, \(R(t)\), is a linear function of the number of hours \(t\) driven. At the start of the trip, there are 350 miles remaining. After 4 hours of driving, there are 150 miles remaining. What is \(R(6)\), the number of miles remaining after 6 hours?

A gym charges a one-time initiation fee plus a constant monthly membership fee. Let \(A(m)\) be the total amount, in dollars, paid after \(m\) months of membership. If \(A(3)=240\) and \(A(7)=400\), what is the initiation fee?
explanation: The monthly membership fee is \(\frac{400-240}{7-3}=\$40\). Using \(A(3)=240\), the initiation fee is \(240-3(40)=\$120\).

stem: The height, in inches, of a burning candle is modeled by a linear function \(h(t)\), where \(t\) is the number of hours since the candle was lit. Initially the candle is 12 inches tall. After 5 hours, it is 7 inches tall. How many hours after being lit will the candle be 4 inches tall?
explanation: The height decreases at a rate of \(\frac{7-12}{5}=-1\) inch per hour, so \(h(t)=12-t\). Setting \(4=12-t\) gives \(t=8\).

stem: A moving company charges a flat pickup fee plus a constant rate per mile. A delivery of 60 miles costs \(\$210\), and a delivery of 150 miles costs \(\$390\). If a customer budgets \(\$280\), what is the maximum number of miles he can afford?

A cellular data plan charges a fixed monthly fee plus a constant rate per gigabyte of data. One month, a customer used 3 gigabytes and was billed \(\$48\). Another month, the customer used 8 gigabytes and was billed \(\$78\). What would the bill be for a month in which the customer uses 6 gigabytes?
explanation: The rate is \((78-48)/(8-3)=30/5=6\) dollars per gigabyte. The fixed fee is \(48-6(3)=30\), so 6 gigabytes costs \(30+6(6)=66\) dollars.

stem: A tutoring service charges an enrollment fee plus a constant hourly rate. After 4 hours, the total cost is \(\$220\). After 10 hours, the total cost is \(\$400\). What would the total cost be for 15 hours?
explanation: The hourly rate is \((400-220)/(10-4)=180/6=30\). The enrollment fee is \(220-30(4)=100\), so 15 hours costs \(30(15)+100=550\) dollars.

stem: A botanist measures the height of a plant each week. The height increases linearly. At the end of week 2, the plant is 8 centimeters tall; at the end of week 5, it is 17 centimeters tall. At the end of which week will the plant first be 20 centimeters tall?
explanation: The growth rate is \((17-8)/(5-2)=9/3=3\) cm per week, and the height at week 0 is \(8-3(2)=2\). Thus \(h=3w+2\). Set \(3w+2=20\), giving \(w=6\).

stem: A taxi company charges an initial fare of \(\$2.50\) plus \(\$1.80\) per mile. Which equation models the total fare \(y\), in dollars, for a trip of \(x\) miles?
explanation: The per-mile charge is the slope, \(1.8\), and the initial fare is the \(y\)-intercept, \(2.5\). Therefore, \(y=1.8x+2.5\).

stem: A delivery service charges a flat pickup fee plus a constant rate per mile traveled. A 10-mile delivery costs \( \$32.00 \), and a 25-mile delivery costs \( \$57.50 \). What is the flat pickup fee?
explanation: Let \(F\) be the flat fee and \(r\) be the rate. The cost difference \(57.50-32.00=25.50\) corresponds to \(25-10=15\) miles, so \(r=25.50/15=1.70\). Then \(F=32.00-10(1.70)=15.00\).

stem: A cell phone plan charges a fixed monthly access fee plus a constant rate per minute of use. A customer who uses 120 minutes in a month pays \( \$42.60 \), and a customer who uses 300 minutes in the same month pays \( \$57.00 \). What is the per-minute charge?
explanation: The additional cost for \(300-120=180\) minutes is \(57.00-42.60=\$14.40\), so the per-minute rate is \(14.40/180=0.08\) dollars.

stem: A plumber charges a fixed service-call fee plus an hourly rate. A 2-hour repair costs \( \$145 \), and a 5-hour repair costs \( \$310 \). What is the plumber's hourly rate?
explanation: The cost increases by \(310-145=\$165\) when the time increases by \(5-2=3\) hours. Thus the hourly rate is \(165/3=\$55\) per hour.

stem: A gym charges a one-time enrollment fee plus a fixed monthly membership fee. After 3 months, a new member has paid \( \$180 \). After 8 months, the member has paid \( \$330 \). What is the one-time enrollment fee?
explanation: The monthly fee is \((330-180)/(8-3)=150/5=\$30\). The enrollment fee is therefore \(180-3(30)=\$90\).

stem: A candle burns at a constant rate. At 1 hour after being lit, the candle is 9 inches tall. At 4 hours after being lit, it is 6 inches tall. What was the candle's original height?
explanation: The height decreases by \(9-6=3\) inches over \(4-1=3\) hours, so the burn rate is \(1\) inch per hour. At 1 hour it has burned 1 inch from its original height, so the original height is \(9+1=10\) inches.

stem: An environmental cleanup crew removes litter from a beach at a constant rate. At 9:00 A.M. there are 740 pounds of litter on the beach. After 3 hours of cleanup, at noon, there are 560 pounds remaining. At what constant rate, in pounds per hour, is litter being removed?
explanation: The crew removed \(740 - 560 = 180\) pounds in 3 hours, so the rate is \(180 \div 3 = 60\) pounds per hour.

stem: A phone company charges a one-time activation fee and a fixed monthly fee. Jada paid \(\$270\) in total for 6 months, and \(\$390\) in total for 10 months. What is the fixed monthly fee?
explanation: The difference in total cost is \(390 - 270 = 120\) dollars, which covers \(10 - 6 = 4\) months of service. Thus the monthly fee is \(120 \div 4 = 30\) dollars.

stem: The value of a coin collection depreciates linearly. The collection was worth \(\$1,200\) when first appraised 5 years ago. Its value now is \(\$800\). If this depreciation continues at the same constant rate, which function \(V(y)\) gives the value of the collection \(y\) years after the initial appraisal?
explanation: The value decreased \(1200 - 800 = 400\) dollars over 5 years, so the annual rate is \(400 \div 5 = 80\) dollars per year. At \(y=0\) the value is \(1200\), so \(V(y)=1200-80y\).

stem: A taxi company charges a flat pick-up fee plus a constant per-mile rate. A 7-mile ride costs \(\$14.60\), and a 12-mile ride costs \(\$21.10\). What is the flat pick-up fee?
explanation: The extra 5 miles cost \(21.10 - 14.60 = 6.50\) dollars, so the per-mile rate is \(6.50 \div 5 = 1.30\) dollars. The flat fee is \(14.60 - 7(1.30) = 14.60 - 9.10 = 5.50\) dollars.

stem: During a severe storm, the water level in a reservoir rises at a constant rate. At 2:00 P.M. the water level is 6.4 feet, and at 5:00 P.M. it is 8.8 feet. How many hours after 2:00 P.M. will the water level reach 11.2 feet, assuming the same rate continues?
explanation: In 3 hours the level rises \(8.8 - 6.4 = 2.4\) feet, so the rate is \(2.4 \div 3 = 0.8\) feet per hour. To rise from 6.4 to 11.2 feet requires \(11.2 - 6.4 = 4.8\) feet, so the time is \(4.8 \div 0.8 = 6\) hours after 2:00 P.M.

stem: A courier company charges a one-time account setup fee plus a constant amount per package delivered. The total charge for delivering 120 packages is \(\$350\), and the total charge for delivering 200 packages is \(\$510\). What is the company's charge per package, in dollars?
explanation: The charge per package is the slope of the linear relationship: \(\frac{510-350}{200-120}=\frac{160}{80}=2\). So the company charges \(\$2.00\) per package.

stem: A cell phone plan charges a fixed monthly fee plus a constant rate per minute used. One month, a customer used 300 minutes and was billed \(\$55\). Another month, the same customer used 700 minutes and was billed \(\$95\). What is the fixed monthly fee, in dollars?
explanation: The per-minute rate is the slope: \(\frac{95-55}{700-300}=\frac{40}{400}=0.10\) dollars per minute. Using \(\text{total}=0.10m+b\), \(55=0.10(300)+b\), so \(b=25\). The fixed monthly fee is \(\$25\).

stem: A craft vendor's total cost to produce 40 candles is \(\$225\), and the total cost to produce 90 candles is \(\$375\). She sells each candle for \(\$10\). How many candles must she sell to break even?
explanation: The variable cost per candle is \(\frac{375-225}{90-40}=\frac{150}{50}=3\). The fixed cost is \(225-3(40)=105\). Break-even occurs when revenue equals cost: \(10x=3x+105\), so \(7x=105\) and \(x=15\).

stem: A water tank starts with 120 gallons and loses water at a constant rate. At 3:00 PM, 3 hours later, it contains 36 gallons. Which equation represents the number of gallons \(g\) in the tank \(t\) hours after noon?
explanation: The rate of change is \(\frac{36-120}{3}=\frac{-84}{3}=-28\) gallons per hour. Thus the amount after \(t\) hours is \(g=120-28t\).

stem: A taxi company charges an initial fee plus a constant charge of \(\$2.50\) per mile. A 6-mile ride costs \(\$21.00\). What is the initial fee, in dollars?
explanation: The mileage charge is \(6 \times 2.50 = 15\). Since the total fare is \(21\), the initial fee is \(21-15=6\) dollars.

stem: A printing company charges a one-time setup fee plus a constant amount for each poster printed. The total cost for 200 posters is \(\$260\), and the total cost for 500 posters is \(\$440\). What is the total cost, in dollars, to print 800 posters?

A swimming pool is being filled with water at a constant rate. At 1:00 P.M. the water is 3 feet deep. At 1:30 P.M. the water is 3.75 feet deep. At this rate, how deep, in feet, will the water be at 2:00 P.M.?
explanation: The depth increases by \(3.75-3=0.75\) feet in 0.5 hour, so the rate is \(1.5\) feet per hour. From 1:00 P.M. to 2:00 P.M. is 1 hour, so the depth is \(3+1.5=4.5\) feet.

stem: A candle is burning at a constant rate. At 7:00 P.M. the candle is 12 inches tall, and at 9:00 P.M. it is 8.4 inches tall. If the candle continues to burn at the same rate, how many hours after 7:00 P.M. will the candle be completely burned?
explanation: From 7:00 P.M. to 9:00 P.M., the candle loses \(12-8.4=3.6\) inches in 2 hours, so it burns at \(1.8\) inches per hour. Time to burn all \(12\) inches is \(\frac{12}{1.8}=\frac{20}{3}\) hours.

stem: A courier service charges a flat daily fee plus a constant rate for each mile driven. On Monday, a driver is charged \(\$96\) for driving 120 miles. On Tuesday, the same driver is charged \(\$132\) for driving 180 miles. What is the flat daily fee, in dollars?
explanation: The rate per mile is \(\frac{132-96}{180-120}=\frac{36}{60}=0.60\) dollars per mile. The flat fee is therefore \(96-120(0.60)=96-72=24\) dollars.

stem: A meal-kit delivery service charges an enrollment fee plus a constant weekly subscription fee. A 4-week subscription costs \(\$180\), and a 7-week subscription costs \(\$270\). What is the weekly subscription fee, in dollars?
explanation: Let total cost \(C(w)=mw+b\). From 4 to 7 weeks, cost increases by \(270-180=90\) dollars over 3 weeks, so \(m=\frac{90}{3}=30\) dollars per week.

stem: A courier service charges a flat pickup fee plus a constant amount per mile. A 10-mile delivery costs \(\$35\), and a 30-mile delivery costs \(\$75\). What would a 25-mile delivery cost, in dollars?

A phone company charges a flat monthly fee plus a constant amount per minute of usage. The bill for 120 minutes of usage is \(\$45\), and the bill for 300 minutes of usage is \(\$69\). If the monthly bill is modeled by \(B(m)=rm+b\), what is the value of \(b\), the flat monthly fee?

A gym charges an initiation fee plus a fixed monthly fee. A member who stays for 6 months pays a total of \(\$180\). A member who stays for 15 months pays a total of \(\$360\). What is the fixed monthly fee, in dollars?
explanation: Let total cost be \(T(n)=f+rn\), where \(n\) is months. The slope is \(r=\frac{360-180}{15-6}=\frac{180}{9}=20\), so the fixed monthly fee is \(\$20\).

stem: A candle burns at a constant rate. One hour after being lit, the candle is 11 inches tall. Four hours after being lit, it is 5 inches tall. What was the height of the candle, in inches, when it was lit?
explanation: Let \(H(t)=b+rt\), where \(t\) is hours after being lit. The slope is \(r=\frac{5-11}{4-1}=-2\). Then \(11=b+(-2)(1)\), so \(b=13\).

stem: A taxi ride costs an initial charge plus a fixed amount per mile. A 3-mile ride costs \(\$11.50\), and a 7-mile ride costs \(\$19.50\). If the fare is modeled by \(F(m)=a+bm\), what is the value of \(a\), the initial charge, in dollars?

A print shop charges a one-time setup fee plus a constant cost per shirt for a custom order. The total cost for an order of 200 shirts is \(\$650\), and the total cost for an order of 350 shirts is \(\$875\). What is the setup fee?
explanation: The cost per shirt is the slope: \((875-650)/(350-200)=225/150=1.5\). Then the setup fee is \(650-200(1.5)=350\).

stem: A museum’s cumulative attendance since a new exhibit opened consists of the opening-day attendance plus a constant number of additional visitors each day. After 4 days, total attendance was \(12{,}000\); after 12 days, total attendance was \(21{,}600\). What is the constant number of additional visitors per day?
explanation: The total attendance is linear in days, so the constant number of additional visitors per day is the slope: \((21{,}600-12{,}000)/(12-4)=9{,}600/8=1{,}200\).

stem: A courier charges a flat pickup fee plus a constant rate per pound. Shipping a 10-pound package costs \(\$32.00\), and shipping a 25-pound package costs \(\$57.50\). What is the cost of shipping a 40-pound package?
A plumber charges a fixed visit fee plus a constant hourly labor rate. The charge for a 2-hour job is \(\$165\), and the charge for a 5-hour job is \(\$285\). What is the charge for a 7-hour job?

A silo is being emptied at a constant rate. After 3 hours of emptying, \(1{,}250\) bushels of grain remain; after 7 hours, \(850\) bushels remain. How many bushels of grain had been removed after 5 hours of emptying?
explanation: The remaining grain decreases at \((1{,}250-850)/(7-3)=100\) bushels per hour, so the initial amount was \(1{,}250+3(100)=1{,}550\). After 5 hours, \(5(100)=500\) bushels had been removed.

stem: A moving company charges a flat travel fee plus a constant rate per mile. A 12-mile move costs \(\$156\), and a 20-mile move costs \(\$220\). What is the company's rate per mile, in dollars per mile?
explanation: The rate per mile is the slope: \(\frac{220-156}{20-12}=\frac{64}{8}=8\).

stem: A gym charges a one-time enrollment fee plus a fixed monthly membership fee. A member who stays 3 months pays \(\$180\) total, and a member who stays 7 months pays \(\$300\) total. If the total payment is a linear function of the number of months, what is the monthly membership fee, in dollars?
explanation: The monthly fee is the slope: \(\frac{300-180}{7-3}=30\). The one-time fee is \(180-3(30)=90\), so the model is \(y=30m+90\).

stem: The height of a burning candle decreases at a constant rate. At 20 minutes after it is lit, the candle is 12 centimeters tall; at 50 minutes after it is lit, it is 6 centimeters tall. What is the height of the candle, in centimeters, 65 minutes after it is lit?
In a certain city, a taxi charges an initial fee plus a constant amount per mile. A 6-mile trip costs \(\$14.80\), and a 10-mile trip costs \(\$20.00\). What is the initial fee, in dollars?
explanation: The rate per mile is \(\frac{20.00-14.80}{10-6}=1.30\). Using the 6-mile trip, the initial fee is \(14.80-6(1.30)=7.00\).

stem: A DJ charges a booking fee plus a constant hourly rate. For a 2-hour event, the total charge is \(\$260\); for a 5-hour event, it is \(\$500\). What is the booking fee, in dollars?
explanation: The hourly rate is \(\frac{500-260}{5-2}=80\). The booking fee is \(260-2(80)=100\).

stem: An electrician charges a fixed service call fee plus an hourly labor rate. For a job that takes 3 hours, the total cost is $145. For a job that takes 6 hours, the total cost is $250. Which function gives the total cost \(C\), in dollars, for a job that takes \(h\) hours?
explanation: The slope is \(\frac{250-145}{6-3}=35\) dollars per hour. The \(C\)-intercept is \(145 - 3(35)=40\), so \(C(h)=35h+40\).

stem: A delivery company charges a flat pickup fee and a constant price per pound shipped. Shipping a 5-pound package costs $23.50, and shipping a 9-pound package costs $33.50. What is the flat pickup fee, in dollars?
explanation: Let \(F\) be the flat fee and \(p\) the price per pound. Then \(F+5p=23.50\) and \(F+9p=33.50\). Subtracting gives \(4p=10\), so \(p=2.50\). Thus \(F=23.50-5(2.50)=11.00\).

stem: A fitness trainer charges an initial consultation fee plus a fixed rate per session. After 4 sessions, a client has paid $310 total. After 10 sessions, the client has paid $580 total. What is the initial consultation fee, in dollars?
explanation: Let \(F\) be the initial fee and \(r\) the rate per session. Then \(F+4r=310\) and \(F+10r=580\). Subtracting gives \(6r=270\), so \(r=45\). Therefore \(F=310-4(45)=130\).

stem: A small business's profit from selling \(x\) items is modeled by a linear function. When the company sells 10 items, the profit is \(-\$150\) (a loss). When it sells 50 items, the profit is \(\$250\). What is the meaning of the slope of this linear function?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The profit increases by \(\$10\) for each item sold.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The profit increases by \(\$20\) for each item sold.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The initial profit at zero items sold is \(-\$150\).

choices.label: D
choices.text: The profit decreases by \(\$10\) for each item sold.

explanation: The slope is \(\frac{250-(-150)}{50-10}=\frac{400}{40}=10\), so the profit increases by \(\$10\) per item sold.

stem: A phone plan charges a constant amount per minute after a monthly base fee. One month, 120 minutes of calls cost $54. The next month, 200 minutes cost $74. Which equation represents the monthly cost \(C\), in dollars, as a function of the number of minutes \(m\) used?

A data plan charges a flat monthly fee plus a constant rate per gigabyte of data used. In June, a customer used 5 gigabytes and was billed \$75. In July, the customer used 8 gigabytes and was billed \$96. At this rate, how many gigabytes would the customer have to use in a month for the bill to be \$110?
explanation: The rate is \(\frac{96-75}{8-5}=\frac{21}{3}=7\) dollars per gigabyte. The flat fee is \(75-5(7)=40\). Thus \(110=40+7g\), so \(g=10\).

stem: A car rental agency charges a fixed fee plus a constant amount for each mile driven. A 100-mile trip costs \$145, and a 250-mile trip costs \$220. What is the total cost, in dollars, for a 400-mile trip?
explanation: The rate is \(\frac{220-145}{250-100}=\frac{75}{150}=0.5\) dollars per mile. The fixed fee is \(145-100(0.5)=95\), so the cost is \(C=0.5m+95\). For 400 miles, \(C=0.5(400)+95=295\).

stem: A bakery models its daily profit \(P\), in dollars, from selling \(n\) cookies using the equation \(P = 0.75n - 12\). What is the best interpretation of the number \(0.75\) in this equation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The bakery pays \$0.75 per day in fixed costs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The bakery must sell 0.75 cookies before it earns any profit.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Each additional cookie sold increases the daily profit by \$0.75.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The bakery sells 0.75 cookies for each dollar of daily profit.

explanation: In \(P=0.75n-12\), the coefficient \(0.75\) is the slope, so it represents the rate at which profit increases per cookie sold: each additional cookie increases the daily profit by \$0.75.

stem: Two water tanks are draining at constant rates. Tank A initially contains 800 liters and loses 10 liters per minute. Tank B initially contains 1150 liters and loses 5 liters per minute. After how many minutes will Tank B contain exactly twice as much water as Tank A?
explanation: Let \(t\) be the number of minutes. The tank amounts are \(A=800-10t\) and \(B=1150-5t\). Setting \(B=2A\) gives \(1150-5t=2(800-10t)=1600-20t\). Thus \(15t=450\), so \(t=30\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{(x^3 y^{-2})^2}{x^4 y^{-5}}\) for \(x\neq 0\) and \(y\neq 0\)?
explanation: Simplify the numerator: \((x^3y^{-2})^2=x^6y^{-4}\). Dividing by \(x^4y^{-5}\) subtracts exponents: \(x^{6-4}y^{-4-(-5)}=x^2y\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\left(\frac{2x^2}{y^3}\right)^{-2}\) for \(x\neq 0\) and \(y\neq 0\)?
explanation: Apply the negative exponent: \(\left(\frac{2x^2}{y^3}\right)^{-2}=\left(\frac{y^3}{2x^2}\right)^2=\frac{y^6}{4x^4}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\sqrt{x^3\sqrt{x}}\) for \(x>0\)?
explanation: Rewrite \(\sqrt{x}\) as \(x^{1/2}\), so \(x^3\sqrt{x}=x^{7/2}\). Taking the square root gives \((x^{7/2})^{1/2}=x^{7/4}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \((x^{1/2}+x^{1/3})(x^{1/2}-x^{1/3})\) for \(x>0\)?
explanation: Using the difference of squares, \((x^{1/2})^2-(x^{1/3})^2=x-x^{2/3}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{\sqrt[4]{x^3}}{\sqrt[3]{x^2}}\) for \(x>0\)?
Which expression is equivalent to \(\left(\frac{x^3 y^{-2}}{x^{-1} y^4}\right)^{-2}\), where \(x>0\) and \(y>0\)?
explanation: Simplify inside the parentheses first: \(x^{3-(-1)}y^{-2-4}=x^4y^{-6}\). Then raise to the \(-2\) power: \(x^{-8}y^{12}=\frac{y^{12}}{x^8}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{8^{x+1}}{2^{3x-2}}\)?
Which expression is equivalent to \(\left(\frac{a^{-2} b^3}{a^4 b^{-1}}\right)^{-1}\), where \(a\neq 0\) and \(b\neq 0\)?
explanation: Inside the parentheses: \(a^{-2-4}b^{3-(-1)}=a^{-6}b^4\). Raising to the \(-1\) power gives \(a^6b^{-4}=\frac{a^6}{b^4}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(2^{x+2}+2^{2x}\)?
explanation: By exponent rules, \(2^{x+2}=2^x\cdot 2^2=4(2^x)\) and \(2^{2x}=(2^x)^2\). Thus the equivalent expression is \(4(2^x)+(2^x)^2\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{x^{-2} y^{3} z^{-1}}{x^{4} y^{-2} z^{5}}\), where \(x\), \(y\), and \(z\) are nonzero?
explanation: Subtract exponents for each base: \(x^{-2-4}=x^{-6}\), \(y^{3-(-2)}=y^5\), and \(z^{-1-5}=z^{-6}\). The result is \(x^{-6}y^5z^{-6}=\frac{y^5}{x^6z^6}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{x^{\frac{3}{2}}y^{-2}}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}y^{-1}}\), where \(x>0\) and \(y>0\)?
explanation: Use the quotient rule for exponents: subtract exponents with the same base. \(x^{\frac{3}{2}} \div x^{\frac{1}{2}} = x^1\), and \(y^{-2} \div y^{-1} = y^{-1}\). Thus the expression simplifies to \(\frac{x}{y}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{(4x^2)^3}{(16x^3)^2}\), where \(x \neq 0\)?
explanation: Simplify the numerator and denominator: \((4x^2)^3 = 64x^6\) and \((16x^3)^2 = 256x^6\). Since \(\frac{64x^6}{256x^6} = \frac{1}{4}\), the expression is equivalent to \(\frac{1}{4}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{8^{x+2}}{2^{3x-1}}\)?

explanation: Factor the numerator as \((x-3)(x+3)\) and the denominator as \((x-3)^2\). Cancel the common factor \(x-3\) to obtain \(\frac{x+3}{x-3}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{x^{-1}+y^{-1}}{x^{-2}-y^{-2}}\), where \(x\), \(y\), \(x+y\), and \(y-x\) are all nonzero?
explanation: Rewrite using positive exponents: \(\frac{\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}}{\frac{1}{x^2}-\frac{1}{y^2}}\). The numerator is \(\frac{x+y}{xy}\) and the denominator is \(\frac{y^2-x^2}{x^2y^2}=\frac{(y-x)(y+x)}{x^2y^2}\). Thus the expression becomes \(\frac{x+y}{xy} \cdot \frac{x^2y^2}{(y-x)(x+y)} = \frac{xy}{y-x}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{6x^3 y^{-2}}{2x^{-1} y^5}\), where \(x\neq 0\) and \(y\neq 0\)?
explanation: Divide the coefficients: \(6/2=3\). Subtract exponents: \(x^{3-(-1)}=x^4\) and \(y^{-2-5}=y^{-7}\). Thus \(\frac{6x^3 y^{-2}}{2x^{-1} y^5}=\frac{3x^4}{y^7}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \((2x^2 y^3)^2(4x y^{-2})^{-1}\), where \(x\neq 0\) and \(y\neq 0\)?
Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{(3x^4)^2}{(x^{-1})^3}\), where \(x\neq 0\)?
explanation: Simplify numerator and denominator: \((3x^4)^2=9x^8\) and \((x^{-1})^3=x^{-3}\). Dividing gives \(\frac{9x^8}{x^{-3}}=9x^{8-(-3)}=9x^{11}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\sqrt[4]{x^3}\sqrt{x^5}\), where \(x\ge 0\)?
explanation: Rewrite the radicals as powers: \(\sqrt[4]{x^3}=x^{3/4}\) and \(\sqrt{x^5}=x^{5/2}\). Adding exponents gives \(x^{3/4+5/2}=x^{3/4+10/4}=x^{13/4}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{(x^{1/2}x^{-2})^3}{(x^{-3})^2}\), where \(x>0\)?
explanation: Inside the numerator, \(x^{1/2}x^{-2}=x^{-3/2}\), so the numerator is \((x^{-3/2})^3=x^{-9/2}\). The denominator is \((x^{-3})^2=x^{-6}\). Dividing gives \(x^{-9/2-(-6)}=x^{3/2}\).

stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(\frac{12a^3b^{-2}}{4a^{-1}b^4}\)?
explanation: Divide coefficients: \(12/4=3\). For \(a\), subtract exponents: \(3-(-1)=4\). For \(b\), \(-2-4=-6\), so the result is \(3a^4b^{-6}=\frac{3a^4}{b^6}\).

stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(\left(\frac{x^{2/3}y^{-3/4}}{x^{-1/3}y^{1/4}}\right)^8\)?
explanation: Simplify inside the parentheses first: \(x^{2/3-(-1/3)}=x\), \(y^{-3/4-1/4}=y^{-1}\). Then raising to the 8th power gives \(x^8y^{-8}\).

stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(\frac{18m^4n^{-3}p^2}{6m^{-2}np^{-3}}\)?
explanation: Divide coefficients: \(18/6=3\). Subtract exponents: \(m^{4-(-2)}=m^6\), \(n^{-3-1}=n^{-4}\), and \(p^{2-(-3)}=p^5\). The equivalent expression is \(3m^6n^{-4}p^5\).

stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \((3^{2x+1})^2 \cdot 9^{x-3}\)?
Which of the following is equivalent to \(\left(\frac{16a^8b^{-4}}{a^4b^2}\right)^{1/4}\)?
explanation: Simplify inside the radical: \(16a^{8-4}b^{-4-2}=16a^4b^{-6}\). Taking the fourth root gives \(16^{1/4}a^{4/4}b^{-6/4}=2ab^{-3/2}\).

stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(\frac{12x^4 y^{-2}}{3x^{-2} y^5}\), where \(x \neq 0\) and \(y \neq 0\)?
explanation: Simplify the fraction: \(\frac{12}{3}=4\), \(x^{4-(-2)}=x^6\), and \(y^{-2-5}=y^{-7}\). Thus the expression is \(4x^6 y^{-7}=\frac{4x^6}{y^7}\).

stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \((x^{2/3} y^{-1/2})^{-3}\), where \(x > 0\) and \(y > 0\)?
Which of the following is equivalent to \(\frac{\sqrt{x} \cdot \sqrt[4]{x^3}}{x^{-1/2}}\), where \(x > 0\)?
explanation: Rewrite as powers of \(x\): \(\sqrt{x}=x^{1/2}\), \(\sqrt[4]{x^3}=x^{3/4}\), and \(x^{-1/2}\) in the denominator becomes \(x^{1/2}\) when moved to the numerator. So the exponent is \(\frac12 + \frac34 + \frac12 = \frac74\).

stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(\left(\frac{2x^3 y^{-2}}{4x^{-1} y^2}\right)^{-2}\), where \(x \neq 0\) and \(y \neq 0\)?
explanation: First simplify inside: \(\frac{2x^3 y^{-2}}{4x^{-1} y^2} = \frac12 x^{3-(-1)} y^{-2-2} = \frac12 x^4 y^{-4}\). Raising to \(-2\) gives \(\left(\frac12\right)^{-2} x^{-8} y^8 = 4x^{-8} y^8 = \frac{4y^8}{x^8}\).

stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(\frac{3x^2 y^{-3}}{6x^{-4} y^{-1}} \cdot (2xy^2)^{-1}\), where \(x \neq 0\) and \(y \neq 0\)?
explanation: The first factor simplifies to \(\frac{3}{6} x^{2-(-4)} y^{-3-(-1)} = \frac12 x^6 y^{-2}\). The second factor is \((2xy^2)^{-1} = \frac12 x^{-1} y^{-2}\). Their product is \(\frac14 x^{5} y^{-4} = \frac{x^5}{4y^4}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \((x^{-2} y^{3} z^{0})^{-3}\), where \(x\), \(y\), and \(z\) are nonzero real numbers?
explanation: Distribute the exponent \(-3\): \(x^{6} y^{-9} z^{0}\). Since \(z^0 = 1\), rewrite the negative exponent as a denominator: \(\frac{x^6}{y^9}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{x^2 - 4}{x^2 - 3x + 2}\), where \(x \neq 1\) and \(x \neq 2\)?
explanation: Factor the numerator as \((x-2)(x+2)\) and the denominator as \((x-1)(x-2)\). Canceling the common factor \(x-2\) gives \(\frac{x+2}{x-1}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\sqrt[3]{x^6 y^3} \cdot y^{-1/2}\), where \(x>0\) and \(y>0\)?
explanation: The cube root gives \(x^{6/3} y^{3/3} = x^2 y\). Multiplying by \(y^{-1/2}\) gives \(x^2 y^{1 - 1/2} = x^2 y^{1/2}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \((4x^{3}y^{-2})^{-2}(2x^{-1}y)^3\), where \(x \neq 0\) and \(y \neq 0\)?
Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{2}{x+1}+\frac{3}{x-1}\), where \(x \neq -1\) and \(x \neq 1\)?
explanation: Use the common denominator \((x+1)(x-1) = x^2-1\). The numerator is \(2(x-1)+3(x+1) = 5x+1\), so the equivalent expression is \(\frac{5x+1}{x^2-1}\).

stem: For \(x>0\), which of the following is equivalent to \(\left(\frac{x^{2/3}}{x^{1/4}}\right)^{-3}\)?
explanation: Simplify inside the parentheses first: \(\frac{x^{2/3}}{x^{1/4}} = x^{2/3 - 1/4} = x^{5/12}\). Then raise to the power \(-3\): \(\left(x^{5/12}\right)^{-3} = x^{-15/12} = x^{-5/4}\).

stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(\frac{2}{x-3}+\frac{1}{x+2}\) for \(x\neq -2,3\)?
explanation: Use the common denominator \((x-3)(x+2)=x^2-x-6\). Then \(\frac{2}{x-3}+\frac{1}{x+2}=\frac{2(x+2)+(x-3)}{x^2-x-6}=\frac{3x+1}{x^2-x-6}\).

stem: For \(x\neq 0\) and \(y\neq 0\), which of the following is equivalent to \((2x^3 y^{-2})^{-2}\)?

Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{2x^3 y^{-2}}{4x^{-1} y^4}\), where \(x\neq 0\) and \(y\neq 0\)?
explanation: Simplify the coefficients and subtract exponents: \(\frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}\), \(x^{3-(-1)} = x^4\), and \(y^{-2-4} = y^{-6}\). Thus \(\frac{1}{2}x^4y^{-6} = \frac{x^4}{2y^6}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\sqrt[3]{27x^9 y^6}\), where \(x\) and \(y\) are real numbers?
explanation: The cube root of \(27\) is \(3\). For exponents, divide by 3: \(x^{9/3}=x^3\) and \(y^{6/3}=y^2\). Therefore \(\sqrt[3]{27x^9y^6} = 3x^3y^2\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \((2x-3)^2 - (x+1)(x-5)\)?
Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{x^2-4}{x^2-3x+2} \cdot \frac{x-2}{x+2}\), where \(x\neq 1\) and \(x\neq \pm 2\)?
explanation: Factor: \(x^2-4=(x-2)(x+2)\) and \(x^2-3x+2=(x-1)(x-2)\). The expression becomes \(\frac{(x-2)(x+2)}{(x-1)(x-2)} \cdot \frac{x-2}{x+2} = \frac{x+2}{x-1} \cdot \frac{x-2}{x+2} = \frac{x-2}{x-1}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\left(\frac{4a^2 b^{-3}}{2a^{-1} b^2}\right)^{-2}\), where \(a\neq 0\) and \(b\neq 0\)?
explanation: Simplify inside the parentheses: \(\frac{4}{2}=2\), \(a^{2-(-1)}=a^3\), and \(b^{-3-2}=b^{-5}\). So the base is \(2a^3b^{-5}\). Raising to \(-2\) gives \(2^{-2}a^{-6}b^{10} = \frac{b^{10}}{4a^6}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{(2x^3y^{-2})^4}{(4x^2y^{-3})^2}\)?
explanation: The numerator is \(16x^{12}y^{-8}\) and the denominator is \(16x^4y^{-6}\). Dividing gives \(x^{12-4}y^{-8-(-6)}=x^8y^{-2}=\frac{x^8}{y^2}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{2x^2+5x-3}{x^2+2x-3}\), for \(x\neq -3\) and \(x\neq 1\)?
explanation: Factor the numerator as \((2x-1)(x+3)\) and the denominator as \((x+3)(x-1)\). Canceling \(x+3\) leaves \(\frac{2x-1}{x-1}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{\left(x^{2/3}y^{-1/4}\right)^6}{\left(x^{1/2}y^{3/4}\right)^{-4}}\)?
explanation: The numerator is \(x^{4}y^{-3/2}\). The denominator is \(x^{-2}y^{-3}\). Dividing gives \(x^{4-(-2)}y^{-3/2-(-3)}=x^6y^{3/2}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{4^{n+1}\cdot 8^{2n-1}}{16^{n-2}}\)?

explanation: Factor each polynomial: \(x^2-9=(x-3)(x+3)\), \(x^2-2x-3=(x-3)(x+1)\), \(x^2-1=(x-1)(x+1)\), and \(x^2+4x+3=(x+1)(x+3)\). Canceling common factors gives \(\frac{x+3}{x+1} \cdot \frac{x-1}{x+3} = \frac{x-1}{x+1}\).

stem: If \(a > 0\) and \(b > 0\), which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{\left(a^{3/2} b^{1/3}\right)^4}{\left(a^2 b^{1/2}\right)^3}\)?
explanation: The numerator is \(a^6 b^{4/3}\) and the denominator is \(a^6 b^{3/2}\). The \(a\)-terms cancel, leaving \(b^{4/3-3/2}=b^{-1/6}=\frac{1}{\sqrt[6]{b}}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \((x^2+3x+2)(x^2-2x+1) - (x+1)^2(x-1)^2\)?
If \(x > 0\), which expression is equivalent to \(\sqrt{x^3} + \sqrt[3]{x^6}\)?
If \(x\) and \(y\) are nonzero and \(x+y \neq 0\), which expression is equivalent to \((x^{-1}+y^{-1})^{-1}\)?
explanation: Since \(x^{-1}+y^{-1}=\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}=\frac{x+y}{xy}\), taking the reciprocal gives \(\frac{xy}{x+y}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{(a^{2/3} b^{-1/2})^{-3}}{a^{1/2} b^{2}}\) ?
explanation: Simplify the numerator: \((a^{2/3} b^{-1/2})^{-3} = a^{-2} b^{3/2}\). Then divide by \(a^{1/2} b^{2}\), subtracting exponents: \(a^{-5/2} b^{-1/2} = \frac{1}{a^{5/2} b^{1/2}}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \((2x^{-2}y^3)^4 (4xy^{-2})^{-2}\) ?
Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{2x^2-8x}{x^2-4x+4} \div \frac{x^2-4x}{x^2-4}\) ?
explanation: Factor and rewrite as multiplication by the reciprocal: \(\frac{2x(x-4)}{(x-2)^2} \cdot \frac{(x-2)(x+2)}{x(x-4)} = \frac{2(x+2)}{x-2} = \frac{2x+4}{x-2}\).

stem: For \(x>0\) and \(y>0\), which expression is equivalent to \(\left(\frac{8x^6}{y^3}\right)^{-2/3}\) ?
explanation: Using the negative exponent, take the reciprocal first: \(\left(\frac{y^3}{8x^6}\right)^{2/3}\). Then cube root and square: \(\frac{y^2}{4x^4}\).

explanation: Simplify the numerator: \((x^{-2}y^{3})^{2}=x^{-4}y^{6}\). Then subtract the denominator exponents: \(x^{-4-3}=x^{-7}\) and \(y^{6-(-4)}=y^{10}\). Thus the expression is equivalent to \(\frac{y^{10}}{x^{7}}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\displaystyle \frac{6x^{3}y^{-2}}{9x^{-1}y^{5}}\) ?
explanation: The constant part simplifies to \(\frac{6}{9}=\frac{2}{3}\). For \(x\), subtract exponents: \(3-(-1)=4\). For \(y\), subtract exponents: \(-2-5=-7\). So the expression is \(\frac{2x^{4}}{3y^{7}}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\sqrt[3]{x^{9}y^{6}}\) ?
explanation: A cube root raises the expression to the \(\frac{1}{3}\) power: \((x^{9}y^{6})^{1/3}=x^{9/3}y^{6/3}=x^{3}y^{2}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \((2x^{2})^{3}(4x^{-5})\) ?
For \(x>0\) and \(y>0\), which expression is equivalent to \(\left(\frac{x^{3/2}y^{-1}}{x^{1/2}y^{1/3}}\right)^{2}\) ?
explanation: Inside the parentheses, subtract exponents: \(x^{3/2-1/2}=x\) and \(y^{-1-1/3}=y^{-4/3}\). Squaring gives \(x^{2}y^{-8/3}=\frac{x^{2}}{y^{8/3}}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{x^{2/3}-1}{x^{1/3}-1}\) for \(x>0\) and \(x\neq 1\)?
explanation: Let \(a = x^{1/3}\). Then the expression is \(\frac{a^2-1}{a-1} = a+1 = x^{1/3}+1\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{(4x^6 y^{-2})^{3/2}}{(2x^3 y^{-1})^2}\) for \(x,y>0\)?
explanation: The numerator is \(8x^9y^{-3}\) and the denominator is \(4x^6y^{-2}\). Dividing gives \(2x^{3}y^{-1} = \frac{2x^3}{y}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{x^{-2}-y^{-2}}{x^{-1}+y^{-1}}\) for \(x,y\neq 0\) and \(x+y\neq 0\)?
explanation: Let \(a=x^{-1}\) and \(b=y^{-1}\). The numerator is \(a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b)\), so the quotient is \(a-b=x^{-1}-y^{-1}=\frac{1}{x}-\frac{1}{y}\).

stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\sqrt[3]{x^2\sqrt{x}}\) for \(x>0\)?
Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{(x^{2/3} y^{1/4})^6}{(x^{1/2} y)^{-2}}\) for \(x,y>0\)?
explanation: The numerator is \(x^4 y^{3/2}\). The denominator is \(x^{-1} y^{-2}\). Dividing gives \(x^{4-(-1)}y^{3/2-(-2)}=x^5 y^{7/2}\).

stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to \(\frac{x^{-3}y^{6}}{x^{-5}y^{2}}\) for \(x \neq 0\) and \(y \neq 0\)?
explanation: Subtract exponents of like bases: \(x^{-3-(-5)}=x^2\) and \(y^{6-2}=y^4\). Thus the expression is \(x^2y^4\).

stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(\left(\frac{4x^3}{y}\right)^2\left(\frac{y^2}{2x}\right)^3\) for \(x \neq 0\) and \(y \neq 0\)?
explanation: First term: \(\left(\frac{4x^3}{y}\right)^2=\frac{16x^6}{y^2}\). Second term: \(\left(\frac{y^2}{2x}\right)^3=\frac{y^6}{8x^3}\). Their product is \(\frac{16}{8}x^{6-3}y^{-2+6}=2x^3y^4\).

stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(\frac{2x^2 - 18}{x^2 - 2x - 15}\) for \(x \neq -3, 5\)?
explanation: Factor the numerator as \(2(x^2-9)=2(x-3)(x+3)\) and the denominator as \((x-5)(x+3)\). Cancel the common factor \(x+3\) to get \(\frac{2(x-3)}{x-5}\).

stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(\left(\frac{a^{1/2}b^{-2}}{a^{-3/2}b^{4}}\right)^{-1}\) for \(a > 0\) and \(b \neq 0\)?
explanation: Inside the parentheses, \(a^{1/2-(-3/2)}=a^2\) and \(b^{-2-4}=b^{-6}\), so the expression is \((a^2b^{-6})^{-1}=a^{-2}b^6=\frac{b^6}{a^2}\).

passage.text: Beginning in 2018, the Westbrook Public Library participated in a statewide e-book consortium. The consortium negotiates bulk discounts from publishers and charges each member library an annual fee based on that library's total e-book circulation. In the six years since Westbrook joined, its e-book checkouts more than tripled, while its physical book circulation dropped by almost half. A library board member argued that the shift to e-books has saved money because the library now spends less on repairing and replacing printed books. That argument, however, ignores the terms of the consortium agreement: the more e-books residents borrow, the more the library pays in consortium fees.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Westbrook's residents now read more books than they did before the library joined the consortium.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Any reduction in print-related expenses may have been partially offset by the rise in e-book circulation fees.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The library should cancel its physical book collection and rely exclusively on e-books.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Consortium fees are unrelated to how many e-books Westbrook residents actually borrow.

explanation: Because the consortium charges fees based on e-book circulation, the tripling of e-book checkouts implies higher consortium fees. The passage's warning about the board member's argument supports the conclusion that print-related savings may be partly offset by these increased fees.

passage.text: At the Bronze Age site of Tel Yaron, archaeologists found a well-defined destruction layer of ash and collapsed bricks. Radiocarbon dates place this destruction at roughly 1450 BCE. In every storage jar excavated from soil below the layer, the handles are rounded. In every storage jar excavated from soil above the layer, within deposits that accumulated over the next few decades, the handles are angular. No pot in the site's continuous sequence has a handle shape intermediate between the two.

stem: Because the deposits are continuous and well stratified, the replacement of rounded handles by angular handles at Tel Yaron most likely occurred

choices.label: A
choices.text: quickly around the time of the destruction, rather than gradually over a long period represented by the surrounding deposits.

choices.label: B
choices.text: only after a different cultural group invaded the region and expelled the original inhabitants.

choices.label: C
choices.text: because the clay available to local potters became harder to shape after the destruction.

choices.label: D
choices.text: as a result of the site's inhabitants copying handle designs from imported vessels.

explanation: The presence of rounded handles below the destruction layer and angular handles in deposits from only a few decades above it, with no intermediate forms in a continuous sequence, most directly supports a rapid transition near the time of the destruction.

passage.text: In 2017, biologists measured the size of the toe pads of green anoles on several small islands. Shortly afterward, two powerful hurricanes swept through the region. When the biologists returned, they found that the average toe pad size among surviving lizards was significantly larger than the average had been before the storms. Previous lab experiments had shown that larger toe pads allow anoles to cling to wet, windswept surfaces much more effectively than smaller toe pads do. The researchers also confirmed that only lizards that survived the hurricanes later produced offspring.

stem: The observed shift in average toe pad size is therefore best explained as

choices.label: A
choices.text: an acquired trait: the storm winds stretched the lizards' toe pads, and the lizards passed these stretched pads directly to their offspring.

choices.label: B
choices.text: a temporary environmental effect that would disappear in the next generation, since the hurricanes had no lasting impact on the lizards' genes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: a result of the hurricanes causing new mutations in the surviving lizards that increased toe pad size in their offspring.

choices.label: D
choices.text: selective survival: lizards with larger toe pads were more likely to withstand the hurricanes and thus made up a larger share of the breeding population.

explanation: The prior lab evidence links larger toe pads to better survival in windy conditions, and the survivors were the only lizards that reproduced. This supports the inference that the change was caused by selective survival rather than acquired traits, temporary effects, or new mutations.

passage.text: A large company introduced a voluntary wellness program that provided subsidized gym memberships and regular health coaching. At the end of the first year, employees who had enrolled in the program submitted 22 percent fewer health insurance claims, on average, than employees who had not enrolled. The company's benefits director recommended expanding the program to all employees, predicting that doing so would lower the company's total health-care spending. The human resources director was skeptical, however, because enrollment was voluntary: employees who already exercised regularly and ate well may have been especially likely to sign up.

stem: Consequently, the comparison between enrolled and nonenrolled employees cannot demonstrate that

choices.label: A
choices.text: the wellness program caused the lower claim rate; the difference could instead reflect the preexisting habits of employees who chose to enroll.

choices.label: B
choices.text: employees who declined to enroll were, on average, as healthy as those who enrolled.

choices.label: C
choices.text: expanding the program would force unhealthy employees to participate against their will.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the company's health-care spending would increase if the program were discontinued.

explanation: Because enrollment was voluntary, the discrepancy in claims may result from health-conscious employees selecting into the program. Thus the data do not prove that the program itself reduced claims.

passage.text: Astronomers detected phosphine in the atmosphere of a temperate exoplanet. On Earth, phosphine is produced mainly by living microbes, and the astronomers could not identify any known nonbiological process that would produce the observed amount under their assumed model of the planet's atmosphere. Several popular articles concluded that the planet must therefore contain life. Yet the planet's actual atmospheric composition is largely unknown, and if the atmosphere contains unusual gases, unfamiliar chemical reactions might create phosphine.

stem: Thus, the phosphine detection is best regarded as

choices.label: A
choices.text: irrefutable evidence of biological activity, because every other explanation has been ruled out.

choices.label: B

passage.text: Remote-work advocates often point to surveys in which employees report getting more done at home. Freed from commutes and open-office interruptions, workers say they can enter deep concentration for hours at a stretch. These self-reports, the advocates argue, translate into real gains for companies that trust employees to manage their own time.
passage.text_b: The benefits of face-to-face collaboration are easy to underestimate. Breakroom conversations, chance meetings, and overheard problems are not mere distractions; they are how ideas combine and propagate. If a workforce is scattered, the informal exchanges that produce breakthrough innovations become rare. A team that is efficient at completing today's tasks may be quietly starving the pipeline of tomorrow's ideas.

passage.text: Historians who emphasize internal causes of Rome’s fall point to a long sequence of civil wars, debased coinage, and a widening gap between rich and poor. By this view, the empire was already critically weakened before any external enemy delivered a final blow.
passage.text_b: The Roman Empire survived countless episodes of corruption and economic mismanagement. What changed in the late empire was the scale and coordination of external threats. Internal problems were not new; the arrival of peoples displaced by distant upheavals turned those problems into a crisis. Absent that external catalyst, the empire would likely have muddled through as it had before.

passage.text: A universal basic income would eliminate the bureaucratic maze of means-tested benefits. Every citizen receives the same modest monthly payment, no questions asked. Poverty would plummet, and recipients could take unpaid caregiving roles or pursue education without the threat of losing benefits.
passage.text_b: The apparent simplicity of a universal basic income masks a brutal fiscal reality. A payment large enough to lift people out of poverty would consume a large share of the federal budget. To pay for it, governments would have to slash existing services that many poor families depend on, such as housing assistance and Medicaid. The net effect could easily leave the most vulnerable worse off.

choices.label: D

explanation: Text 2 claims that paying for a universal basic income would force cuts to services that poor families depend on, so the net effect could leave the most vulnerable worse off. The author would therefore dispute Text 1’s claim that poverty would plummet by pointing to these losses.

passage.text: Replacing short-haul flights and automobile trips with high-speed rail is one of the fastest ways to cut transportation emissions. A single train can carry hundreds of passengers with a fraction of the energy per mile of cars or planes. Over its decades-long operating life, a high-speed line avoids millions of tons of carbon dioxide.
passage.text_b: Every new transportation project starts with a carbon debt. Steel production, concrete manufacturing, and earthmoving for a rail line release enormous amounts of greenhouse gases before the first train runs. Moreover, faster travel encourages people to make more and longer trips, so the reduction in emissions per mile can be offset by a growth in total miles traveled.

passage.text: Local food advocates often insist that eating food grown in one's immediate region is morally and environmentally superior to food shipped across continents. They point to the fossil fuels consumed by long-distance trucking and air freight, and argue that 'food miles' are a clear measure of ecological harm. Shorter supply chains, they conclude, mean fewer emissions and stronger community economies.
passage.text_b: Several life-cycle assessments complicate this picture. Tomatoes grown in naturally heated Mediterranean greenhouses, for example, can have a smaller carbon footprint when shipped to northern Europe than tomatoes produced in local energy-intensive hothouses. Lamb raised in New Zealand and transported to Britain can be less carbon-intensive than British lamb raised on feedstocks, because New Zealand's grazing systems use fewer inputs. In other words, transport distance is only one variable; production method, energy source, and storage practices can matter more. A sweeping 'buy local' rule may therefore be an unreliable guide to sustainability.

passage.text: Some of the most consequential ideas in modern business were not generated during scheduled meetings but through unplanned conversations by the coffee machine or across an office hallway. Virtual workplaces can be deliberately designed to pair people across disciplines and to record conversations that would otherwise evaporate. passage.text: An education worth the name should not treat students simply as future employees. Its aim is to furnish minds with historical perspective, imaginative literature, and fundamental scientific reasoning—the capacities to think critically about human life. For students from families with no financial cushion, the most liberating form of learning is one that leads to a competent trade and a decent income. Besides, the boundary between vocational and intellectual is false: skilled technical work often involves complex judgment, collaborative problem-solving, and continuous learning. A program that gives students marketable expertise is not narrowing their minds; it is giving them instruments to act on the world.

passage.text: Our society cannot shut down fossil fuel plants until we have a reliable source of carbon-free power that runs regardless of weather. Wind and solar are intermittent; on calm nights they generate little or nothing. Thus, an electricity grid that leans heavily on renewables will frequently fall short, forcing utilities to burn natural gas or turn to nuclear energy. The honest conclusion is that nuclear power, not renewables, should be the centerpiece of a decarbonized grid.

A portfolio of geographically dispersed wind and solar farms is rarely idle everywhere at once, and battery storage is already capable of shifting supply across the hours. More important, flexible consumers—from industrial plants to electric vehicles—can be harnessed through smart pricing to match demand to times of abundance. The fear of a 'reliability gap' is largely a problem of outdated policies, not an immutable property of renewable energy.

passage.text: Social media platforms are mainly to blame for rising political polarization. Online algorithms are a tool, not the engine; if they disappeared tomorrow, strategic politicians would simply find other channels.

passage.text: Text 1: Programs that send robots to Mars and telescopes into deep space capture the public's imagination. These missions inspire young people to study science and engineering, creating the next generation of innovators.
passage.text_b: Text 2: The government has limited resources, and every dollar spent on a space mission cannot be used to address urgent problems on Earth, such as improving public health and repairing infrastructure. Public curiosity should not be the main reason for such expensive investments.

stem: How would the author of Text 2 most likely react to the argument in Text 1?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Space missions should be funded only if they also improve public health directly.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inspiring students is a desirable outcome, but other urgent problems may deserve the money more.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The excitement caused by space exploration is not worth any government support.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The best response to earthbound problems is to send more spacecraft.

explanation: Text 2 argues for weighing opportunity costs; inspiring students is nice but may not outweigh pressing needs on Earth.

passage.text: Telecommuting is a boon to productivity. Freed from office interruptions, employees report more focused time on complex tasks. The flexibility to structure their own schedules also lets workers match tasks to their peak energy, yielding better output per hour.
passage.text_b: The very isolation that remote employees praise is a hidden liability. Innovation rarely emerges from solitary concentration; it emerges when colleagues exchange half-formed ideas by chance. A workplace that optimizes for unbroken focus may quietly starve the creative collisions that sustain long-term growth.

stem: Which of the following would the author of Text 2 most likely say in response to Text 1's claim that remote work gives employees more focused time on complex tasks?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Even if remote work allows more focus, it may undermine the collaborative exchanges that lead to breakthrough ideas.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Focused time on complex tasks is the only factor that matters for productivity, so remote work is clearly superior.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Telecommuting is beneficial only when employees structure schedules around their peak energy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The informal interactions that drive innovation are less important than reducing interruptions.

explanation: Text 2 argues that isolation, even if it allows focus, reduces the chance encounters that produce innovation. Thus the author would acknowledge the focused work Text 1 praises but warn that collaboration may suffer.

passage.text: Adolescents' biological clocks make it difficult to fall asleep before 11 p.m., yet many schools require them in class by 7:30. Shifting start times to 9:00 would allow teenagers to get the recommended eight to ten hours of sleep, improving alertness, grades, and mental health.
passage.text_b: Moving to a later bell would not occur in a vacuum. Sports practice, part-time jobs, and family dinners are all built around the current schedule. If dismissal is pushed into late afternoon, many students would have to choose between participating in these activities and getting home at a reasonable hour.

stem: How would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the proposal in Text 1?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The evidence linking sleep to academic performance is too weak to justify any change.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The benefits of added sleep must be weighed against the logistical disruptions that a later schedule would create.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Teenagers should focus on academic achievement rather than extracurricular activities.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Schools should keep current start times because no one can change adolescent sleep cycles.

explanation: Text 2 does not deny the benefits of more sleep; it points out real costs of changing the schedule. The author would therefore say that any benefits must be considered alongside the disruptions the change would cause.

passage.text: For passenger cars, battery electric vehicles are the clear choice. Charging stations are increasingly common, and electricity is far cheaper than gasoline or diesel. Over the life of the vehicle, owners save thousands of dollars.
passage.text_b: The calculus changes when the vehicle is a semi-truck hauling freight. A battery heavy enough for a five-hundred-mile route leaves less room for cargo, and recharging a massive battery can take hours. Hydrogen fuel cells can be refueled in minutes, keeping trucks on the road and delivering value that a per-mile energy comparison misses.

stem: How would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Text 1's emphasis on lower running costs for battery electric vehicles?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cost per mile is the only relevant factor, so battery electric vehicles are superior for all uses.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Battery electric vehicles may be economical for cars, but for heavy trucks, time lost to charging can override fuel savings.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hydrogen is cheaper than electricity for every type of vehicle.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trucking companies should avoid hydrogen because fueling stations are not yet widespread.

explanation: Text 2 accepts that battery electric vehicles work well for passenger cars but argues that for trucks, the need to minimize downtime changes the value calculation. Thus the author would say long charging times can erase the fuel-cost advantage.

passage.text: Homework extends learning beyond the classroom. When students practice skills at home, they consolidate what was taught in school and develop good study habits. The routine of completing and turning in assignments also instills a sense of responsibility early in life.
passage.text_b: Research on elementary-age children finds little academic benefit from homework, but it does find increased family conflict and negative attitudes toward school. stem: How would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Text 1's claim that homework builds responsibility?

choices.text: The responsibility lesson is undermined when homework leads to family conflict and negative attitudes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: However stressful, homework still teaches students to meet deadlines.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Parents should not help with homework because doing so weakens the responsibility lesson.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Elementary students should receive even more homework to build study habits and responsibility.

explanation: Text 2 directly challenges the idea that homework teaches responsibility, observing that it often creates family stress and negative attitudes. The author would say this outcome makes the supposed responsibility lesson ineffective.

passage.text: Growing food in cities is a powerful remedy for two problems at once. Rooftop and vacant-lot farms shorten supply chains, cutting the emissions associated with trucking produce across the country. At the same time, they give residents in food deserts fresh, healthy options within walking distance.
passage.text_b: Though urban farms are a lovely amenity, they are not a solution at any meaningful scale. City land is expensive, and yields per square foot are low compared with commercial farms. For a city to feed even a small share of its population, food must still travel long distances from rural regions.

stem: How would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Text 1's claim that urban farming cuts transportation emissions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any reduction in emissions is worth the cost of urban land.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The reduction in transportation emissions is outweighed by the low yields and high costs that limit urban farming's reach.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Commercial farms should be moved into cities to take advantage of vacant lots.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Food deserts cannot be solved unless every neighborhood contains a rooftop farm.

explanation: Text 2 argues that urban farms cannot produce enough food to replace long-distance shipping. Therefore the author would concede some local food is grown but suggest the emission savings are limited by low yields and high costs.

passage.text: Among the thousands of objects recovered from the ancient shipwreck, one of the bronze instruments, long encrusted with sand and marine growth, ______ researchers with direct evidence of an advanced navigation system.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject of the verb is "one" (not "bronze instruments" or "thousands of objects"), so the singular verb "provides" is required.

passage.text: The university's board of trustees, having reviewed the financial projections and listened to comments from faculty members, announced ______ decision to delay construction of the new science center.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A collective noun such as "board" is singular when it acts as one unit, so the singular possessive "its" is correct; "it's" means "it is" and "they're" means "they are."

passage.text: By the time the rescue team arrived at the mountain refuge, the storm ______ the lower slopes in nearly two meters of snow, making further searches impossible.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The storm occurred before the rescue team arrived in the past, so the past perfect "had blanketed" correctly shows the earlier of two past events.

passage.text: Neither the lead researcher nor the laboratory assistants ______ able to explain the anomalous result, so the experiment was scheduled to be repeated.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: In a "neither...nor" construction, the verb agrees with the nearer subject; here "assistants" is plural, so the past plural "were" is correct.

passage.text: A number of environmental factors, including fluctuations in temperature and the presence of airborne pollutants, ______ currently being studied by the conservation team.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The phrase "a number of" means "several" and takes a plural verb; here "are" is the plural present-tense verb needed with "currently."

passage.text: On an isolated island, a biologist spent decades studying a population of seed-eating birds. During successive drought years, plants produced mostly hard, thick-shelled seeds, and birds with deeper beaks survived at highest rates. Mean beak depth in the population increased over that period. After the drought ended, prolonged wet years made small, soft seeds abundant, a food source that small-beaked birds handle more rapidly. Yet the birds' average beak depth remained high and did not shift downward. Because beak depth is strongly heritable, the most likely explanation is that ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: natural selection ceased to operate on beak depth once the drought ended.

choices.label: B
choices.text: the wet years favored other traits strongly enough to mask any effect of beak depth.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the genetic variation necessary for a shift back to smaller beaks had been largely lost during the drought years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: small-beaked birds had migrated away from the island during the drought.

explanation: Since beak depth is heritable and wet conditions favor small-beaked birds, the failure of average beak depth to decrease is best explained by the loss of genetic variation for smaller beaks during the earlier selection event.

passage.text: Excavators recovered storage jars from a Roman merchant ship that sank around 100 CE. Several jars, identified by clay composition as from Rhodes, contained visible olive-oil residue. An equal number of jars from another region contained no food residue whatsoever, while jars from a third region held traces of wine. The absence of residue in the second group is significant because oil and wine leave distinctive organic films on fired clay and these films survive millennia in anaerobic environments. Therefore, the second group of jars most likely ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: was carried on deck and washed clean before the ship sank.

choices.label: B
choices.text: was made from a clay that was unable to absorb liquids.

choices.label: C
choices.text: had been manufactured long after the other jars and therefore was not in use.

choices.label: D
choices.text: originally held a dry commodity such as grain, which would not have left the same kind of film.

explanation: Because oil and wine leave lasting residue films in surviving jars, the absence of such residue suggests the other jars held goods that would not leave that kind of film, such as a dry commodity.

passage.text: Researchers asked hundreds of volunteers to guess the number of beans in a jar. Individual guesses varied enormously, but the average guess was within a few percent of the true count. In another condition, volunteers could see several previous guesses before giving their own. Their responses clustered together, but the average became less accurate. This finding suggests that the 'wisdom of crowds' depends crucially on ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the guesses being made independently rather than being influenced by others.

choices.label: B
choices.text: the participants being experts in the subject being judged.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the true answer being known to at least one member of the group.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the number of guesses being as large as possible.

explanation: When volunteers saw others' guesses, guesses clustered and accuracy fell, showing that the crowd's collective accuracy depends on independent judgment rather than social influence.

passage.text: Two adjacent cities of similar size had nearly identical summer temperatures for decades. City X then replaced many parks and tree-lined streets with concrete plazas and asphalt parking, while City Y maintained its greenery. Over the next twenty years, summer temperatures in City X rose substantially relative to City Y. The observed difference cannot be explained by global climate trends, since the two cities experienced the same broader regional climate. Thus, the temperature divergence is most directly attributable to ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: normal year-to-year weather fluctuations in City X.

choices.label: B
choices.text: heat generated by new buildings in City X being stored in the soil.

choices.label: C
choices.text: an increase in automobile use in City X that had no effect in City Y.

choices.label: D
choices.text: a reduction in evaporative cooling and shade caused by land-cover changes in City X.

explanation: The only major difference between the cities is City X's loss of vegetation, which reduces shade and evaporative cooling; the temperature divergence is thus best attributed to those land-cover changes.

passage.text: Some archaeologists argue that ancient cave paintings were created only as art, with no practical function. But a survey of a cave complex found that the paintings are not randomly distributed: they cluster in chambers with particularly pronounced sound reflections, while chambers with absorbing surfaces have few paintings. Among the painted chambers, those with the strongest echoes contain the most elaborate compositions. This pattern strongly undermines the idea that the paintings were purely decorative, because it suggests that ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ancient artists preferred to work in chambers where sound carried poorly.

choices.label: B
choices.text: the placement and elaboration of paintings were linked to the acoustic properties of the chambers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the cave complex was used as a residence rather than a ceremonial site.

choices.label: D
choices.text: cave chambers were chosen to protect the paintings from wind and moisture.

explanation: Paintings cluster in echo-prone chambers and are most elaborate where echoes are strongest, so their placement appears deliberately connected to acoustic properties rather than being purely decorative.

passage.text: Cave-dwelling populations of the Mexican tetra have lost their eyes. Because eye tissue is costly to build and maintain, some biologists have argued that natural selection favored eye loss as an energy conservation mechanism. Yet when researchers compared resting metabolic rates, cavefish and surface fish were indistinguishable. The cavefish do, however, have substantially more taste buds and a larger jaw than their surface-dwelling relatives.

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The loss of eyes in cavefish must have been caused by genetic drift rather than natural selection.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The energy saved by reducing eyes may have been redirected to other structures, so eye loss may not lower overall metabolic cost.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cavefish expend more energy than surface fish because they must move their larger jaws to eat.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Surface fish would develop more taste buds if they were raised in the dark.

explanation: The passage says cavefish and surface fish have indistinguishable resting metabolic rates, despite cavefish lacking energy-expensive eyes. The cavefish also have extra sensory and feeding structures, so the most logically supported conclusion is that the energy saved by eye loss may have been redirected to those other structures.

passage.text: At a sixth-millennium-BCE settlement, archaeologists found clay tags lying beside large storage jars. Some scholars think the tags were simply waste flakes, while others believe they are an early accounting system. In one building, each jar had a clay tag, and the number of oval-shaped impressions on the tag corresponded exactly to the estimated volume of grain once stored in that jar; jars with no measurable grain residue had tags with no oval impressions. Tags from a nearby pottery workshop showed similar oval impressions but no relation to storage volumes.

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The oval impressions were probably a notation for grain quantities, so the tags are more likely accounting records than waste flakes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The oval impressions were probably the personal marks of the potters who fired the tags.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The tags from the pottery workshop show that the oval impressions had a purely decorative function.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The tags from the storage building and the workshop were made by different cultures.

explanation: The strong relationship between oval impressions and stored grain volumes, together with the absence of that relationship for workshop tags, most directly supports the conclusion that the impressions encode grain quantities and thus that the tags were used for accounting.

passage.text: People often believe that walking is automatic and does not require attention. In a laboratory experiment, researchers asked participants to walk on a treadmill at their preferred speed. The participants were then asked to memorize a list of words while continuing to walk at the same speed. Compared with a control session in which they walked without doing the memory task, participants' stride became more variable, but their subsequent recall of the words was no worse.

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Walking and memorizing are carried out by entirely separate brain systems.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The memory task was so easy that it did not draw any attention away from walking.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Participants probably used attention to maintain word recall at the expense of a consistent walking pattern.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The participants walked more slowly during the memory task, which is why their recall did not decline.

explanation: Because memory performance stayed the same while walking became less consistent, the most logical inference is that attention was shifted from maintaining a steady gait to the memory task.

passage.text: To test whether an invasive shrub harms native plants by releasing persistent chemicals into the soil, researchers grew native seedlings in soil collected from areas long occupied by the shrub and in soil from uninvaded areas. Growth was identical. In another experiment, they planted native seedlings either alone or with a living shrub in the same pot; seedlings with the shrub grew significantly less.

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The shrub suppresses native plants through competition for light rather than through chemicals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chemicals that remain toxic in soil after the shrub is removed are probably not the cause of the suppression.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The shrub's suppressive effect occurs only if the soil has been previously invaded.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Soil from uninvaded areas contains chemicals that protect native seedlings from the shrub.

explanation: Native seedlings grew the same in soil from invaded and uninvaded areas, so any toxic chemicals released by the shrub are not persisting in the soil in an active form. The later experiment shows the living shrub does suppress natives, likely by another means.

passage.text: Objects in the natural world do not have grammatical gender, yet many languages assign masculine or feminine gender to nouns for these objects. In one study, monolingual speakers of a gendered language rated pictures of objects with masculine names as more similar to typical male faces than did speakers of a non-gendered language; the reverse was found for objects with feminine names. Bilingual speakers of the gendered and non-gendered languages changed their ratings depending on which language they had recently used, even though all instructions and rating scales were identical.

stem: Which conclusion most logically completes the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Grammatical gender is based on the physical features of the objects it labels.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bilingual speakers are less likely than monolingual speakers to be influenced by language.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The language being used can influence speakers' perceptions of inanimate objects.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Speakers of non-gendered languages are unable to perceive typical male or female faces.

explanation: The ratings of pictures shifted when bilingual speakers switched languages, and monolingual speakers of gendered languages showed gender-consistent biases. This most directly supports the claim that the language being used can influence how speakers perceive inanimate objects.

passage.text: Dr. Ayana Brooks ____ developed the new vaccine at her university laboratory.

choices.text: known for her bold color choices

passage.text: Mayor Elena Cruz ____ will speak at the opening ceremony.

passage.text: Brightwater ____ attracts thousands of visitors each summer.
