stem: In right triangle \(PQR\), the right angle is at \(Q\), and \(m\angle P = 35^\circ\). What is \(m\angle R\)?
explanation: The angles of a triangle sum to \(180^\circ\), so \(m\angle R = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 35^\circ = 55^\circ\).

stem: In triangle \(ABC\), \(m\angle A = 50^\circ\) and \(m\angle C = 60^\circ\). Side \(BC\) is extended through \(C\) to point \(D\). What is \(m\angle ACD\)?
explanation: First, \(m\angle B = 180^\circ - 50^\circ - 60^\circ = 70^\circ\). The exterior angle \(\angle ACD\) equals the sum of the remote interior angles: \(50^\circ + 70^\circ = 120^\circ\), or equivalently \(180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ\).

stem: In right triangle \(ABC\) above, the right angle is at \(B\), \(AB = 8\), and \(\angle A = 35^\circ\). Which expression gives the length of hypotenuse \(AC\)?
explanation: In \(\triangle ABC\), side \(AB\) is adjacent to \(\angle A\) and \(AC\) is the hypotenuse. Thus \(\cos 35^\circ = \dfrac{AB}{AC} = \dfrac{8}{AC}\), so \(AC = \dfrac{8}{\cos 35^\circ}\).

stem: In right triangle \(PQR\) above, \(\angle R\) is the right angle. If \(\sin P = \cos 35^\circ\), what is the measure of \(\angle Q\)?
explanation: For the acute angles of a right triangle, \(\sin P = \cos(90^\circ - P) = \cos Q\). Since \(\sin P = \cos 35^\circ\), \(Q = 35^\circ\). Alternatively, \(P = 55^\circ\) and \(Q = 90^\circ - 55^\circ = 35^\circ\).

stem: In the right triangle above, angle \(A\) measures \(30^\circ\), and hypotenuse \(AB\) has length 10. What is the length of side \(BC\)?
explanation: Side \(BC\) is opposite angle \(A\). Using SOH, \(\sin 30^\circ = \frac{BC}{AB} = \frac{BC}{10}\). Since \(\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}\), \(\frac{BC}{10} = \frac{1}{2}\), so \(BC = 5\).

The 18–29 group's after count of 45 is less than the 30–44 group's 55. The 45–59 group changed from 30 to 50, so it increased.

stem: The graph of \(y=f(x)\) is shown above. The graph is a parabola with vertex at \((-2,1)\) and passes through \((0,5)\). If the graph of \(f\) is shifted 3 units to the left and 2 units up, which of the following is the equation of the new graph?
explanation: The given parabola has vertex \((-2,1)\), so \(f(x)=a(x+2)^2+1\). Since \((0,5)\) lies on it, \(5=4a+1\), so \(a=1\). Thus \(f(x)=(x+2)^2+1\). Shifting 3 units left replaces \(x\) with \(x+3\), and shifting 2 units up adds 2, giving \(y=((x+3)+2)^2+1+2=(x+5)^2+3\).

stem: The graph of \(y=f(x)=-2x^2+4x+1\) is shown. After the graph is translated 3 units to the left and 1 unit up, what is the vertex of the translated graph?
explanation: Complete the square: \(f(x)=-2x^2+4x+1=-2(x-1)^2+3\), so the original vertex is \((1,3)\). Translating 3 units left gives \(x=1-3=-2\), and translating 1 unit up gives \(y=3+1=4\). The vertex is \((-2,4)\).

stem: In right triangle \(ABC\) shown, angle \(C\) is a right angle, \(AC = 3\), \(BC = 4\), and \(AB = 5\). What is \(\sin A\)?
explanation: For angle \(A\), the opposite side is \(BC = 4\) and the hypotenuse is \(AB = 5\). Thus \(\sin A = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{4}{5}\).

stem: In right triangle \(DEF\) shown, angle \(E\) is a right angle, \(DE = 12\), \(EF = 5\), and \(DF = 13\). If \(\sin D = \frac{5}{13}\), what is \(\cos F\)?
explanation: Angles \(D\) and \(F\) are complementary acute angles, so \(\cos F = \sin(90^\circ - F) = \sin D = \frac{5}{13}\). Equivalently, using SOH-CAH-TOA, \(\cos F = \frac{EF}{DF} = \frac{5}{13}\).

stem: In the right triangle shown, the right angle is at \(C\), \(\angle A = 35^\circ\), and \(AB = 10\). What is the length of side \(BC\)?
explanation: Side \(BC\) is opposite \(\angle A\), and \(AB\) is the hypotenuse. By SOH, \(\sin 35^\circ = \dfrac{BC}{10}\), so \(BC = 10\sin 35^\circ\).

stem: In the right triangle shown, the right angle is at \(Q\), \(\angle R = 25^\circ\), and the hypotenuse \(PR = 15\). What is the length of side \(QR\)?
explanation: Side \(QR\) is adjacent to \(\angle R\), and \(PR\) is the hypotenuse. By CAH, \(\cos 25^\circ = \dfrac{QR}{15}\), so \(QR = 15\cos 25^\circ\).

stem: In right triangle \(PQR\) above, the right angle is at \(Q\), \(PQ=6\), \(QR=8\), and \(PR=10\). What is the value of \(\cos(\angle R)\)?

stem: In right triangle \(ABC\) shown above, \(AB = 13\), \(BC = 5\), and \(\angle A = \theta\). What is the value of \(\cos \theta \cdot \tan \theta\)?
explanation: Since \(AC\) is adjacent to \(\theta\) and \(BC\) is opposite \(\theta\), use the Pythagorean theorem: \(AC = \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = 12\). Then \(\cos \theta = \frac{12}{13}\) and \(\tan \theta = \frac{5}{12}\). Thus \(\cos \theta \cdot \tan \theta = \frac{12}{13} \cdot \frac{5}{12} = \frac{5}{13}\).

stem: In right triangle \(DEF\) shown above, \(DE = 12\), \(EF = 5\), and \(\angle D = \alpha\). What is the value of \(\sin(90^\circ - \alpha) - \cos(90^\circ - \alpha)\)?
explanation: The right angle is at \(E\), so \(\sin \alpha = \frac{EF}{DF} = \frac{5}{13}\) and \(\cos \alpha = \frac{DE}{DF} = \frac{12}{13}\). Using \(\sin(90^\circ - \alpha) = \cos \alpha\) and \(\cos(90^\circ - \alpha) = \sin \alpha\), the expression equals \(\frac{12}{13} - \frac{5}{13} = \frac{7}{13}\).

stem: Which claim is best supported by the data in the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The average score gain was larger for students in the in-person program than for students in either online program.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Students in the live-online program made larger average score gains than students in the in-person program.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A majority of students in the self-paced online program earned score gains below 9.1 points.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The in-person program had more students and a higher satisfaction rate than either online program.

explanation: The table shows average gains of 14.2 points for in-person, 12.4 for live online, and 9.1 for self-paced online. Thus the in-person program had the largest average score gain, so A is supported. B reverses the in-person/live-online comparison, C makes a claim about the distribution of individual scores that the average alone cannot support, and D is false because the live-online program had more students (32) than the in-person program (30).

passage.text: Researchers assigned students to learn 20 new vocabulary words either by spacing practice sessions over several days or by cramming the night before a test. The table shows the mean number of words students recalled on an immediate test and on a delayed test one week later.

stem: Which statement is best supported by the data in the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Students who crammed recalled more words on the delayed test than on the immediate test.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Students who crammed recalled more words on the immediate test than students who used spaced practice did.

choices.label: C
choices.text: On the immediate test, the two groups' mean recall scores were close, but on the delayed test, the spaced-practice group recalled more words on average.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Because the cramming group had more students, its lower mean score on the delayed test was caused by the larger sample size.

explanation: The immediate-test means were 16.2 for spaced practice and 15.9 for cramming, a difference of only 0.3 words. On the delayed test, spaced practice recalled 12.8 words on average compared with 8.4 for cramming. Therefore C is directly supported. The other choices are contradicted by the table or attribute cause without evidence.

visual.title: Mean vocabulary words recalled out of 20

stem: The trapezoid shown below has parallel bases of length 8 and 4, and the distance between them is 3. What is the area of the trapezoid?
explanation: The area of a trapezoid is \(\frac{1}{2}(b_1+b_2)h\). With \(b_1=8\), \(b_2=4\), and \(h=3\), the area is \(\frac{1}{2}(8+4)(3)=18\).

stem: The rectangular prism shown below has length 5, width 3, and height 4. What is the volume of the prism?
explanation: The volume of a rectangular prism is \(\text{length} \times \text{width} \times \text{height}\). So \(5 \times 3 \times 4 = 60\).

stem: The figure above shows a rectangular prism with side lengths 4, 5, and 6. What is the volume, in cubic units, of the prism?
explanation: The volume of a rectangular prism is length times width times height: \(4 \times 5 \times 6 = 120\) cubic units.

stem: The graph of \(y=f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane is shown above. The vertex of the parabola is \((1,4)\), and the parabola passes through \((0,3)\). The graph is shifted 2 units to the left and 3 units down to produce the graph of \(y=g(x)\). Which of the following defines \(g(x)\)?
explanation: The graph shown has vertex \((1,4)\) and passes through \((0,3)\), so \(f(x)=-(x-1)^2+4\). Shifting left 2 units replaces \(x\) with \(x+2\), and shifting down 3 units subtracts 3: \(g(x)=f(x+2)-3=-((x+2)-1)^2+4-3=-(x+1)^2+1\).

stem: The graph of \(y=g(x)\) is shown above. The parabola has vertex \((1,-2)\) and passes through \((0,1)\). If \(g(x)=f(x-2)+1\), which of the following defines \(f\)?

passage.text: A researcher conducted an eight-week study to see whether brief daily reading exercises improve students' reading comprehension. Students were randomly assigned to one of three groups: one group completed exercises using Strategy A, another group used Strategy B, and a control group did no extra exercise. The table below shows the number of students in each group and the average improvement in the students' reading-comprehension test scores from before to after the eight-week study.

stem: Which statement is best supported by the data in the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: More students were assigned to use Strategy B than to use Strategy A.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The control group’s average improvement of \(5\) points was half the Strategy A group’s average improvement of \(18\) points.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Students using Strategy B improved by an average of \(24\) points, which was greater than the average improvement of \(18\) points for students using Strategy A.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Students using Strategy A improved by an average of \(18\) points, the largest average improvement of any group.

explanation: The table shows that the Strategy B group had an average improvement of \(24\) points, while the Strategy A group had an average improvement of \(18\) points and the control group had \(5\) points. Therefore, the data support the statement that students using Strategy B improved more, on average, than students using Strategy A. Choice A is false because both strategy groups had 120 students; B is false because 5 is not half of 18; and D is false because 24 is larger than 18.

stem: In right triangle \(ABC\) above, \(AC=5\), \(BC=12\), and \(AB=13\). What is \(\cos \angle A\)?
explanation: For angle \(A\), the adjacent side is \(AC=5\) and the hypotenuse is \(AB=13\), so \(\cos A = \frac{AC}{AB} = \frac{5}{13}\).

stem: In right triangle \(PQR\) above, \(\angle P = 30^\circ\) and \(\angle Q = 60^\circ\). Which of the following is equal to \(\sin 30^\circ\)?
explanation: Since \(\sin x = \cos(90^\circ - x)\), we have \(\sin 30^\circ = \cos(60^\circ) = \cos 60^\circ\).

stem: The right triangle \(ABC\) is shown. Angle \(C\) is a right angle, \(AC=24\), \(BC=7\), and \(AB=25\). What is the value of \(\sin A\)?
explanation: Since \(\sin A\) is opposite over hypotenuse, \(\sin A = \frac{BC}{AB} = \frac{7}{25}\).

stem: In the right triangle \(DEF\) shown, angle \(F\) is a right angle, \(DE=10\), and \(\angle D = 35^\circ\). Which expression gives the length of side \(EF\)?
explanation: Side \(EF\) is opposite \(\angle D\), and \(DE\) is the hypotenuse. Thus \(\sin 35^\circ = \frac{EF}{10}\), so \(EF = 10\sin 35^\circ\).

stem: In right triangle \(PQR\) shown, \(\angle Q = 90^\circ\) and \(\sin P = \frac{5}{13}\). What is the value of \(\cos R\)?
explanation: Angles \(P\) and \(R\) are complementary, so \(\cos R = \cos(90^\circ - P) = \sin P = \frac{5}{13}\).

passage.text: Researchers surveyed employees at a technology company about their work arrangements and collaboration habits. The table shows, for each work arrangement, the average number of hours employees spent in collaborative meetings per week, their self-rated productivity on a scale from 1 to 10, and the percentage who said they were considering leaving their job within a year.

stem: Which statement is best supported by the data in the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Remote employees had fewer average collaborative hours per week than either other group and reported lower self-rated productivity than either other group.

choices.label: B
choices.text: On-site employees averaged the most collaborative hours per week and reported the lowest turnover intention.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hybrid employees averaged more collaborative hours per week than remote employees but reported higher self-rated productivity than remote employees.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The group with the fewest collaborative hours reported the highest self-rated productivity and the lowest turnover intention, whereas the group with the most collaborative hours reported the lowest self-rated productivity and the highest turnover intention.

explanation: Remote employees had the fewest average collaborative hours (6.2), the highest self-rated productivity (8.4), and the lowest turnover intention (12%). On-site employees had the most average collaborative hours (12.5), the lowest self-rated productivity (6.8), and the highest turnover intention (25%). Thus choice D accurately describes the pattern in the data.

visual.title: Work arrangement, collaboration, productivity, and turnover intention

passage.text: Public health officials collected data from residents in three neighboring districts. The table shows the average distance from a residence to the nearest store selling fresh produce, the average number of weekly servings of fresh produce residents reported eating, and the percentage of residents classified as food insecure.

stem: Which statement is best supported by the data in the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: District A had the greatest average distance to a fresh food store but the lowest food insecurity rate.

choices.label: B
choices.text: District C had the shortest average distance to a fresh food store and the highest weekly fresh produce servings.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Across districts, a greater average distance to the nearest fresh food store was associated with fewer weekly fresh produce servings and a higher food insecurity rate.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Across districts, a greater average distance to the nearest fresh food store was associated with more weekly fresh produce servings and a lower food insecurity rate.

explanation: As the average distance to the nearest fresh food store increases from 0.4 miles in District A to 1.3 miles in District B to 2.5 miles in District C, weekly fresh produce servings fall from 6.2 to 4.1 to 3.0, while food insecurity rises from 9% to 17% to 26%. Choice C correctly describes this association.

visual.title: Distance to fresh food, produce servings, and food insecurity by district
headers: Average distance to nearest fresh food store (miles)

stem: In right triangle \(ABC\), angle \(B\) is the right angle. If \(AB = 6\) and \(BC = 8\), what is the value of \(\sin A\)?
explanation: By the Pythagorean theorem, \(AC = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = 10\). Since \(\sin A\) is the side opposite angle \(A\) divided by the hypotenuse, \(\sin A = \frac{BC}{AC} = \frac{8}{10} = \frac{4}{5}\).

stem: In right triangle \(DEF\), angle \(E\) is the right angle. If \(\sin D = \frac{7}{25}\), what is \(\cos F\)?
explanation: The acute angles of a right triangle are complementary, so \(D + F = 90^\circ\). Thus \(\cos F = \sin(90^\circ - F) = \sin D = \frac{7}{25}\).

passage.text: To evaluate whether adding a dedicated left-turn signal reduces vehicle delays, a city measured average delay during morning rush at four intersections before and after installation. The number of vehicles per hour at each intersection and the average delays are shown in the table.

stem: Which statement is most strongly supported by the data in the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Intersection 4, which had the highest traffic volume, had the greatest absolute reduction in average delay.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intersection 2 had a greater percent reduction in average delay than any other intersection shown.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intersection 3 had the smallest percent reduction in average delay of the intersections shown.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intersection 1 had the greatest percent reduction in average delay of the intersections shown.

explanation: Percent reduction equals the reduction in delay divided by the before delay. Intersection 1: 15/60 = 25%; Intersection 2: 30/90 ≈ 33.3%; Intersection 3: 10/50 = 20%; Intersection 4: 10/80 = 12.5%. Therefore, Intersection 2 had the greatest percent reduction, not Intersection 4, 3, or 1.

passage.text: A botanist sowed seeds of three plant species in full sunlight and in shade to investigate how light condition affects germination. The table shows the number of seeds planted and the number that germinated for each species and light condition.

stem: Which statement is most strongly supported by the data in the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Species A had a higher germination rate in shade than in sunlight.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Species B had a higher germination rate in shade than in sunlight.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only Species C had a higher germination rate in shade than in sunlight.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Each species had a higher germination rate in sunlight than in shade.

explanation: Germination rates: Species A: 60/100 = 60% in sunlight, 40/100 = 40% in shade. Species B: 48/80 = 60% in sunlight, 24/80 = 30% in shade. Species C: 30/120 = 25% in sunlight, 72/120 = 60% in shade. Thus only Species C had a higher germination rate in shade than in sunlight.

stem: In the right triangle \(XYZ\) above, \(\angle Y\) is a right angle and \(\angle X\) measures \(30^\circ\). If \(XZ = 10\), what is the length of \(\overline{YZ}\)?
explanation: Side \(\overline{YZ}\) is opposite the \(30^\circ\) angle at \(X\), and \(\overline{XZ}\) is the hypotenuse. Thus \(\sin 30^\circ = \frac{YZ}{XZ} = \frac{YZ}{10}\), so \(YZ = 10\sin 30^\circ = 5\).

stem: In the right triangle \(PQR\) above, \(\angle Q\) is a right angle and \(\angle P\) measures \(42^\circ\). Which of the following is equal to \(\sin 42^\circ\)?
explanation: Because \(\angle Q = 90^\circ\), the remaining angle \(\angle R = 90^\circ - 42^\circ = 48^\circ\). For \(\angle P\), \(\sin 42^\circ = \frac{QR}{PR}\). For \(\angle R\), \(\cos 48^\circ = \frac{QR}{PR}\). Therefore, \(\sin 42^\circ = \cos 48^\circ\).

stem: The scatterplot above shows the number of hours students volunteered in a month and the number of community service points they earned. The line of best fit passes through the points \((2, 50)\) and \((10, 90)\). Based on the line of best fit, what is the predicted number of service points for a student who volunteered for \(6.5\) hours?
explanation: The slope of the line of best fit is \(\frac{90-50}{10-2}=\frac{40}{8}=5\). Using the point \((2,50)\), the equation is \(y=5x+40\). For \(x=6.5\), \(y=5(6.5)+40=72.5\).

stem: The scatterplot above shows the number of bird species observed at different elevations in a mountain range. The line of best fit passes through \((400, 80)\) and \((1400, 32)\). Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of the line of best fit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: For every 100-meter increase in elevation, the predicted number of bird species decreases by \(4.8\).

choices.label: B
choices.text: For every 100-meter increase in elevation, the predicted number of bird species decreases by \(48\).

choices.label: C
choices.text: For every additional bird species, the predicted elevation increases by about \(4.8\) meters.

choices.label: D
choices.text: For every additional bird species, the predicted elevation increases by about \(20.8\) meters.

explanation: The slope is \(\frac{32-80}{1400-400}=\frac{-48}{1000}=-0.048\) species per meter, or \(-4.8\) species per 100 meters. Thus the predicted number of species decreases by \(4.8\) for each 100-meter increase in elevation.

stem: The figure above shows a rectangular prism with side lengths 3 cm, 4 cm, and 5 cm. What is the volume of the prism, in cubic centimeters?
explanation: The volume of a rectangular prism is length times width times height, so \(3 \times 4 \times 5 = 60\) cubic centimeters.

stem: In triangle \(XYZ\) shown, \(\angle Y = 90^\circ\), \(XY = 24\), \(YZ = 7\), and \(XZ = 25\). If \(\angle Z = \theta^\circ\), what is the value of \(\cos(90^\circ - \theta) + \sin \theta\)?
explanation: From angle \(\theta\), the opposite side is \(XY = 24\) and the hypotenuse is \(XZ = 25\), so \(\sin \theta = \frac{24}{25}\). Since \(\cos(90^\circ - \theta) = \sin \theta\), the expression equals \(\frac{24}{25} + \frac{24}{25} = \frac{48}{25}\).

stem: In right triangle \(ABC\) shown, \(\angle C = 90^\circ\), \(AC = 4x\), \(BC = 3x\), and \(AB = 15\). If \(\angle A = \theta^\circ\), what is the value of \(\cos(90^\circ - \theta)\)?
explanation: By the Pythagorean theorem, \((4x)^2 + (3x)^2 = 15^2\), so \(25x^2 = 225\), giving \(x = 3\). Thus \(BC = 9\) and \(AB = 15\). At angle \(\theta\), \(\sin \theta = \frac{BC}{AB} = \frac{9}{15} = \frac{3}{5}\). Since \(\cos(90^\circ - \theta) = \sin \theta\), the answer is \(\frac{3}{5}\).

passage.text: Researchers assigned 90 tomato plants randomly to three fertilizer treatments: a control, an organic fertilizer, or a synthetic fertilizer. After one growing season, they recorded the yield of each plant and calculated the mean and standard deviation shown in the table.

stem: Which statement is best supported by the data in the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The synthetic fertilizer produced a lower mean yield than the organic fertilizer.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The yields of plants in the organic fertilizer group were more spread out than the yields of plants in the synthetic fertilizer group.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The control group's mean yield was more than one-third less than the synthetic fertilizer group's mean yield.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The synthetic fertilizer group's yields were more spread out than the control group's yields.

explanation: The standard deviation for the organic group (1.2 kg/plant) is greater than that for the synthetic group (0.9 kg/plant), so the organic yields were more variable, or spread out. The mean yields show synthetic was higher than organic, the control mean was not more than one-third less than the synthetic mean, and the synthetic group had a smaller standard deviation than the control group.

passage.text: A school district surveyed students about their daily reading time outside of class and collected their end-of-year vocabulary test scores. The table below summarizes the results by reading-time category.

stem: Which statement is best supported by the data in the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Students who read for more than 60 minutes per day had a higher mean vocabulary score than students in any other reading-time category.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The mean vocabulary score increased by more than 10 points whenever the reading-time category increased.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vocabulary scores among students who read for 0–15 minutes per day were less variable than scores among students who read for 31–60 minutes per day.

choices.label: D
choices.text: More students in the study read for 16–30 minutes per day than for all the other reading-time categories combined.

explanation: The table shows that the more-than-60-minutes category had the highest mean score (79) of the four categories. The 16–30-minute category has only 52 students versus 133 in the other categories combined, the score increases are 6, 7, and 4 points, not more than 10, and the 0–15-minute group has a larger standard deviation than the 31–60-minute group, so those choices are contradicted by the data.

visual.title: Vocabulary Scores by Daily Reading Time

stem: In the figure shown, trapezoid \(ABCD\) has bases \(AB\) and \(CD\). If \(AB=14\), \(CD=6\), and the height of the trapezoid is 5, what is the area of the trapezoid?
explanation: The area of a trapezoid is \(A = \frac{1}{2}(b_1+b_2)h\). Substitute \(b_1=14\), \(b_2=6\), and \(h=5\): \(A=\frac{1}{2}(14+6)(5)=50\).

stem: In the figure shown, a right circular cylinder has a diameter of 6 feet and a height of 7 feet. What is the volume of the cylinder?
explanation: The radius is half the diameter, so \(r=3\) ft. The volume of a cylinder is \(V=\pi r^2 h\). Thus \(V=\pi(3)^2(7)=63\pi\) cubic feet.

stem: The figure shows a rectangle with length \(10\) and width \(6\). A right triangle with legs \(4\) and \(4\) has been cut out of the upper-right corner, leaving the shaded region. What is the area, in square units, of the shaded region?
explanation: The original rectangle has area \(10 \times 6 = 60\). The cut-out right triangle has area \(\frac{1}{2}(4)(4) = 8\). The shaded area is \(60 - 8 = 52\).

stem: In the right triangle shown, \(\sin A = \frac{5}{13}\). What is \(\cos B\)?
explanation: Angles \(A\) and \(B\) are complementary in a right triangle, so \(\cos B = \sin(90^\circ - B) = \sin A = \frac{5}{13}\). Using the figure, \(\cos B = \frac{BC}{AB} = \frac{5}{13}\).

passage.text: A city transportation agency surveyed 450 residents who commute primarily by bus, private car, bicycle, or walking. Respondents rated their overall commute satisfaction from 1 (very dissatisfied) to 5 (very satisfied). The table displays, for each mode, the number of respondents, the average satisfaction rating, the percentage who rated their commute 4 or 5, and the average one-way commute time in minutes.

stem: Which statement is best supported by the data?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Walking commuters had a higher average satisfaction rating and a shorter average commute time than bicycle commuters.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bus commuters had a lower percentage of high-satisfaction ratings than private-car commuters, and their average commute was shorter than that of private-car commuters.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Because more private-car commuters than any other group were surveyed, private car was the most common primary commute mode among all city residents.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bicycle commuters had a higher average satisfaction rating than walking commuters but had a longer average commute time.

explanation: The table shows that walking commuters had a higher average satisfaction rating (4.3) than bicycle commuters (4.0) and a shorter average commute (18 minutes vs. 25 minutes). The other statements either misread values or make an unsupported claim about all city residents from a survey subset.

visual.title: Commute survey results by primary mode

passage.text: A horticulture researcher grew tomato seedlings under four soil treatments, with 40 seedlings monitored in each treatment for four weeks. The table shows the average seedling height, the percentage of seedlings that developed at least five true leaves, the survival rate, and the average root length.

stem: Which statement is best supported by the data?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Compost A produced taller seedlings, on average, than Compost C and had a higher survival rate.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Compost B had a higher survival rate than Compost A, but fewer than 75% of its seedlings had at least five true leaves.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Compost C produced the tallest seedlings on average, even though it had the lowest survival rate of the four treatments.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The control treatment had the lowest average height and the lowest survival rate.

explanation: Compost C had the greatest average height (18.6 cm) and the lowest survival rate (82%). Compost A did not outgrow Compost C, Compost B had 76% of seedlings with at least five true leaves, and the control treatment did not have the lowest survival rate.

visual.title: Tomato seedling results after four weeks
headers: % with at least five true leaves

stem: Parallelogram \(ABCD\) is graphed in the \(xy\)-plane with vertices \(A(1,1)\), \(B(7,1)\), \(C(8,4)\), and \(D(2,4)\), as shown. What is the area of parallelogram \(ABCD\)?
explanation: The base \(\overline{AB}\) lies on \(y=1\), so its length is \(7-1=6\). The height is the vertical distance from \(y=1\) to \(y=4\), which is \(3\). Thus, the area of the parallelogram is \(6 \cdot 3 = 18\).

passage.text: To improve employee compliance with safety rules, a technology company offered a redesigned online training course. Employees were randomly assigned to receive either the original text-only version or a new version that added audio explanations. The company recorded whether each employee completed the training and, for those who completed it, how long the training took.

stem: Which statement is most strongly supported by the data in the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Employees assigned to the text-only version completed the training at a higher rate and in less time than employees assigned to the version with audio.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Employees assigned to the text-plus-audio version completed the training at a higher rate, but those who completed it took longer on average than text-only completers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The text-plus-audio version was less effective than the text-only version because the average completion time for the text-plus-audio version was longer.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The higher completion rate for the text-plus-audio version proves that every employee in that group found the audio explanations helpful.

explanation: The table shows that 84% of employees assigned to the text-plus-audio version completed the training, compared with 71% of those assigned to the text-only version. Among completers, the text-plus-audio group took 39 minutes on average, while the text-only group took 32 minutes. Therefore, B accurately describes both comparisons. A reverses the completion-rate finding; C treats longer completion time as evidence of lower effectiveness, which the data do not establish; D overgeneralizes from group data to individual attitudes.

passage.text: In an agricultural experiment, researchers compared drip irrigation with subsurface irrigation for growing tomatoes in a semiarid region. Fifty plots received each irrigation method, and researchers recorded total tomato yield and total water use for each plot.

stem: Which statement is most strongly supported by the data in the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Subsurface-irrigated plots had a higher average tomato yield and used less water on average than drip-irrigated plots.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Drip-irrigated plots had a higher average tomato yield but used more water on average than subsurface-irrigated plots.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Subsurface-irrigated plots produced an average of 5.2 kg more tomatoes per plot than drip-irrigated plots.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Drip-irrigated plots used more water but produced a higher average yield, suggesting that drip irrigation is the more efficient method.

explanation: The table shows that subsurface-irrigated plots had a mean tomato yield of 73.2 kg per plot, compared with 68.4 kg for drip-irrigated plots, and used 3,600 liters per plot compared with 4,100 liters for drip-irrigated plots. Thus A is directly supported. B reverses the yield result; C is an arithmetic error because the actual difference is 73.2 − 68.4 = 4.8 kg, not 5.2 kg; D reverses which method had the higher yield.

visual.caption: Tomato yield and water use by irrigation method.

stem: A gardener recorded the number of hours of sunlight each of 10 tomato plants received per day and the number of tomatoes the plant produced. The scatterplot above shows the data, and the line of best fit is shown. Based on the line of best fit, what is the best estimate of the predicted increase in the number of tomatoes produced when the daily sunlight increases from 4 hours to 7 hours?
explanation: The line of best fit predicts about \(3.2(4)+2.5=15.3\) tomatoes at 4 hours and \(3.2(7)+2.5=24.9\) tomatoes at 7 hours. The difference is \(24.9-15.3=9.6\), which is closest to 10 tomatoes.

stem: A teacher asked each student in a study group to record the number of hours spent practicing problems. The scatterplot above shows the practice time, in hours, and the score on a quiz. The line of best fit is shown. For the student who practiced 6 hours, what is the residual (actual score minus predicted score) for that student, based on the line of best fit?
explanation: The line of best fit is \(y = 6x + 36\). For \(x = 6\), the predicted score is \(6(6)+36=72\). The actual score from the scatterplot is 70, so the residual is \(70 - 72 = -2\).

passage.text: A school district surveyed 200 high school students about their typical nightly sleep duration and their current GPA. The table below shows the number of students in each sleep-duration category for two GPA groups.

stem: Which of the following statements is most directly supported by the data in the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Among students who reported getting less than 6 hours of sleep, fewer than half had a GPA of 3.0 or above.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A majority of students with a GPA below 3.0 reported getting less than 6 hours of sleep.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Students who got 6–7 hours of sleep were more likely than students who got more than 7 hours to have a GPA of 3.0 or above.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The proportion of students with a GPA of 3.0 or above who got more than 7 hours of sleep was greater than half.

explanation: Among the 60 students who got less than 6 hours of sleep, 20 had a GPA of 3.0 or above, so that proportion is \(20/60 = 1/3\), which is fewer than half. The other statements are not supported: 40 of 85 low-GPA students were in the less-than-6-hour group, 50 of 80 6–7-hour students had high GPAs while 45 of 60 more-than-7-hour students did, and 45 of 115 high-GPA students got more than 7 hours of sleep.

passage.text: A city surveyed 500 residents about two proposed bicycle infrastructure projects: Project A, adding protected lanes on a main avenue, and Project B, adding neighborhood bike boulevards. The table shows respondents' choices by whether they live within 5 miles of downtown.

stem: Which of the following statements is most directly supported by the data in the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Respondents living within 5 miles of downtown were more likely than respondents living farther away to support Project A.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Among respondents who supported Project A, more than half lived within 5 miles of downtown.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Respondents living farther than 5 miles from downtown were more likely than respondents living within 5 miles to support Project B.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Respondents living within 5 miles of downtown were more likely than respondents living farther away to support Project B.

explanation: Of the 240 respondents living within 5 miles, 100 supported Project B, or \(100/240 \approx 41.7\%\). Of the 260 respondents living farther away, 90 supported Project B, or \(90/260 \approx 34.6\%\). Therefore, those living within 5 miles were more likely to support Project B. The other statements misread the percentages: Project A support was 25% within versus about 46% farther away, only 60 of 180 Project A supporters lived within 5 miles, and Project B support was higher among those within 5 miles.

stem: In right triangle \(XYZ\), angle \(Z\) is the right angle. If \(XZ = 6\) and \(YZ = 8\), what is \(\cos X\)?
explanation: Because \(Z\) is the right angle, the hypotenuse is \(XY = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = 10\). At angle \(X\), the adjacent side is \(XZ = 6\), so \(\cos X = \frac{6}{10} = \frac{3}{5}\).

stem: In right triangle \(PQR\), angle \(Q\) is the right angle and angle \(P = 35^\circ\). Which of the following expressions is equal to \(\sin P\)?
explanation: Since the acute angles in a right triangle are complementary, \(R = 90^\circ - 35^\circ = 55^\circ\). The sine of an angle equals the cosine of its complement, so \(\sin 35^\circ = \cos 55^\circ\). Thus \(\sin P = \cos R = \cos 55^\circ\).

passage.text: A researcher investigated how two species of nitrogen-fixing bacteria affect the growth of alder seedlings. Seedlings were grown in soil with low, medium, or high phosphorus concentration, and each seedling was inoculated with either Rhizobium, Frankia, or no bacteria (control). The table shows the mean dry mass, in grams, of the seedlings in each condition after 12 weeks.

stem: Which statement is best supported by the data in the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At all phosphorus levels, seedlings inoculated with Frankia had a greater mean dry mass than seedlings inoculated with Rhizobium.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inoculation with Rhizobium was associated with a larger increase in mean dry mass between low and high phosphorus than inoculation with Frankia was.

choices.label: C
choices.text: For seedlings inoculated with Frankia, mean dry mass increased by more than 30% from low to high phosphorus.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Among seedlings that were not inoculated, increasing phosphorus from medium to high produced a greater increase in mean dry mass than increasing it from low to medium.

explanation: For Rhizobium, mean dry mass rose from 5.1 g at low phosphorus to 9.6 g at high phosphorus, an increase of 4.5 g. For Frankia, it rose from 6.3 g to 8.1 g, an increase of 1.8 g. Thus Rhizobium was associated with a larger increase. The other choices misread specific rows or compare percentages incorrectly.

passage.text: A city surveyed residents in four neighborhoods about their composting habits. For each neighborhood, the table shows the number of residents surveyed and the percentage of those residents who reported composting food scraps.

stem: Which statement is best supported by the data in the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: More residents composted in South than in West.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The number of residents who composted in North was less than the number who composted in East.

choices.label: C
choices.text: South had the highest percentage of composters, but West had the greatest number of composters.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If 20 more of the surveyed residents in East had reported composting, East would have had a higher composting percentage than South.

explanation: The number of composters is percent times surveyed count: North 0.32×250=80, East 0.25×320=80, South 0.40×200=80, West 0.35×280=98. South had the highest percentage (40%), while West had the greatest number (98), so C is correct.

stem: The graph of \(y=f(x)\) is shown in the \(xy\)-plane. The graph is a parabola with vertex at \((-1,2)\) and also contains the point \((1,6)\). If \(g(x)=f(x+1)-2\), what are the coordinates of the vertex of \(g\)?
explanation: The point \((1,6)\) determines the vertical stretch: \(f(x)=(x+1)^2+2\). Replacing \(x\) by \(x+1\) shifts the graph 1 unit left, so the vertex \((-1,2)\) moves to \((-2,2)\). Subtracting 2 shifts it down to \((-2,0)\). Alternatively, \(g(x)=((x+1)+1)^2+2-2=(x+2)^2\), so its vertex is \((-2,0)\).

stem: The graph of \(y=f(x)\) is shown in the \(xy\)-plane. The graph is a parabola with vertex at \((3,1)\) and contains the point \((1,-3)\). If \(g(x)=f(x+4)+5\), which of the following defines \(g\)?
The rectangle in the figure has a length of \(12\text{ cm}\) and a width of \(5\text{ cm}\). What is the area, in square centimeters, of the rectangle?
explanation: The area of a rectangle is length times width, so \(12 \times 5 = 60\). Thus the area is \(60\text{ cm}^2\).

stem: The rectangular prism in the figure has a length of \(4\) inches, a width of \(3\) inches, and a height of \(5\) inches. What is the volume, in cubic inches, of the prism?
explanation: The volume of a rectangular prism is length times width times height, so \(4 \times 3 \times 5 = 60\). Thus the volume is \(60\text{ in}^3\).

passage.text: A cognitive scientist studied how the timing of practice affects memory in younger and older adults. Participants in each age group were randomly assigned to learn a list of 50 new vocabulary items through either spaced practice (items introduced several times over a two-hour session) or massed practice (items presented together in one block). The next day, all participants took a recall test. The table below shows the group averages.

stem: Which statement is best supported by the data in the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Younger adults using massed practice recalled more words than older adults using spaced practice.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Older adults recalled more words after massed practice than younger adults recalled after spaced practice.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Spaced practice improved recall by a larger margin for older adults than for younger adults.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The advantage of spaced practice over massed practice was larger for younger adults than for older adults.

explanation: Spaced practice gave younger adults \(34.2 - 18.5 = 15.7\) additional words recalled, while it gave older adults \(23.8 - 12.6 = 11.2\) additional words recalled. Thus the advantage of spaced practice was larger for younger adults.

visual.title: Average number of words correctly recalled after 24 hours

passage.text: In a study of how automatically presented words can interfere with emotion recognition, researchers asked college students to classify faces as happy or angry as quickly as possible. On each trial, a word was shown on the face. In the congruent condition, the word matched the facial expression; in the incongruent condition, it did not. The table shows the mean response times in milliseconds.

stem: Which statement is best supported by the data in the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: For angry faces, the average response time was faster in the incongruent condition than in the congruent condition.

choices.label: B
choices.text: For happy faces, the average response time increased by more than 100 milliseconds from the congruent condition to the incongruent condition.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The difference between average response times for happy and angry faces was greater in the incongruent condition than in the congruent condition.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the congruent condition, the average response time for happy faces differed from that for angry faces by less than 50 milliseconds.

explanation: For happy faces, the mean response time increased from 612 ms to 734 ms, a difference of 122 ms, which is more than 100 milliseconds. The other choices either contradict the table or rely on incorrect differences.

visual.title: Mean response times by facial expression and condition

stem: In the figure above, \( \triangle ABC \) is a right triangle with legs \(AB = 8\) and \(AC = 6\). What is the area of the triangle?
explanation: The area of a triangle is \( \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} \). Using base \(8\) and height \(6\), the area is \( \frac{1}{2}(8)(6)=24 \).

stem: The figure above shows a rectangular prism with dimensions \(3\), \(4\), and \(5\). What is the volume, in cubic units, of the prism?
explanation: The volume of a rectangular prism is \( \text{length} \times \text{width} \times \text{height} \). Here, \(3 \times 4 \times 5 = 60\).

stem: The graph of a quadratic function \(f\) is shown in the \(xy\)-plane. Which of the following equations could define \(f\)?
explanation: The parabola has vertex \((3,-2)\), so \(f(x)=a(x-3)^2-2\). Using the point \((1,6)\): \(6=a(1-3)^2-2=4a-2\), so \(4a=8\) and \(a=2\). Therefore \(f(x)=2(x-3)^2-2\).

stem: The graph of \(f\) is shown in the \(xy\)-plane. The function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x)=-f(x)+2\). Which of the following equations defines \(g\)?
In the right triangle \(PQR\) shown, \(PQ = 5\), \(QR = 12\), and \(PR = 13\). Which of the following is equal to \(\sin R\)?
explanation: For angle \(R\), the opposite side is \(PQ = 5\) and the hypotenuse is \(PR = 13\). Thus \(\sin R = \frac{5}{13}\).

stem: In the right triangle \(ABC\) shown, \(\angle C = 90^\circ\), \(\angle A = x^\circ\), and \(\angle B = y^\circ\). If \(AC = 24\), \(BC = 7\), and \(AB = 25\), what is the value of \(\cos y\)?
explanation: Since \(y = 90^\circ - x\), \(\cos y = \sin x\). For angle \(A\), \(\sin x = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{BC}{AB} = \frac{7}{25}\). Directly at angle \(B\), \(\cos y = \frac{BC}{AB} = \frac{7}{25}\).

stem: The figure above shows a composite figure made of a rectangle and a triangle. The rectangle has dimensions 8 cm by 5 cm. The triangle has a base that coincides with the top side of the rectangle and has a height of 6 cm above the rectangle. What is the total area of the figure, in square centimeters?
explanation: The rectangle has area \(8 \times 5 = 40\). The triangle has base 8 cm and height 6 cm, so its area is \(\frac{1}{2}(8)(6) = 24\). Total area is \(40 + 24 = 64\) square centimeters.

stem: The figure above shows a rectangular prism with dimensions 4 cm by 3 cm by 5 cm. What is the volume of the prism, in cubic centimeters?
explanation: The volume of a rectangular prism is \(\text{length} \times \text{width} \times \text{height}\). Thus \(4 \times 3 \times 5 = 60\) cubic centimeters.

stem: A trapezoid is shown above with parallel bases \(AB\) and \(CD\). The length of \(AB\) is 12 centimeters, the length of \(CD\) is 8 centimeters, and the perpendicular distance between the bases is 5 centimeters. What is the area, in square centimeters, of the trapezoid?
A rectangular prism is shown above. Its length is 6 centimeters, width is 4 centimeters, and height is 5 centimeters. What is the volume, in cubic centimeters, of the prism?
explanation: The volume of a rectangular prism is \(V = lwh\). Substituting \(l = 6\), \(w = 4\), and \(h = 5\): \(V = 6 \cdot 4 \cdot 5 = 120\).

stem: In the right triangle above, angle \(C\) is a right angle. If \(\cos B = \frac{12}{13}\), what is \(\sin A\)?
explanation: Angles \(A\) and \(B\) are complementary, so \(\sin A = \cos(90^\circ - A) = \cos B\). Thus, \(\sin A = \frac{12}{13}\). Equivalently, \(\sin A = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{BC}{AB} = \frac{12}{13}\).

stem: The scatterplot above shows the relationship between the number of hours per week a group of runners spent training and their marathon finish times. The line of best fit is also shown. Based on the line of best fit, what finish time does the model predict for a runner who trains 10 hours per week?
explanation: The line of best fit has equation \(y = 280 - 5.5x\), where \(x\) is training hours per week. Substituting \(x = 10\) gives \(y = 280 - 55 = 225\). Choice B is the observed time for a runner near 10 hours, not the line-of-best-fit prediction.

visual.title: Training hours vs. Marathon finish time

stem: The scatterplot above shows the relationship between the number of practice problems completed before an exam and the exam score for each student in a class. The line of best fit is \(y = 68 + 0.6x\), where \(x\) is the number of practice problems completed and \(y\) is the predicted exam score. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of the line of best fit in this context?

choices.label: A
choices.text: For each additional practice problem completed, a student's actual exam score increases by exactly \(0.6\) points.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A student who completed no practice problems is predicted to have an exam score of \(68\).

choices.label: C
choices.text: For each additional practice problem completed, the predicted exam score increases by \(0.6\) points.

choices.label: D
choices.text: For each additional point on the exam, a student is predicted to have completed \(0.6\) more practice problems.

explanation: In the equation \(y = 68 + 0.6x\), the slope is \(0.6\). Since \(x\) is the number of practice problems and \(y\) is the predicted exam score, the model predicts an increase of \(0.6\) points for each additional practice problem. Choice A incorrectly uses “actual” instead of “predicted,” and choice D reverses the variables.

stem: In right triangle ABC above, angle A measures \(40^\circ\) and angle B measures \(50^\circ\). Which of the following is equal to \(\sin(40^\circ)\)?
explanation: For complementary acute angles in a right triangle, \(\sin\theta = \cos(90^\circ - \theta)\). Thus \(\sin(40^\circ) = \cos(50^\circ)\).

stem: The trapezoid above has parallel bases of length 10 and 4 and a height of 6. What is the area of the trapezoid?
explanation: The area of a trapezoid is \(\frac{1}{2}(b_1+b_2)h\). Here, \(\frac{1}{2}(10+4)(6)=\frac{1}{2}(14)(6)=42\).

stem: The rectangular prism shown has dimensions 4, 3, and 5. What is the volume of the prism?
explanation: The volume of a rectangular prism is length times width times height: \(4 \times 3 \times 5 = 60\).

stem: In the right triangle above, angle \(D\) is the right angle, \(DE=12\), \(DF=5\), and \(EF=13\). If \(\sin \theta = \frac{5}{13}\), what is \(\cos \alpha\)?
explanation: Angles \(\theta\) and \(\alpha\) are complementary, so \(\sin \theta = \cos(90^\circ - \theta) = \cos \alpha\). Therefore, \(\cos \alpha = \frac{5}{13}\). Equivalently, from the figure, \(\cos \alpha = \frac{DF}{EF} = \frac{5}{13}\).

stem: The graph of a quadratic function \(f\) is shown in the \(xy\)-plane. Which of the following could define \(f(x)\)?
explanation: The graph has vertex \((3,-2)\), so in vertex form \(f(x)=a(x-3)^2-2\). Since \((1,6)\) lies on the graph, \(6=a(1-3)^2-2\), so \(4a-2=6\) and \(a=2\). Thus \(f(x)=2(x-3)^2-2\).

stem: The graph of \(f\) is shown in the \(xy\)-plane. The function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x)=f(x-2)-5\). What is the vertex of the graph of \(g\)?
explanation: The vertex of \(f\) is \((1,2)\). Replacing \(x\) with \(x-2\) shifts the graph right 2 units, and subtracting 5 shifts it down 5 units. Therefore the vertex of \(g\) is \((1+2,2-5)=(3,-3)\).

stem: A rectangular prism has dimensions 6, 4, and 3, as shown. What is the volume, in cubic units, of the prism?
explanation: The volume of a rectangular prism is \(V = lwh\). Here, \(l=6\), \(w=4\), and \(h=3\), so \(V = 6 \times 4 \times 3 = 72\) cubic units.

stem: In the right triangle above, angle \(C\) is a right angle. Which expression is equal to \(\sin A\)?
explanation: Since \(A+B=90^\circ\), \(\sin A = \cos(90^\circ - A) = \cos B\). From the side lengths, both are \(\frac{3}{5}\).

stem: In right triangle \(RST\) above, \(\angle T = 90^\circ\), \(RT = 8\), and \(ST = 6\). What is \(\cos \angle R\)?
explanation: For angle \(R\), the adjacent side is \(RT = 8\) and the hypotenuse is \(RS = 10\). Thus \(\cos R = \frac{8}{10} = \frac{4}{5}\).

stem: In right triangle \(ABC\) above, \(\angle C = 90^\circ\), \(AB = 25\), \(AC = 7\), and \(BC = 24\). What is \(\tan \angle A\)?
explanation: For angle \(A\), the opposite side is \(BC = 24\) and the adjacent side is \(AC = 7\). Thus \(\tan A = \frac{24}{7}\).

stem: In right triangle \(ABC\) shown, angle \(C\) is a right angle, \(AC=8\), and \(BC=15\). What is \(\sin A\)?
explanation: Using the Pythagorean theorem, the hypotenuse is \(\sqrt{8^2+15^2}=17\). For angle \(A\), the opposite side is \(BC=15\), so \(\sin A=\frac{15}{17}\).

stem: In right triangle \(XYZ\) shown, angle \(Y\) is a right angle, \(XY=24\), and \(YZ=7\). What is \(\tan X\)?
explanation: Using the Pythagorean theorem, \(XZ=\sqrt{24^2+7^2}=25\). For angle \(X\), the opposite side is \(YZ=7\) and the adjacent side is \(XY=24\), so \(\tan X=\frac{7}{24}\).

stem: In the right triangle shown, \(AC = 12\), \(BC = 5\), and \(\angle C\) is a right angle. What is \(\tan A\)?
explanation: The hypotenuse is \(AB = \sqrt{12^2 + 5^2} = 13\). For angle \(A\), the opposite side is \(BC = 5\) and the adjacent side is \(AC = 12\). Therefore, \(\tan A = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}} = \frac{5}{12}\).

stem: In right triangle \(ABC\) above, \(\angle C = 90^\circ\), \(AC = 6\), \(BC = 8\), and \(AB = 10\). What is \(\sin \angle BAC\)?
explanation: At angle \(A\), the opposite side is \(BC = 8\), and the hypotenuse is \(AB = 10\). Therefore, \(\sin \angle BAC = \frac{8}{10} = \frac{4}{5}\).

stem: In right triangle \(PQR\) above, \(\angle Q = 90^\circ\), \(\angle P = 32^\circ\), and \(PQ = 12\). Which of the following expressions gives the length of \(\overline{QR}\)?
explanation: Since \(\tan P = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}} = \frac{QR}{PQ}\), we have \(\tan 32^\circ = \frac{QR}{12}\). Multiplying both sides by 12 gives \(QR = 12 \tan 32^\circ\).

stem: A rectangular garden is 8 feet long and 5 feet wide. What is the area of the garden, in square feet?
explanation: The area of a rectangle is length times width: \(8 \times 5 = 40\) square feet.

stem: A rectangular box has a length of 6 centimeters, a width of 3 centimeters, and a height of 4 centimeters. What is the volume of the box, in cubic centimeters?
explanation: The volume of a rectangular prism is length times width times height: \(6 \times 3 \times 4 = 72\) cubic centimeters.

stem: The graph of the quadratic function \(f\) is shown in the \(xy\)-plane above. The function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x) = f(x + 3) - 4\). What are the coordinates of the vertex of \(g\)?
explanation: The vertex of \(f\) shown is \((-2, 1)\). In \(g(x)=f(x+3)-4\), replacing \(x\) with \(x+3\) shifts the graph 3 units left, and subtracting 4 shifts it 4 units down. Thus the vertex of \(g\) is \((-2-3,\,1-4)=(-5,-3)\).

stem: The graphs of the quadratic functions \(f\) and \(g\) are shown in the \(xy\)-plane above. The function \(g\) is a transformation of \(f\). Which of the following defines \(g\)?
explanation: The graph of \(f\) has vertex \((-1, 2)\), while the graph of \(g\) has vertex \((4, -3)\). To map \(f\) to \(g\), shift the graph 5 units right and 5 units down. A shift 5 units right corresponds to \(x-5\), and a shift 5 units down corresponds to subtracting 5. Therefore \(g(x)=f(x-5)-5\).

stem: A cylinder is shown with radius 3 and height 4. What is the volume, in cubic units, of the cylinder in terms of \(\pi\)?
explanation: The volume of a cylinder is \(V = \pi r^2 h\). Substituting \(r = 3\) and \(h = 4\) gives \(V = \pi(3^2)(4) = 36\pi\) cubic units.

stem: The scatterplot above shows the number of years of experience \(x\) and the number of defective items produced per week \(y\) for 14 assembly-line workers. A line of best fit is also shown. Which of the following equations best represents the line of best fit?
explanation: The line of best fit crosses the \(y\)-axis near 20 and drops to about 12 when \(x=10\), giving a slope of about \((12-20)/10 = -0.8\). Thus \(y = -0.8x + 20\) best matches the line.

visual.title: Assembly Workers: Experience vs. Defective Items

stem: An electric vehicle's battery charge, \(y\) percent, is recorded after the vehicle has been driven \(x\) miles. The scatterplot above shows the data and a line of best fit. Based on the line of best fit, what is the predicted battery charge, in percent, for a vehicle that has been driven 180 miles?
explanation: The line of best fit has slope \(-0.4\) and a \(y\)-intercept of 100, so its equation is \(y = 100 - 0.4x\). Substituting \(x = 180\) gives \(y = 100 - 72 = 28\). Therefore, the predicted battery charge is \(28\%\).

stem: In right triangle \(ABC\) above, \(\angle C\) is the right angle. If \(AC = 3\) and \(BC = 4\), what is \(\sin A\)?
explanation: First find the hypotenuse using the Pythagorean theorem: \(AB = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{25} = 5\). For angle \(A\), the opposite side is \(BC = 4\), so \(\sin A = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{BC}{AB} = \frac{4}{5}\).

stem: The figure above is composed of a rectangle and a semicircle. The rectangle has length 10 and height 6, and the semicircle is attached along the top side of the rectangle. What is the total area of the figure?
explanation: The rectangle has area \(10 \times 6 = 60\). The semicircle has radius \(10/2 = 5\), so its area is \(\frac{1}{2}\pi(5^2) = 12.5\pi\). Total area = \(60 + 12.5\pi\).

stem: The rectangular prism shown has dimensions 4, 3, and 5 as indicated. What is the volume of the prism?
explanation: The volume of a rectangular prism is length \(\times\) width \(\times\) height. Here, \(4 \times 3 \times 5 = 60\).

stem: The graph of \(y=f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane is a parabola with vertex at \((-2,1)\) and passing through \((0,5)\), as shown. If \(g(x)=f(x-3)+1\), which of the following equations defines \(g\)?
explanation: The graph shows a parabola in vertex form: \(f(x)=(x+2)^2+1\), since its vertex is \((-2,1)\) and \((0,5)\) satisfies \((0+2)^2+1=5\). Then \(g(x)=f(x-3)+1=((x-3)+2)^2+1+1=(x-1)^2+2\).

stem: The figure above shows a parallelogram. The length of the base is 10 inches, the length of each slanted side is 8 inches, and the perpendicular height is 6 inches. What is the area, in square inches, of the parallelogram?
explanation: The area of a parallelogram is base times height: \(10 \times 6 = 60\) square inches. Using the slanted side length (\(10 \times 8 = 80\)) or multiplying the slanted side by the height (\(8 \times 6 = 48\)) are common errors.

stem: The figure above shows a right rectangular prism with dimensions 5, 3, and 4. What is the volume, in cubic units?
explanation: The volume of a rectangular prism is length times width times height: \(5 \times 3 \times 4 = 60\) cubic units.

stem: A figure is formed by placing a semicircle on top of a rectangle, as shown. The rectangle has width 8 and height 4, and the semicircle has diameter equal to the width of the rectangle. What is the area, in square units, of the figure?
explanation: The rectangle has area \(8 \times 4 = 32\). The semicircle has radius \(4\), so its area is \(\frac{1}{2}\pi(4)^2 = 8\pi\). Thus the total area is \(32 + 8\pi\).

stem: A cylindrical water tank has a radius of 3 meters and a height of 10 meters, as shown. What is the volume of the tank, in cubic meters?
explanation: The volume of a cylinder is \(V = \pi r^2 h\). With \(r = 3\) and \(h = 10\), \(V = \pi(3^2)(10) = 90\pi\).

stem: In right triangle \(ABC\), the right angle is at \(A\), \(AB = 6\), and \(AC = 8\). What is the area of triangle \(ABC\)?
explanation: The area of a right triangle is \(\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}\). Using \(AB = 6\) as the base and \(AC = 8\) as the height gives \(\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 8 = 24\).

stem: The rectangular prism shown has length 5, width 4, and height 3. What is the volume of the prism?
explanation: Volume of a rectangular prism is \(\text{length} \times \text{width} \times \text{height}\), so \(5 \times 4 \times 3 = 60\).

stem: The figure above shows a right circular cylinder with a diameter of 6 and a height of 10. What is the volume, in cubic units, of the cylinder?
explanation: The cylinder has diameter 6, so its radius is \(3\). Volume is \(\pi r^2 h = \pi(3^2)(10) = 90\pi\) cubic units.

stem: The rectangle shown has a length of \(7\) centimeters and a width of \(5\) centimeters. What is the area, in square centimeters, of the rectangle?
explanation: The area of a rectangle is length times width, so \(A = 7 \times 5 = 35\) square centimeters.

stem: The scatterplot above shows the advertising expenditure \(x\) (in hundreds of dollars) and weekly revenue \(y\) (in thousands of dollars) for a clothing store, along with the line of best fit \(y = 2.1x + 3.2\). The point at \((5, 16)\) represents a week with $500 spent on advertising and $16,000 in revenue. What is the residual, in thousands of dollars, for this point?
explanation: For \(x = 5\), the line of best fit predicts \(y = 2.1(5) + 3.2 = 13.7\). The actual revenue is \(y = 16\). The residual is actual minus predicted: \(16 - 13.7 = 2.3\) thousand dollars.

stem: The scatterplot above shows the relationship between the amount of fertilizer applied (in pounds per acre) and the yield (in bushels per acre) for 9 plots of land. The line of best fit is shown. A farmer wants to use the line of best fit to predict the yield for a plot receiving \(80\) pounds per acre. Which of the following is the best reason why this prediction is not appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The line of best fit predicts a yield of \(84\) bushels per acre, which is too high to be realistic.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The data show a nonlinear association, so the line of best fit cannot be used to make any prediction.

choices.label: C
choices.text: \(80\) pounds per acre is outside the range of the data, so the prediction would be an extrapolation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The actual yield at \(80\) pounds per acre would likely be higher than the line predicts because yields generally increase with more fertilizer.

explanation: The data set includes fertilizer amounts only between 10 and 60 pounds per acre. Predicting the yield at 80 pounds per acre would require extending the line of best fit beyond the observed range, which is an extrapolation and is not statistically justified.

stem: The scatterplot above shows the number of hours a group of students studied for a science exam and their exam scores. The line of best fit is shown. Based on the line of best fit, what is the predicted exam score for a student who studied for \(6.5\) hours?
explanation: The line of best fit has equation \(y = 8x + 50\). Substituting \(x = 6.5\) gives \(y = 8(6.5) + 50 = 52 + 50 = 102\).

stem: The scatterplot above shows the height, in centimeters, of 12 plants and the amount of fertilizer, in grams, each plant received. The line of best fit is shown. For the plant that received \(5\) grams of fertilizer and had a height of \(29\) centimeters, what is the residual? (The residual is the actual height minus the height predicted by the line of best fit.)
explanation: For \(x = 5\), the predicted height is \(3(5) + 15 = 30\) cm. The residual is actual minus predicted: \(29 - 30 = -1\).

stem: The scatterplot above shows the number of hours 12 students spent studying for a final exam and their exam scores. The line of best fit for the data is \(s = 6.5h + 40\), where \(h\) is the number of hours studied and \(s\) is the predicted exam score. One student represented by the point \((4, 70)\) studied for 4 hours and earned a score of 70. What is the residual for this student? (A residual is the difference between the actual score and the predicted score.)
explanation: For \(h = 4\), the line of best fit predicts \(s = 6.5(4) + 40 = 26 + 40 = 66\). The actual score is 70, so the residual is \(70 - 66 = 4\). Choice B is correct.

stem: The scatterplot above shows the number of years of experience and average weekly sales for 13 sales representatives. A line of best fit for the data is drawn. According to the line of best fit, the predicted weekly sales increase by approximately how many dollars for each additional 5 years of experience?
explanation: The line of best fit passes through \((0, 800)\) and \((10, 3200)\), so its slope is \((3200 - 800) / (10 - 0) = 240\) dollars per year. Therefore, over 5 additional years, the predicted weekly sales increase by \(240 \times 5 = 1200\) dollars.

stem: The scatterplot above shows the number of hours per week a group of students practiced a musical instrument and their scores on a performance test (out of 100). The line of best fit is also shown. Based on the line of best fit, what score would a student who practiced 7 hours per week be predicted to receive?
explanation: Using two points on the line of best fit, \((2,25)\) and \((10,45)\), the slope is \(\frac{45-25}{10-2}=2.5\). The equation of the line is \(y=2.5x+20\). Substituting \(x=7\) gives \(y=2.5(7)+20=37.5\).

stem: A chemist measures the concentration of a reactant at several times after a reaction begins. The scatterplot above shows the data, and the line of best fit is drawn. Based on the line of best fit, after approximately how many hours will the concentration of the reactant be 0 grams per liter?
explanation: The line of best fit passes through \((4,20)\) and \((9,10)\), so its slope is \(\frac{10-20}{9-4}=-2\). The equation is \(y=-2x+28\). Setting \(y=0\) gives \(0=-2x+28\), so \(x=14\).

Trapezoid \(ABCD\) is shown in the \(xy\)-plane above. The coordinates of \(A\), \(B\), \(C\), and \(D\) are \((2,2)\), \((10,2)\), \((6,6)\), and \((4,6)\), respectively. What is the area of trapezoid \(ABCD\)?
explanation: The bases of the trapezoid are \(AB\), with length \(10 - 2 = 8\), and \(CD\), with length \(6 - 4 = 2\). The height is the vertical distance between the bases: \(6 - 2 = 4\). Thus the area is \(\frac{1}{2}(8 + 2)(4) = 20\).

stem: The rectangular prism shown above has a length of 8 inches, a width of 5 inches, and a height of 6 inches. What is the volume of the rectangular prism, in cubic inches?
explanation: The volume of a rectangular prism is length times width times height: \(8 \times 5 \times 6 = 240\) cubic inches.

stem: A garden bed is shaped like quadrilateral \(ABCD\) shown above. Side \(\overline{AB}\) is parallel to side \(\overline{CD}\). If \(AB=9\) meters, \(CD=15\) meters, and the perpendicular distance between \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{CD}\) is \(8\) meters, what is the area, in square meters, of the garden bed?
explanation: The garden bed is a trapezoid. Its area is \(\frac{1}{2}(b_1+b_2)h = \frac{1}{2}(9+15)(8)=96\) square meters.

stem: A cylindrical water tank is shown above. The tank has a diameter of 10 feet and a height of 12 feet. What is the volume, in cubic feet, of the tank?
explanation: The radius is half the diameter, so \(r=5\). Thus \(V=\pi r^2 h = \pi(5^2)(12)=300\pi\) cubic feet.

stem: The scatterplot above shows the shoulder height, in centimeters, and weight, in kilograms, of 12 adult dogs. A line of best fit for the data is also shown. Based on the line of best fit, what is the predicted weight, in kilograms, of an adult dog with a shoulder height of 60 centimeters?
explanation: The line of best fit passes through approximately (40, 22) and (70, 46). Its slope is (46 - 22)/(70 - 40) = 0.8, so the line can be written as y = 0.8x - 10. Substituting x = 60 gives y = 0.8(60) - 10 = 38.

stem: The scatterplot above shows the number of hours a group of students spent practicing a musical piece each week and their scores on a performance test, out of 100 points. A line of best fit is shown. Based on the line of best fit, a student who practiced 5 hours per week would be predicted to have a performance score closest to which of the following?
explanation: The line of best fit can be approximated by y = 7x + 58, where x is practice time in hours and y is the predicted performance score. For x = 5, the predicted score is y = 7(5) + 58 = 93.

stem: The figure shows a 12 ft by 8 ft rectangle with a right triangle cut out of one corner. The legs of the right triangle are 4 ft and 3 ft. What is the area, in square feet, of the shaded region?
explanation: The area of the rectangle is \(12 \times 8 = 96\). The area of the right triangle is \(\frac12 \times 4 \times 3 = 6\). The shaded area is \(96 - 6 = 90\) square feet.

stem: The figure shows a right circular cylinder with radius 3 feet and height 8 feet. What is the volume of the cylinder, in cubic feet?
explanation: The volume of a cylinder is \(V = \pi r^2 h\). Substituting \(r = 3\) and \(h = 8\) gives \(V = \pi(3^2)(8) = 72\pi\) cubic feet.

stem: The figure above shows a trapezoid with bottom base 8, top base 4, and height 6. What is the area, in square units, of the trapezoid?
explanation: The area of a trapezoid is \(\frac{1}{2}(b_1 + b_2)h\), where \(b_1\) and \(b_2\) are the bases and \(h\) is the height. So the area is \(\frac{1}{2}(8 + 4)(6) = 36\) square units.

stem: The figure above shows a right circular cylinder with a base radius of 3 feet and a height of 8 feet. What is the volume, in cubic feet, of the cylinder?
explanation: The volume of a right circular cylinder is \(V = \pi r^2 h\). Substituting \(r = 3\) and \(h = 8\) gives \(V = \pi (3^2)(8) = 72\pi\) cubic feet.

stem: In triangle \(PQR\) shown above, \(\overline{PQ} \cong \overline{PR}\) and \(\angle QPR = 40^\circ\). What is the measure of \(\angle PQR\)?

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: , famous as much for his bongo playing as for his quantum electrodynamics work,

choices.label: B
choices.text: , famous as much for his bongo playing as for his quantum electrodynamics work

choices.label: C

choices.label: D
choices.text: ; famous as much for his bongo playing as for his quantum electrodynamics work;

explanation: The phrase “famous as much for his bongo playing as for his quantum electrodynamics work” is a nonessential modifier and must be set off by both an opening and a closing comma. Choice A supplies both commas. B lacks the closing comma, C lacks the opening comma, and D incorrectly uses semicolons around the modifier.

stem: In the figure, \(\triangle ABC\) is a right triangle with \(AB=6\) and \(AC=8\). A semicircle whose diameter is \(\overline{BC}\) is constructed outside the triangle. The entire region shown is shaded. What is the area of the shaded region?
explanation: The triangle area is \(\frac12(6)(8)=24\). By the Pythagorean theorem, \(BC=\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10\), so the semicircle radius is \(5\). Its area is \(\frac12\pi(5)^2=\frac{25\pi}{2}\). Thus the total shaded area is \(24+\frac{25\pi}{2}\).

stem: A right circular frustum is shown with bottom radius \(9\), top radius \(3\), and height \(8\), all in centimeters. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?
explanation: Extend the sides upward to form the missing small cone. Let its height be \(h\). By similar triangles, \(\frac{h}{h+8}=\frac{3}{9}\), so \(h=4\). The large cone has volume \(\frac13\pi(9)^2(12)=324\pi\), and the small cone has volume \(\frac13\pi(3)^2(4)=12\pi\). Thus the frustum volume is \(324\pi-12\pi=312\pi\). Equivalently, the frustum formula gives \(\frac13\pi h(R^2+Rr+r^2)=\frac13\pi(8)(81+27+9)=312\pi\).

stem: In right triangle \(ABC\) above, \(\angle C\) is a right angle, \(AB=25\), \(BC=15\), and \(\angle B\) is marked. What is \(\sin B\)?
explanation: By the Pythagorean theorem, \(AC=\sqrt{25^2-15^2}=20\). For angle \(B\), the opposite side is \(AC\) and the hypotenuse is \(AB\), so \(\sin B = \frac{AC}{AB} = \frac{20}{25} = \frac{4}{5}\).

stem: In right triangle \(DEF\) above, \(\angle E\) is a right angle, \(DE=3\), \(EF=7\), and \(\angle F\) is marked. What is \(\cos F\)?
explanation: The hypotenuse is \(DF=\sqrt{3^2+7^2}=\sqrt{58}\). For angle \(F\), the adjacent side is \(EF=7\), so \(\cos F=\frac{EF}{DF}=\frac{7}{\sqrt{58}}\). Equivalently, \(\cos F=\sin D=\frac{7}{\sqrt{58}}\).

stem: During one week, a librarian asked 20 students how many books they had borrowed from the school library. The dot plot above shows the distribution of the responses. What is the mean number of books borrowed per student?
explanation: From the dot plot, the frequencies are 0:2, 1:3, 2:4, 3:6, 4:3, 5:2. The total number of books is \(0(2)+1(3)+2(4)+3(6)+4(3)+5(2)=51\). There are 20 students, so the mean is \(51/20=2.55\).

stem: The dot plot above shows the number of miles run in one week by each of 18 participants in a running club. Based on the dot plot, which of the following statements is true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The mean is greater than the median.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The median is greater than the mode.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The mean is equal to the median.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The range is less than the mean.

explanation: The frequencies are 1:6, 2:7, 3:3, 4:1, 5:1. The sum is \(6(1)+7(2)+3(3)+1(4)+1(5)=38\), so the mean is \(38/18 \approx 2.11\). The median is the average of the 9th and 10th values, both 2, so the median is 2. The mode is 2. The range is \(5-1=4\). Therefore, the mean is greater than the median.

stem: In the right triangle above, \(\angle C\) is a right angle, \(\alpha = \angle BAC\), and \(\beta = \angle ABC\). If \(AB = 10\) and \(\tan \alpha = \frac{3}{4}\), what is \(\sin \beta\)?
explanation: Since \(\tan \alpha = \frac{BC}{AC} = \frac{3}{4}\), let \(BC = 3k\) and \(AC = 4k\). Then the hypotenuse \(AB = 5k\). Given \(AB = 10\), \(k = 2\), so \(AC = 8\) and \(BC = 6\). Because \(\beta = 90^\circ - \alpha\), \(\sin \beta = \cos \alpha = \frac{AC}{AB} = \frac{8}{10} = \frac{4}{5}\).

stem: In the right triangle above, \(\angle E\) is a right angle. If \(DE = 24\) and \(\cos F = \frac{5}{13}\), what is \(\tan D\)?
explanation: Since \(\cos F = \frac{EF}{DF} = \frac{5}{13}\), let \(EF = 5k\) and \(DF = 13k\). By the Pythagorean theorem, \(DE = 12k\). Given \(DE = 24\), \(k = 2\), so \(EF = 10\) and \(DF = 26\). Then \(\tan D = \frac{EF}{DE} = \frac{10}{24} = \frac{5}{12}\). Equivalently, \(\tan D = \cot F = \frac{\cos F}{\sin F} = \frac{5/13}{12/13} = \frac{5}{12}\).

stem: The dot plot above shows the number of hours 18 students spent on homework in one week. What is the median number of hours spent on homework?

stem: In triangle \(ABC\) above, the measures of \(\angle A\), \(\angle B\), and \(\angle C\) are \(2x^\circ\), \(3x^\circ\), and \(4x^\circ\), respectively. What is the value of \(x\)?
explanation: The angle measures of a triangle sum to \(180^\circ\), so \(2x + 3x + 4x = 180\). Thus \(9x = 180\), so \(x = 20\).

stem: In the figure above, \(D\) lies on \(\overline{AB}\) extended through \(B\). If \(\angle BAC = 60^\circ\) and \(\angle BCA = 50^\circ\), what is the measure of \(\angle CBD\)?
explanation: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle ABC = 180^\circ - 60^\circ - 50^\circ = 70^\circ\). Since \(\overline{AB}\) is extended through \(B\) to \(D\), \(\angle ABC\) and \(\angle CBD\) are supplementary. Therefore \(\angle CBD = 180^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ\).

stem: In triangle \(ABC\) shown, the measure of angle \(A\) is \(35^\circ\) and the measure of angle \(B\) is \(85^\circ\). What is the measure of angle \(C\)?
explanation: The interior angles of a triangle sum to \(180^\circ\), so \(m\angle C = 180^\circ - 35^\circ - 85^\circ = 60^\circ\).

stem: In triangle \(ABC\) shown, \(AB = AC\) and the measure of angle \(BAC\) is \(40^\circ\). What is the measure of angle \(ABC\)?
explanation: Since \(AB = AC\), triangle \(ABC\) is isosceles, so \(\angle ABC = \angle ACB\). Let each base angle be \(x\). Then \(2x + 40^\circ = 180^\circ\), giving \(x = 70^\circ\).

stem: The dot plot above shows the distribution of scores on a 10-point quiz for 20 students. Based on the dot plot, which of the following statements is true?
explanation: There are 20 scores. The sum of the scores is 88, so the mean is \(88/20 = 4.4\). The median is the average of the 10th and 11th scores, which are 3 and 4, so the median is \(3.5\). The mode is 4. Since \(4.4 > 3.5\), the mean is greater than the median.

stem: The dot plot above shows the ages of the 12 participants in a workshop. If the age of the oldest participant is removed from the data set, which of the following best describes the change in the mean and the median of the ages?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The \( \text{mean} \) decreases, and the \( \text{median} \) stays the same.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The \( \text{mean} \) increases, and the \( \text{median} \) stays the same.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The \( \text{mean} \) stays the same, and the \( \text{median} \) stays the same.

explanation: The original sum of ages is \(18(2)+19(3)+20(3)+21(2)+22+45=262\), so the mean is \(262/12 \approx 21.83\). The median of the 12 values is the average of the 6th and 7th values, both 20, so the median is 20. After removing 45, the new sum is 217, so the new mean is \(217/11 \approx 19.73\). The median of the remaining 11 values is the 6th value, still 20. Thus the mean decreases and the median stays the same.

stem: The figure shows a solid capsule consisting of a right circular cylinder of height 8 and radius 5, with a hemisphere attached to each end. What is the total volume of the solid?
explanation: The cylinder has volume \(\pi(5^2)(8)=200\pi\). Each hemisphere has volume \(\frac{2}{3}\pi(5^3)=\frac{250\pi}{3}\), so two hemispheres have volume \(\frac{500\pi}{3}\). Total volume is \(200\pi + \frac{500\pi}{3}=\frac{1100\pi}{3}\).

stem: The figure shows an isosceles trapezoid with bases of lengths 12 and 20 and congruent legs of length 5. What is the area of the trapezoid?
explanation: Drop perpendiculars from the endpoints of the top base to the bottom base. The top base length is 12 and the bottom base length is 20, so the remaining horizontal distance is \(8\), split evenly as \(4\) on each side. Each right triangle therefore has leg 4 and hypotenuse 5, so the height is \(3\). Area is \(\frac{12+20}{2}(3)=48\).

stem: In \(\triangle ABC\) above, \(\angle BAC = 35^\circ\) and \(\angle ABC = 90^\circ\). What is the value of \(\angle ACB\)?
explanation: The angle measures in a triangle sum to \(180^\circ\). Thus \(\angle ACB = 180^\circ - 35^\circ - 90^\circ = 55^\circ\).

stem: In \(\triangle ABC\) above, point \(D\) lies on \(\overline{AB}\) extended beyond \(B\). If \(\angle CBD = 120^\circ\) and \(\angle ACB = 50^\circ\), what is the value of \(\angle BAC\)?
explanation: Since \(\angle CBD = 120^\circ\), the interior angle \(\angle ABC = 180^\circ - 120^\circ = 60^\circ\). Then \(\angle BAC = 180^\circ - 60^\circ - 50^\circ = 70^\circ\).

stem: In the figure above, triangle \(ABC\) is shown. If the measure of angle \(A\) is \(65^\circ\) and the measure of angle \(B\) is \(80^\circ\), what is the measure of angle \(C\)?
explanation: The sum of the interior angles of a triangle is \(180^\circ\). Thus \(\angle C = 180^\circ - 65^\circ - 80^\circ = 35^\circ\).

stem: In the figure above, triangle \(PQR\) is shown with side \(QR\) extended through \(R\) to \(S\). If the measure of angle \(QPR\) is \(55^\circ\) and the measure of angle \(PQR\) is \(60^\circ\), what is the measure of angle \(PRS\)?
explanation: The interior angle at \(R\) is \(180^\circ - 55^\circ - 60^\circ = 65^\circ\). Since \(\angle PRS\) forms a linear pair with that angle, \(\angle PRS = 180^\circ - 65^\circ = 115^\circ\). Equivalently, an exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: \(55^\circ + 60^\circ = 115^\circ\).

stem: In the figure, triangle \(ABC\) is shown. If \(\angle A = 50^\circ\) and \(\angle B = 60^\circ\), what is the measure of \(\angle C\)?
explanation: The sum of the interior angles of a triangle is \(180^\circ\). So \(\angle C = 180^\circ - 50^\circ - 60^\circ = 70^\circ\).

stem: In the figure, \(\angle BAC = 50^\circ\) and \(\angle ACB = 70^\circ\). Side \(AB\) is extended beyond \(B\) to point \(D\). What is the measure of \(\angle CBD\)?
explanation: The exterior angle \(\angle CBD\) equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: \(50^\circ + 70^\circ = 120^\circ\). Alternatively, the interior angle at \(B\) is \(180^\circ - 50^\circ - 70^\circ = 60^\circ\), so the supplementary exterior angle is \(180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ\).
